Everything about this game is phenomenal. The duality of the controls is brilliant; simple yet diverse in execution.  The art style creates a gorgeous environment in which to explore and it helps to make the world feel as alive as the two main characters. The story-telling is well done, given that all of the dialogue is in a fictitious language, and it engages the player as the two brother's interact with one another and the world around them.  The puzzles are inventive but not complicated and go well with the platforming elements throughout the game.  A job well done to make a puzzle-platformer that is so emotionally engaging. 10/10.  A must play for any who appreciate games as art.

If you're new to GTAV, don't bother. Don't waste the money.
The graphics are beautiful, and the gameplay is interesting, but the players make it pointless. You cannot earn money quickly enough in this game to have a fighting chance against people who have been playing it since the beginning. Occasionally, what are known as "modders" (really just cheaters using a "mod menu"), will come along and be either total a**holes, or will be super generous and give you tons of money. Either way, Rockstar will do nothing about them.
However, when it's time for another pack release ("Heists", "I'm Not A Hipster", "Gunrunning"), Rockstar will take away all of the money modders gave you - meaning you can't do anything with the new release, but those cheating can. It's an incredibly asinine system, intended to "encourage" (read: extort) players to spend real-life money on their "shark cards" or whatever for in-game money. It creates an extremely negative, wildly-unbalanced multiplayer system.
If you don't mind being pummeled by players who've been playing much longer than you have, by all means, pay new-release pricing for this game (it came out four years ago, but is still $60) and struggle with the regret of that purchase.

Rise Of The Triad is a very straightorward first person shooter, similar to shooters like Duke Nukem and Serious Sam. I've said it before and I'll say it again; these games are not my cup of tea. It's all about shooting down lots and lots of enemies, while trying to find the many, many secrets hidden around the levels. There was a time where that *was* fun, but nowadays it's just an outdated concept that's no fun and extremely shallow.
The graphics are acceptable. Everything looks sharp but the game has no own personality. It looks... generic.
Also, the framerate is all over the place. It definitely could've been optimized better than this. But it works I guess.
The voice acting is ok, and the sounds get the job done. The whole thing is passable.
In the end I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone, even if you have played the original way, way back. Not for this price, at least.

Tired of playing the same old boring Tower Defence? Do you crave for more WW1 themed games instead of all this modern warfare rubbish we get fed every single dang day? Maybe this game might interest you...
Toy Soldiers is a game about little army men duking it out on various gameboards, one side having to defend themselves against waves of the enemy using tactical placement of machine guns and artillery, as well as deploying early tanks and aircraft to help weakin the attacking force until they can no longer charge your HQ. At first, it might not sound like much, but once you start playing you fall in love with this well made game.
For one, WW1 is the perfect setting for a tower defence game, considering the infamous nature of the war. What also helps set this apart from other TD games is how much more "open" it is when it comes to dealing with enemy waves. In most TD games, enemies march in single file, which honestly is a rather underwhelming display of power and tactics.. While in a way, they still march towards you in a line here, it is a much looser, more widened line, making it feel more like an enemy army is charging at you rather than a big cluster of random thugs effortlessly walking towards your base. Also unlike other TDs, in some maps you have to go on the offencive in order to win the day, which caught me off guard when it happened and amused me quite a bit when I was given control of an early tank and sent to take ground for my defending force and expand my influance on the battlefield.
There is plenty of content to keep you busy for a fair few hours as well, so your money doesn't go to waste should you invest in this title. I wish I could go on, but I don't want to drone on and on about all the good things about the game. The only problem this game has is that it might not work on all computers, due to it being a port of an Xbox game.. But if you can get it to work, it is a lovely game to play, and if you love the first World War, I do suggest you get this delightful title if you can afford it.

Probably the worst horror game I've ever played. Reasons below:
-No tutorial. When an enemy comes up to you to eat your face off, you're supposed to defeat it with the flashlight somehow, but the game doesn't mention how.
-Unplayably difficult. You need to find twenty-something pages to get anywhere, and around every corner is another shadow person or the Scat Man (sorry, did I say Scat Man? I meant Hat Man). Also, any time he gets you, you go back to the beginning of the game and have to find all those pages again.
-It has save points, but they are so scarce and far between that they're nigh nonexistent.
-It has a graphics quality bar that changes literally nothing.
-The only scary thing about this game is how awful it is. The Hat Man is about as scary as a hangnail. The Shadow People, even less.
-Blatant Slender ripoff. Find pages while a shadowy entity chases you... Uh-huh. Doesn't sound familiar at all.
Save your 50 cents. Go play Slender: The Arrival instead if you're seeking something similar that will actually scare.

The Sims 3 is an awesome game that simulates life in fun and rewarding ways. There are a huge number of expansion packs and other DLC that add a great deal to the game. These range from small gameplay elements, to clothing and furniture, to new careers, worlds, and lifestates.
Although interest in this game is waning because The Sims 4 is due out soon, I'm sure fans will continue to play it for a long time to come. If for no other reason, then it will be a long while before TS4 will have anywhere near the amount of content that is now available for TS3 by means of expansion packs, stuff packs, and multitudes of mods.
If you like designing, building, and furnishing homes, then there is a great deal of fun to be had in this game.
If you like creating a character and making all their dreams come true, and achieving all their goals - romance, marriage, children, career, whatever - then you'll have a blast. If you'd rather choose some poor lost soul to torment, visit misery and an early demise upon ... this, too, can be arranged.
Whether you prefer to play as a family-oriented type whose focus is their family, as an evil mastermind who seeks political leadership of the world, as a 'romance' type whose life goal is to woohoo with as many sims as possible, or as a fire-fighting hero with a bent for community service, you can do it. This, and oh so much more.
Do you wish to play as a witch, a genie, a werewolf or vampire, a fairy, a ghost, or an ordinary sim? All these lifestates - and more - are available if you have the right expansion packs.
There are also multitudes of ingame achievements for those into that kind of thing (like me).
The only real negative, imo, is the cost if you want more than just the base game ... and believe me, you do. Which is why I waited for the Steam sales to purchase them.

This game offers a very unique style of gameplay that I've never quite seen or played in all my years of gaming.  While I've played the RPG warrior or mage needing to shop for supples and potions more times then I can count, I've never seen the perspective from the shop keeper trying to earn a little chunk of the advenrturers treasures.
This game offers almost twenty "quests" as you would call them as they are simply goals that start out easy and progressively get harder.  Each one will tell you the goal such as sell 10 of each type of potion or earn 5000 gold as well as other requirements needed to pass it such as paying taxes every 5 minutes and keeping your shop appeal at a certain level on inspections.
To make a profit, you must order your goods from a list by simply going into shop-keep mode, then hitting your Q button to bring up a list of supplies to order from.  Once an order is placed, you can then place your items on any of your available tables and racks for display but be sure to change your profit margin as it it set to 100% by default which means you will sell it for exactly what you paid for it!  You can hold down your shift key while pressing the + and - keys to change this rate faster and once you set it, it will stay there for that entire level unless you change it again.  You can also charge a different rate for a specific item or items by changing your rate before placing that item(s) and then changing it back.  It's all much easier then I can make it sound here in words.
The wizards and warriors who come into your shop will bring in tons of dirt and grime which will quickly dirty your floor and lower your shop appeal.  Lower shop appeal equals less customers and could prevent you from passing a specific level as well, so go to your broom mode on the riht side of your screen and simply left click around the dirt to instantly clean up the mess, and be sure you do this frequently!  Thankfully, atleast for me, sweeping the floor never seemed like a chore or like an annoyance, and in fact it seemed to add to the overal challenge and enjoyment I experienced.  It's hard to describe, but it just works well with this game!
As a shop keeper, you'll also have to deal with the common thieves that will frequently try and steal your goods, robbing you of the potential income those items could earn you!  You can go into fight mode and slash a sword at them or blast them with an electric charge, but they run fast and in a crowded store, this can be easier said then done!  Because you cannot leave your store, all the thieves need to do is escape the front entrance into the street and they are gone with your goods (and money)!  Thankfully there are items and perks you can earn with your experience that will help you deal with the pesky thieves such as an automatic entrance thief zapper.
Speaking of experience, it is earned from almost everything you do in the game, and lets you add your choice of perks such as extra profit from items sold to quicker delivery times on your orders and much more!
In addition to all of these quest style levels in the game, you have a free-play mode where you can simply order and sell what you choose to try and earn mass profits over time.  This game mode is tied to the quests however as the more quests you conquer, the more items you'll have to choose from on the order list in the shop-keep mode.
There's so much more I could talk about here such as the requirement to go into build mode to take out your hammer and repair your tables or they could break over time and rats that invade your messy store or the raiding barbarians that mess your life as a shop keeper up early on!  Add it all up, and for a $5 USD early-access game, this one truly delivers a ton of value and fun!
Highly recommneded for any RPG fan or anyone who enjoys this unique style of game!  Be sure you check out my review above as it gives a much better demonstration of this game then all my wordy words written in text here!
Oh, and be sure you sweep of your damn boots before you step into my shoppe!  Is that how your momma raised you!  {{..Takes out my glowing right hand to threaten electricity up your pesky azz!! }}

Kingdoms of Amalur Reckoning is perhaps one of the most underestimated games on the market. From a glance it boasts nice graphics, decent amount of content and a well-crafted combat system. However, I can assure you it’s also offers a beautiful fantasy world that has completely engrossing likeable characters with tonnes of side quest (With all DLC).  I’ll admit playing with PC controls can be somewhat challenging, however the controller settings are an utter breeze. The game has a vast range of unique weaponry and armour available, which makes every task, every hidden object, and every enemy slain feel greatly more rewarding.
The only complaint I have in relation to this game, is the item limit, it can be a royal pain when you’re collecting different sets to switch between. Aside from your abilities and destinies there are various skills to upgrade:  Alchemy, blacksmithing, detect hidden, dispelling, lock picking, mercantile, persuasion, sagecraft and stealth, which are upgradable from basic to master. These enable you to interact better within quests or be worse off depending on which you focus on. A tale of two sons… I admit I don’t take the time to play many games like this, but I’m glad I took the time to play Brothers (at the recommendation of my brother, coincidentally). The Brothers' world is like playing in a dream. I found myself taking quite a few screenshots, and I have to say I was pleasantly surprised and impressed with the experience. The artwork and scenery were beautiful and powerful in a way most games do not achieve. I found my mood affected by the lighting, music, weather, ambient sounds, and the moods of the brothers and other characters throughout the story (in spite of there not being a single real English "word" uttered). I liked the unique dual-character control concept (while we’re on the subject, note that this game requires a gamepad on the PC). It took only a few minutes to get used to, and it added a unique and memorable feel to the game. I enjoyed the attention to detail in the environment (on the beaten path), and the interesting puzzles and mechanics involved with making your way through the world, escaping peril, and coming to the journey’s end. The brothers compliment each other, and the gameplay reflects their differences in size and strength well. I was definitely feeling the feels by the end of this journey. I had to punch a tree to feel better.
My complaints are few, but for the sake of a balanced review I’ll say that there were a few things that were a minor bother. There are no difficulty settings, so what you see is what you get. I maybe let one brother die 2-3 times on accident during the entire game (due to falling). The “combat” was as slow and easy as it comes, and the puzzles were pretty simple and obvious. Your path is linear, and there is little room for exploring besides the few achievements available in the game (you can easily get them all the first time through, with maybe 10 extra minutes of gameplay). I think I would have enjoyed the game more if the devs had chosen not to use gibberish throughout the game in the place of real dialogue, but to each his own. I think this was probably a low budget issue, but it still works. For the most part, you know exactly what’s going on and what the characters are feeling and saying, but I would have felt closer to the characters if there was a compelling script. The game’s end is powerfully emotional, but the gibberish detracted from the seriousness of the story in my opionion.
All-in-all, if you’re looking for an enjoyable, relaxing, short game to play in one or two sittings then “Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons” is an excellent choice. The powerful emotional journey more than makes up for the simple puzzles and easy gameplay.

I always liked reflex based games, titles that allow you to always push towards your limits, but there’s something in particular that makes Zero Reflex so cool and exciting! This is a very interesting game because it brings in front a whole bunch of cool mechanics, and all of them are combined towards perfection in a stellar manner, as you would expect.
What makes Zero Reflex great for me is the simple fact that this title offers you 30 seconds of amazing goodness. Simply put, you need to survive in a ton of worlds that have an eye at the center of it all, and that particular eye throws a ton of stuff at you. It can attack you directly, from behind or you will have to avoid numbers, small balls and so on. It’s a unique combination of tools that can be accessed here, and all of them are offered in an amazing manner which you will love for sure.
It’s exciting and fun what a simple reflex title can do, and I have to say that I really like their mechanic when you die. The idea is simple, when you die, you get transported to the previous level, so if you finished level 20, started 21 and you died there within those 30 seconds, then you will get back to level 20. This way the game doesn’t really offer a setback, instead it’s created to be more rewarding and fun as a whole, which you will love for sure.
The whole idea of passing all 60 challenges and winning $10000 is amazing, but let’s face it, this can be a tough challenge even for those that are accustomed with this type of game. The title can be frustrating at times, true, but it’s the entire nature of playing such a game that offers such a feeling, so you can expect yourself to spend a lot of time playing and trying to complete each level.
I was impressed with Zero Reflex to be honest, as it does an amazing job when it comes to making its gameplay fun, accessible and quirky! It’s a really cool game, and at the end of the day this is what matters the most. It’s exciting, funny, but also frustrating, so it’s basically the perfect combination for those that want to enjoy a challenge and also have fun playing this sort of title. If you like such as experience, hop in for the ride, Zero Reflex is amazing!

Hello again!
I read the two last updates and I was really please by what I read.
First the counter systems, I couldn’t thank you enough for adding that, it will feel more like and actual fight than a hit and run mechanic.
Then the team attack mechanics, I didn’t even mentioned it in my last evaluation because I thought I would be difficult to make, and yet you say you will do it… guys just good job.
Ultimate! That is fine for me, but yet you didn’t give us any details on it… so I can’t say much about it.
I won’t talk about what the community already asking very loudly (more character, more dialogue, and more cutscene)
First, cooldown. The skill point system, I’m sorry to say that, doesn’t work well. Soon the player realize the skills are not balanced, one is clearly more powerful than the others and yet, they all cost the same thing (the Aoe tend to be the most powerful one) so instead of having 3 nice skill, you just spam the one that work the best. So I propose a cooldown mechanic, so you could use all skill without feeling a waste of resource. About the combo, instead of being the resource provider, it could give a bonus Xp (like you had a combo of 26 hit, you gain 26 xp, just a suggestion). Even though I don’t think this is the main concern of the game, its actually make more sense that the character have to rest a bit before redo their power attack, instead of have to hit nonstop to gain the energy to hit more.
Aura:
Even the game is great so far, I still think it could be better with the fight looking more like in the show (after all it still the best things in the show is the fight scene) and the aura mechanic of the game doesn’t fit. I understand that aura need to be recover fast after the fight to make it enjoyable (and to prevent the player to wait after each combat before continue), but in combat it doesn’t need to be that way. I say give more auras and give a regen over time in combat. I don’t know the actual number in the game but just so you get the point there is an example: 100 aura points, with like 5 auras regen per seconds in combat, and 50 regen sec out of combat. With the actual dmg per hit of monster vary from 2-5 for basic grim to 10-20 for boss. You really need to break the hit and run mechanics, and I think the counter mechanic is the first step; this is the way for it.
Progress:
Unlock skill upgrade by completing challenge is nice, but not yet enough. I think you need to keep lvling system in game that restart each time you play, but you need a better reason than unlock skill by challenge to replay, if you don’t, no matter how fun it is, it will feels like a waste of time if you finish the game and gain nothing from it. There is many way to fix that, like the rune system in league of legend or the paragon lvl in Diablo 3 for example.
Then Semblance, if yang has a sort of skills that match her semblance, Weiss have glyphs in her ability look, and Blake make a clone who do a spin attack, they just look like their semblance, they don’t feel like it (except for yang, good job on that one even if it could be better).

Passive: the lower her aura is, the more dmg she does, the bonus doesn’t have to be huge, but need to be there.

Blake:

At first the game lures you in with a scary atmosphere, and gives you a simple goal to find some pages, and a random ghost for some reason. And for a while, the only thing to scare you is your imagination as you go through a literal endless 1st level that's extremely hard to find anything in, but after a while you learn that this game isn't going to abuse you, it's going to take things slow, maybe a little too slow for a horror game, but then on the second level, it starts getting a little scarier with better ambience, Hatman gets faster and goes through walls for some great jumpscares, as well as an even creepier atmosphere and a little more progress through the story, though not much. Even so, it's a pretty well made game and I'm so excited that the official release finally came. However, there are still some issues that I don't quite like.. Not too big but issues: TOO BIG! Holy crap finding your way through this place and collecting items is harder than a dark souls boss, and progression through 1 level can take maybe an hour if you're not familiar with the game, and seeing the same thing over and over again isn't fun. The second issue is that Hatman only gets harder through levels and not time.
I should know, because I'm one of the people who spent an hour on the first level. As you're looking through the first floor frantically looking for missing pages, or an item you may have missed, you get lost easily and well.. It stops being fun. Mostly because Hatman is like a companion you can kill but respawns.. Kind of like Tails in the sonic franchise, he never dies and he will come back later but.. You can kill him again easily. The problem with this is like a battle in skyrim against a townie who can't die, you can hit him over and over and over and over again but he won't go down for good, and the battle is infinite because you can't die to him either. The only option is to step outside and face the guards waiting for you,,,, though in this game that's more like the only option is to keep searching for items..
But other than ALL of that, great game!

What make classic Mario Kart great? Seeing your skill and knowledge of tracks increase and slowly you start to win cups that seemed impossible.  When is it at it worst?  when too much luck is involved. Blue shell anyone?
This game is all-in on the luck part. Tracks dont require much knowledge outside some basic shortcuts + key/gate locations and certain rare spots where you actually need to use brakes.
What decides the positions is actualy what you get for powerups. Torpedo or Teleport once or twice in a game and you are golden.  You better also know how to defensively use power ups also right at the first 1000cc cup so dont expect 1000cc to be the 'training wheels' cup. it is just the least broken one.
Career mode is a mess.  You will be pressing restart quite many times during multi-track racing cups. Luckily the final order of drivers seem to be much more random than on Mario Kart where your main rival is faster than anyone else.
Multiplayer is dead. DLC structure is a mess. Tracks as DLC i can understand but the rest is some of the most useless crap i have seen in a DLC. And the prices. oh my.

I rather study Sonic All-Stars Racing Transformed more complex mechanics or just go back to Mario Kart rather than try to seriously play this game. I will be putting some more hours into this but it's clear already i can just forget about a proper career game and just play this casually. That way it's obviously been designed too.

Pure Racing is the worst game mode I've ever played in any game, EVER. Spent two hours restarting Monaco over, and over, and over just so I could finish 4th. Despite the fact that it's IMPOSSIBLE to finish 1st in this gamemode unless you started first, somehow the AI that had won previous races also won again at Monaco and I ended up 2nd in the series. All that work, just to get my best possible finish of never-higher-than-fourth and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t AI wins, AGAIN.
Once you strip this game down of all its mario kart clone mechanics, there is literally nothing left -- this game accomplishes absolutely nothing. I had already grown weary of these ridiculous physics at this point. You can't make any corner because you just drift back and forth across the track, sometimes completely unpredictably. If any of the moronic AI get within an inch of you, which they seem incapable of NOT doing, they will trigger an absolutely unforgivable knockback effect that COMPLETELY stops all of your momentum. Naturally, it affects the AI less than it does the player so navigating through the clusterf*ck of garbage AI seems perfectly legit.
This is quite possibly the worst AI I've ever raced against in any game, at least in recent memory. Maybe it's just emphasized by the ridiculous physics which are, I suppose, designed to discourage less than optimal racing. Trying to retain a faint connection to real F1 racing, they make it abundantly clear that COLLISIONS ARE BAD, MMKAY. Be a respectful driver.. and wreck them with power-ups like a good boy/girl.
However, optimal racing is an impossibility, especially when comparing a play to an AI. All of these problems are almost mute when a part of this merely acceptable Mario Kart clone. Then, strip the game down to "Pure Racing" and you just get slapped in the face with its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
Unbelievibly, despite the AI never taking an optimal race line or hitting any of the apexes of any corner, they are still consistantly as fast as if not faster than the player, unless you rely on the ridiculous draft system. If you brake into a corner properly, you WILL get rammed from behind and your race ruined. If you try to carfully overtake an AI through a corner on the outside and miraculously don't get hit from behind or have an AI slow to a crawl right in front of you, then the car on the inside WILL turn into your line and ruin your race.
So to recap, the AI never brake in corners and overtake you with easy, an often ram into you from behind. Yet, often times when entering a corner they will brake unpredictably and cause you to ram into them, even though they never brake. Despite the fact that the AI never take an optimal race line around the track, they make perfect time around corners, never missing boosts, while the player is in a constant struggle not to drift out of bounds while somehow managing to brake in a way to not get hit, enter corners in a way you can't be surprised by AI braking, or allowing any AI an opportunity to try and pass you on the side or enter your racing line.
Honestly, even though this game is a Mario Kart clone I expected it to have a stronger more realistic racing feel than it does. Furthermore, the amount of control I actually feel like I have over the car feels about comparable to ice tracks in Mario Kart, but not quite that extreme.
The power-ups lack any originality.
Oh, and the pit stops, oh my god the put stops. I could rage about them forever, about how AI will go into the pits on the last stretch and still win or even pass me, how if I go into the pits I will get passed by 3 other cars, all this mostly due to the fact that some pits are LONG AF and waste so much time while others might even be faster than the main race line.. seems legit. Ultimately, this inconsistancy leads to times where the standard of not pitting on the last stretch ends up with you losing the race. So, just keep in mind that whichever decision you make is probably the wrong one.
I would die for some online matchmaking to this game so that I don't have to deal with these AI, but I have yet to see a single person any of the times I've looked for a match.
Perfectly decent party game -- it's exactly what you'd expect. I'm not disappointed with my purchase, as these types of games are fun just to mess around on. I'd recommend this game to anyone who is into this type of game, despite the fact that they are probably better off just continuing to play their kart racer of choice. Jimmy Johnson's Anything With an Engine, right?
Edit: Just spent the last couple days playing Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed and it blows this game out of the water. It really made me realize how all the parts of F1 Race Stars work against each other, making it an incredibly unfluid and irritating experience. I'm not sure if on top of everything else that the tracks or poorly designed, or if it's just the terrible gameplay and uncontrollable cars that make it feel that way.
In the end, I could only recommend this game if you already know you want it. If not for the ridiculous collision effects, this game would still be passable. Truly one of the worst mechanics I've had to struggle against in any racing game.

Having played this game a while I will tell you all the pros and cons so you can decide if this game is for you. I greatly enjoy this game personally, but I am also a 16th Dan Katarina and 15th Dan Claudio, and don't mind just jumping into ranked. You may have a different experience based on your level of knowledge with previous Tekken games / your will to get better at this game. I rate this game 9/10 personally.
PROS:
-Best Graphics of any PC fighter. If you have a high end card you will love this.
-Large Roster with more characters coming.
-Customization system is pretty standard for a Tekken game but worlds beyond what you can do in Street Fighter / other games. (You can make your characters look like characters from other games or your favorite anime etc.)
-Game has endless replayability both at the beginner and expert level. You can always find a new way to improve your offense or defense.
-Most sticks and pads work flawlessly and you can even hotswap if you have a lot of people playing on one setup.
-Netplay is passable and you can find a good percentage of quality matches at 4 or 5 bars.
-Training mode is passable with many options to help you attack or defend against the dummy.
CONS:
-Game doesn't really teach you how to improve. You are given some sample combos with varying usefulness and sent on your way. (some people don't even know this exists! Check the bottom of your character's movelist for these sample combos)
-Frame Data not included in game. (If you care to know character frame data you'll have to do your own research)
-Story was fun for me as a Tekken fan but pretty lacking for a 'story'.
-Because the game doesn't teach you, learning how to defeat players of higher rank can be quite difficult for beginners. You need to depend on resources outside the game like Youtube videos / tutorials.
-Right now the only good offline mode outside of VS is Treasure battle, which gets old as a gimmick quickly. There is Tekken Bowl DLC coming soon though.

Whilst at work, I was reading Kotaku, and discovered that the developers of Zero Reflex were offering $10,000 to the player who could beat it first. I rushed home, bought it the moment it came out, and proceeded upon my descent into the maddening hell that is this game.
Zero Reflex is self-explanatory. You're limited to moving around a perfectly circular track that surrounds a nameless Eye. The Eye employs different attack patterns in each level, which you progress through in a random order. You work your way through the game, avoiding the things that make you die. Continue to do so until you win. Harder than it sounds, I assure you. "Ah," you think to yourself, "well that may be so for you, puny mortal, but I am the God of the bullet-hell genre." Well then, my Lord, if that is the case then you should definitely buy this, but seriously, this game'll still make you cry.
The unique twist that Zero Reflex employs is that whenever you die to a level, you have to repeat a certain amount of the levels you had completed prior. Die in any of those, and you regress even further. The higher the difficulty you're playing at, the further you regress with each death, and the less life you're given in order to survive each level. Effectively the game has 60 levels, comprised of 20 unique level designs, each with three difficulty modifers. Beat all 20 once, and you're made to repeat them at a higher difficulty. In the final set of 20, you die after one hit, and are sent back three levels for each death. Please be warned; this can get very upsetting.
I haven't quite beaten the game yet. I came incredibly close, before it decided to take what little hope I had of success, and beat me religiously with it until I gave up. And so I'm taking a break to write this review. However, I do believe that the $10,000 has already been won, given the amount of people with 100% of the achievements. That said, don't let it discourage you from buying this. For less than $5 it's a steal, the developers deserve your money, and what's more, it'll develop a love-hate relationship with you that you'll be telling your kids about for years. - "Ah yes, Timmy. I remember the days when I used to play Zero Reflex. I lost both of my hands to that vile game, y'know. Marvellous it was, marvellous."

Note: Now, This game is in early access and I believe there possibly going to more things included in the future, so I may update my review further once development of the game is nearly complete.
This Game... I mean it seems to be good, the concept seems rather nice. The main purpose of the game is to manage store in an fantasy world, an RPG one in fact to where you offer items to commoners and heroes. Though It doesn't sound that hard of a job to do such an thing unless the heroes go and act like the kind of heroes that players tend to be, those kind to which mess everything up for fun or even steal something out of plain view. You will feel the pain of an typical RPG Shop clerk, having to reorganize your wares, keeping an close eye on your customers, and also have to beware of barbarians who occasionally pay you an visit to ransack your store. Yet, I know I make all of this sound like something that could be an pain, but it's actually quite fun in my opinion.
As you progress through the scenarios in the game, you get level ups that allow you get bonus things that will help you out along the way and may unlock things from the missions. Also from the start of the game, you have in your possession an sword and an lightning spell that allows you to humorously take care of your thieving heroes and bloodthirsty barbarians, all while you are protecting your wares. The "combat" seems quite good and easy, though mainly with the greedy thieves, but difficult with the barbarians.
There is even an freeplay mode which allows you to completely manage the store (Yet, I don't know if you can change the style and structure of the entire store, maybe it will be possible in the future.), which you lay the display containers where ever you wish, though I would strongly advise that you keep them away from the door until you have no choice or your thieves will make an quick escape. Also I did mention that you unlock things in the scenarios, did I? Well, these things are usually new items to sell that will give you more profit. The difficulty for freeplay mode will increase as you proceed.
I will have to say that game is pretty decent for it's concept and current price, though I look forward to more improvement in the future. This game reminds me of an game "Recettear: An Item Shop's Tale" in it's current form except you don't kill your customers in it for an Health potion and the heroes are kinder than in this game. When I get the time, I may even make an video of this game once sometime has passed by. Currently, I haven't yet found any bugs within the game. This game is worth an look into for those who love management and trading games especially those who know of the cutesy Recettear game. The game only cost about $5, an pretty good price for an early access game like this.

Once you learn the levels a bit though it's not as big of a deal. I also played this on a much ♥♥♥♥♥ier computer so that may have contributed.

That being said, Interceptor has done a fantastic job since the game's launch patching most of the issues this game had, fixing optimization, adding new levels, adding a new gun that the community was allowed to name, and much more all for free. One of the best modern reboots of old-school FPS. It does a great job at maintaining that super fast-paced and extremely exaggerated gameplay that makes old-school fps adrenalinic and challenging. ROTT could be considered a deconstruction of the old-school FPS genre. It's almost a parody that overly-exaggerates the main elements of its genre: you could consider it the Saints Row of old-school FPS. The skill required to beat this game on the hardest difficulties adds replay value and because what little there is of plot does not get in the way of the action, it's pretty suitable for speedrunning on a competitive level. The only big issue with this game is the fact that it uses the Unreal Engine 3, which has a not-so-great performance and bad netcode (which makes it pretty unsuitable for competitive play in multiplayer). It would have ran much smoother and with better networking on the unreal engine 2004 IMHO. TL;DR: great singleplayer, one of the few reboots that maintains the old-school feel but don't expect a decent multiplayer, and also don't expect the game to run at capped 120 fps constantly.

Don't be put off by the cheesy, cartoony graphics and outrageous exaggerations of the gameplay. If you are a Formula 1 who liked Mario Kart at any point in your life, this a great game to get during a Steam sale. Sure, the items are frustratingly rigged and the whole game's full of gimmicks, it's still great fun, especially since you can race as caricatures of your favorite real-life drivers and even some
exaggerations of real racecourses (from 2012, at least).
Do note this is NOT a game to treat as a simulation in the same way that Codemaster's flagship Formula 1 games should be seen as. This is simply old-fashioned, item-throwing, boost-abusing, absolutely almost chaotic random fun you'd expect from any arcade racing game. And it excels at that, though the Multiplayer feature is a bust, unfortunately.
In terms of DLC, the addon tracks are great fun, and ignore the accessories. They're borderline useless and a waste of money. Other than that, you've got yourself a pretty solid arcade game to kill some hours. And you'll have plenty of fun, if your expectations aren't built around the Formula 1 simulators.

It's a nice game to waste a half hour or so. It's pretty much an arcade game and most gamers will easily pick this one up. There's no learning curve and even the flying and steering as well as aiming is quite casual. I bought if for a few bucks and it's fun enough.
The A.I. is very accurate with the turrets and it's often more efficient to just let the computer do the defending while the player jumps into the vehicles to mop up or to take over some of the turret platforms. The A.I. however has a specific range for each turret and will only fire when enemies enter that range.  If done in manual control, most of your turrets can fire across the map and mow down the enemy before they can even gather up for a proper assault.
There's not too many variation with the turrets though. I found the flame/gas/spray turrets too short range and inefficient compared to the machine gun. I mostly wind up with howitzers, machine guns and the occasional anti air gun depending on the level.
Like I said the game doesn't really require you to put too much thought into it.  Enemies are quite fragile and even vehicles can die to machine gun fire after some effort. The only difficulty comes from the bosses/mini bosses being bullet sponges.
A cheap game for some casual fun.

As having been a Deus Ex fan since the original, I was excited to hear that the 2011 Human Revolution would be receiving a sequel starring everyone's favorite badass covert-ops augmented super-agent Adam Jensen - the man with a gravelly voice and friggin' swords for arms. Mankind Divided picks up two years after Human Revolution. Adam Jensen is re-introduced into a world that hates Augs, the people who decided to go through with physical cybernetic augmentations to their bodies. It's caused a massive rift between the two very differernt societies and Prague is the epicenter for what could be a new flashpoint. It's up to Adam Jesnsen and his bio-mechanical enhancements to uncover the conspiracy and take out the bad guys. Collateral Damage notwithstanding.
There have been some serious gameplay improvements from Human Revolution, but Mankind Divided essentially plays almost the same as its predecessor. Its gunplay feels a lot better as ADS is now set to the Right Mouse Button rather than the Middle -- which is now, by default, reserved for a toggled augment of your choosing. The cover system has actually been slightly improved with the addition of more dynamic movement while in cover. Once you get in cover and look around you can press Space to either move to a different spot or to entirely new cover altogether. Adam can now grab onto ledges more fluidly, as well. Overall, while it still plays the same, it
so much better.
This, I think, is a good thing. I really dislike when a game series drastically changes its own mechanics for the sake of being "fresh and new." Veterans from Human Revolution will feel right at home while it still feels fresh and new all the same.
The Augments are definitely a lot better, as well. You have all of the same as you could get in Human Revolution plus some additional "hidden" augmentations that are unlocked after a story sequence early on in the game. These bring an entirely different feel to the game and are very welcome additions.
Now, I can't talk about this game without mentioning the performance - lest I be crucified by the vindictive hands of the internet. I run this game on an
,
, and an
. I'm well past the recommended specifications of the game and yet I do suffer some performance issues at 1440p. My framerates flucutate anywhere between 40 to 70, but after turning a few settings down I maintain anywhere between 50 to 80 depending on where I am in the game world. The game obviously needs to have an optimization patch, and it needs it sooner rather than later.
However, performance has not impacted my ability to play the game -- although despite my 17+ hour running time I'm not very far, yet -- as of completing this review, I'd completed what I would consider the "First Chapter" of the game's story and had just barely begun the next. I am playing on its highest default difficult, "Give Me Deus Ex." So far, I'm having a hell of a time with it. There's a lot to explore and uncover, and a lot of options to get around to your objectives.
I feel that this time around, Eidos Montreal finally got it right by bringing us as close to a modern Deus Ex experience as they can. It will never surpass the original game, and nobody should ever think that it would, but it's definitely very high up there for me.
EDIT: I've gone a little bit further in the story and can confirm that just about every section so far can be done either through brute-force combat, covert stealth, or a mish-mash of both. On the highest difficulty it makes for a very tense experience. So far I've not run into what might be considered a "boss fight" through fighting like in Human Revolution. I've also just reached the first major branch in the story and am eager to see what the consequences of it are.
EDIT EDIT: I have fully completed the game plus its side missions on Give Me Deus Ex Difficulty. I can confirm that the ending is definitely extremely disappointing and looks to set up the game for future sequels and DLCs. It feels like this was only the "first chapter" of a much larger plot that the developers seemingly wanted to do.
The whole game can be completed within 20 hours, shorter if done at a lower difficulty.
, the game itself was very well paced despite the ending. It was an extremely enjoyable experience overall.

Questions I ask myself when I review a game:
1. Was it fun?
>>Yes. DXMD is fun. I'm currently enjoying it.
2. How are the graphics?
>>Pretty good. Can't complain about it since I'm running a Fury X
3. What stands out the most?
>> I'd say the voice acting and sound track. I've always been a fan of the cyber punk style of DX sound tracks
4. Does this feel like a DX game?
>> Yes. It feels more "Deus Ex" than HR was, certainly better than Invisible war.
5. Storyline
>> Didn't play through the entire game yet but so far I'm intrigued.
6. Do microtransactions bother me?
>> No. I'm not a nitpicky moron. I paid $60 for a video game, if I complain about optional microtransactions then I deserve to be castrated before I can reproduce.
Thankfully I'm rational human being with a decent grasp on logic so things like this do not bother me at all.
7. How are the controls?
>> Could use some improvement. I'm not a fan of them to be honest. I picked the default scheme so maybe I should switch it up, but at this point it will only hurt me. The default controls (Xbone controller) feel clunky. Not exactly set up for smooth gameplay.
8. Would I recommend this game?
>> Yes. I do recommend it. It's a well polished game with a heavy story on top and plenty of content to keep you busy for over 30 hours (according to other reviews). The voice acting and graphics are top notch. I was a bit disappointed that DX12 wasn't included at launch but I'm willing to look past that since it is not a game breaking element. This is the most proper DX game to date since the original IMHO. I loved HR but that game spent too much time baby sitting the player instead of giving them a proper DX experience. DXMD definitely strikes a chord for me.
I really like the fact that they obtained the original voice actors from DX to set up the JC Denton storyline. It's small details like those that show me dedication.

Deus Ex Mankind Divided has been so far a fantastic experience and a well improved sequel from Human Revolution. Just about everything you can think about from Human Revolution has been improved on, better voice acting, larger city hubs, better hacking, more augmentations, better weapon customization, more weapons, better stealth, just overall an amazing amount of replayability and many side quests and options on how you would like to complete those objectives.
In Deus Ex Mankind Divded you once again play as Adam Jensen, taking place in 2029, 2 years after the events of Human Revolution, Jensen is faced with the aftermath of the Augmentation Incident and how he is going to solve it. Feeling like his choice from Human Revolution was a failure. After Hugh Darrow's hijack on the Bio-chip in 2027, augmented people all over the planet are forced against their will to violently attack those around them. The public is outraged and therefore despise people with augmentations. This causes the world to become divided and augs and natural humans are segregated.
Adam Jensen works for the Interpol-funded Task Force 29 that deals with augmented terrorists that have sprung up in response to this backlash. However, his allegiance is split between Task Force 29 (TF29) and a hacker group known as the Juggernaut Collective. Following his discovery of the Illuminati in 2027, Jensen is determined to bring down the shadowy group and collaborates with the Juggernaut Collective in an attempt to achieve this.
If you aren't struggling with performances issues then the game runs very smooth 60 fps with little to no frame drops in city hubs and large areas. The stealth mechanics have been improved from Human Revolution with smarter AI and the improvement to running from cover to cover, now you can efficiently run further distances to cover and avoid being detected by AI, The weapon customization is much better with the addition of crafting parts to add upgrades to your weapons like rate of fire, accuracy, ammo count, and damage along with purchasable attachments for your weapons. This game still gives you the freedom to choose your path to your objectives and how you want to complete those objectives whether you want to sneak your way through undetected, hack your way past all of the security measures, run and gun your way through places, or take the non-lethal route and use your tranquilizer rifle to put targets to sleep. You have all of these options in Deus Ex Mankind Divided you never feel like the game is linear because of the abundance of side quests, if you get bored of doing the main quest, go do a side quest or two to take a break. In Deus Ex Mankind Divided you never have to feel like you're forced to do something you don't want to do, you can choose based on your style of gameplay.
All I have to say about the graphics is wow. These graphics are the best i've ever seen. The reflections are flawless, the textures are crisp, the shadows are perfectly curved. This game just has beautiful graphics to say the least, but with that said, it takes a pretty beefy computer to play Deus Ex Mankind Divided.
The soundtrack defintely has a Deus Ex and cyberpunk esque to it. Michael McCann did a fantastic job on the soundtrack with great ambient pieces, tense cliffhanger pieces, and action-packed combat pieces.
Deus Ex has always been a franchise of replayability and Mankind Divided never falls short in the aspect of replayability. With anywhere from 4-10 options on how to complete your objectives, theirs always room to wonder what would've happened if you completed an objective this or that way. This opens doors for lots of replay value. The great thing about Deus Ex is you will not feel that your money has gone to waste, you could sit there and play this game 3 times and still have a different experience.
Yes. Without a doubt. Despite the performance issues, microtransactions and save locked dlc, this game is still a masterpiece of a story driven 1st/3rd person shooter. This game has everything from beautiful graphics, to a great soundtrack, to a fantastic story and smooth gameplay. This game is everything you want in a cyberpunk stealth game.

P.S. If you're having performance issues here are some steps you can try.
1. Play the game on High rather than Ultra: High looks almost as good as Ultra but uses a lot less power.
2. Turn off MSAA. MSAA uses unnecessary resources for little or no improvment to the graphics.
3. Update your drivers to the latest version.

I wasn't going to leave a review for this game until I finished it. But seeing how there's so many negative reviews on Steam I wanted to try and tip the balance back into positive.
First of all - I'd rather not insult people, but frankly - most of the reviews here seem incredibly whiny, pathetically whinging, or just plain stupid.
1) The Day 1 DLC (that you get for preordering) - some of the items it gives you are limited to one use .....apparently. Personally, since it was FREE, I haven't really noticed and don't give a rats derriere. ALSO - this DLC gives you an extra mission, and other content. So whining about it seems the very definition of over entitlement in my book.
IT COST NOTHING TO GET THIS DLC....!!! But lets put the boot into an amazing game because we're a big bunch of crybabies....
2) It has performance issues....funny, I haven't noticed any. It amazes me how pc gamers sneer at the fixed architecture of consoles, and then give negative reviews for a game which doesn't run well on THEIR SYSTEM - despite these kind of problems being FIXED WITH A PATCH SOON ENOUGH......
Personally - this runs perfectly on my pc, which is nothing special.
SO: Moving past these issues - HOW DOES THE ACTUAL GAME PLAY?.....
The short version:
If you loved 'Deus Ex Human Revolution' - you can buy this in complete confidence. It's excellent.
The long version:
This plays flipping brilliantly, which is why I'm so sickened by the negativity it has managed to obtain here. The level design is superb, the controls are very flexible yet super slick, and everything has been enhanced from its predecessor. In short - its everything that a sequel should be.
'Deus Ex Mankind Divided' takes place in a future where some humans have mechanical augmentations, that enhance their strength / agility / allow interaction with machines for things like hacking / turn invisible, or even sprout explosive projectiles from their arms. Due to an incident in the previous game these augmented people are feared by society, and find themselves hounded by the police.
The hero of the game is Adam Jensen - a man given augmentations after he was critically wounded during the events of 'Human Revolution', and who is now currently part of a taskforce investigating a terrorist threat. However, this is just the tip of the iceberg - and much more powerful forces are secretly manipulating things behind the scenes, as the shadowy group 'The Illuminati' continue their plans to shape the world for their own ends.....
At this point I don't know how the overall story arc is handled, mainly because I've spent 8 hours just following side quests. Which have been very enthralling - well written, and always with the thrill of discovering little things here and there.
To have people saying this is a linear game is a joke - I haven't even done the first part of the main storyline at this point......'Mankind Divided' is a game I was wary of after its initial reveal trailer, but now that I've played it I feel very foolish to have ever doubted it.
Even if it does come apart towards the end (which I wouldn't know yet) what I've played so far is too magnificent to be deemed "bad", and those people who've criticised it should hang their heads in shame. Whether stealth is your thing, or a violent shoot out - the game will meet your needs.
Every inch of its setting is jam packed with options. At its most basic - you can shoot your way through the game. But maybe you'd prefer exploration - either discover a nifty route that bypasses obstacles, or maybe find a password that opens a door - or lets you hack a computer thats controlling cameras or security turrets. Maybe you'll just distract guards and stealth your way past.
In some scenarios you could bribe someone, or find a new piece of information that you can use. There's very few AAA games that offer this amount of freedom to how you approach it, and even fewer that actually have decent shooting AND stealth mechanics whilst doing so. 'Mankind Divided' does all of these things superbly, and I find it ridiculous that people still complain about it....no wonder most high budget games are so shallow and cr*p when the players are this hard to please!
In case my position on this game isn't clear - the eight hours I've experienced have been superb.

A crazy and unique open-world, action, adventure, and real-time strategy game.  That's right... it even has RTS game-play that was modeled after the amazing Sega Genesis classic Herzog Zwei.  There is quite a bit of depth to the RTS with lots of different unit types and the ability to control where each group of units go on the battlefield. It's no fluke Rise of the Triad's 2013 remake has invited attention and excitement from a niche of arena and twitch FPS fans. A title fondly recalled in memories of the few being remade in UE3 is enough to make even the most cynical player dream of a return of the fast-paced, chaotic times of FPS yore.
Made after the now toxic Duke Nukem Forever licence was taken away, ROTT is obviously made by a team with fond memories of the original. In fact, it's probably a little too fond. As you progress further and further through the game, you realise core gameplay has changed very little in the almost twenty years since the first game was released. Sure, rocket jumping is a breeze, now, and it even has mouselook like all the kids are talking about. But with a tedious array of enemies that almost exclusively barrel at you with hitscan rifles that even the swiftest player is bound to be scraped by, it's less of a ballet of surreal ultraviolence and turns too closely into a frantic porridge hunt or, worse, a slow, careful shooter that rewards careful, slow approach to situations than maneuverability and split second twitch aiming.
Nothing has been learned in all this time from the evolution of the genre, whichever way you look it - It does not have the interesting array of weaponry or diverse cast of monsters that Doom has to constantly challenge you, nor does it have leaning or cover that a more modern, "tactical" shooter would encourage. It sits in the middle of both of these design philosophies as it once was all that time ago. But it can't rest on its laurels after all this time when the original simply wasn't considered particularly good. Its infamy came from its explicit violence, gore, and sense of humour, the latter of which has been replaced with painfully unfunny toilet humour and even more referential and internet meme humour (Writers everywhere, please, if you're reading this, can we have some good, original comedy, please?).
And even if you are a die-hard fan of the original, believing it is gameplay perfection, you'll find it difficult to still justify the purchase of this when the game is technically flawed in too many ways to count. Performance issues, bugs, map clipping errors, and technical shortcomings (You cannot rebind the weapon keys, half of your keyboard is likely not to work with binds, and you cannot turn off the mouse acceleration in the game, you need to edit a .ini file for this - In 2013, this is inexcusable!). With an apparently two programmers on a team of fifty artists, it's obvious where the emphasis on design was here, and if your technical foundation is not adequate, the content in it is wasted. If you must bring back a game from the past as close to the original as possible, you simply need more than pretty graphics and a 3D environment to justify its existence when even basic features and options do not exist or are broken.
I want to love this game. It's built with passion and a clear hatred of how FPS games have forgotten their roots. But to be so aloof about your own darling harms its credibility and place on the stage - There is nothing wrong with an obnoxious plotline and setting that still takes itself seriously, without hiding behind humour and ironic, meta-humour. And perhaps the developers need to be honest with themselves: Why make a throwback title that refuses to change anything about the core gameplay, when the original was sub-par? Maybe ROTT94 should have been left in the past as a stepping stone to where we are now, and a more respectable example of how arena FPS can hold strong in modern times. Maybe we could, dare I say... come up with something original, instead of tying ourselves to dated ideas that fog the timeless ones?

Tekken 7 is the latest in the Tekken series, a 4 button 3D fighting game. Each button corresponds to a different limb (left arm, right arm, left leg, right leg) and the fact that it's 3D means that you can sidestep some moves depending on how well they track. Played have access to high attacks (standing blocked, ducked), mid attacks (standing blocked), and low attacks (crouch blocked). It's often flaunted as one of the hardest fighting games to learn, and while this is true, it is also one of the most rewarding. Movement and spacing are crucial parts of fundamentals, and often in games you'll see players dancing around each other with Korean Backdashes and sidesteps, like boxers circling in a ring before making their next move. The game is balanced to the point where every character is truly viable, and the tier list is only relevant in regards to who has access to more options. A common piece of advice for new players looking for a main is to just pick someone who you like or think looks cool. Be prepared to spend lots of time in the practice room before testing your skills online though. Rounds in Tekken are 60 seconds long, and combos are important to dealing damage, so you will have likely spent hours practicing them until they're muscle memory. Walls, wall breaks, and floor breaks can be used as combo extenders. When both players are at low health and both throw out moves that could potentially kill at the same time (which happens more often than you'd think) the game will enter slow motion as you find yourself on the edge of your seat in anticipation, leading to many hype moments. On the more casual side of things there is character customization, so you can dress up your characters with items you've unlocked in the game's treasure mode, if you care for that. Other single player modes include arcade mode and the story mode. In terms of the story, it's not the best Tekken has had to offer but there's still plenty of good moments. The game was advertised to be the end of the Mishima saga, which is the conflict between Kazuya Mishima and his father Heihachi Mishima, and that's what it is. It's not a long story mode and I'd say I beat it in about 4-6 hours. Depending on how well you play it may go by quicker, but it's actually a pretty tough story mode, especially the final boss (that last fight is awesome btw).  Overall, Tekken 7 is a game with a rapidly growing player base and gameplay that offers something for everyone. Even some of my non-competitive friends have found themselves enjoying Tekken as it's a game where you can just mash buttons, and while that may not be optimal or safe, it can still lead to some awesome things. Just be aware that if you decide to take the game seriously, you will be spending A LOT of time playing.
TLDR: Tekken 7 is a highly complex, well balanced, fast paced, competitive fighting game. There's less single player content but enough depth to the gameplay that you will never stop improving, and never want to stop playing.

One of those stereotypical Korean games, it's a sequel to the old carpal-tunnel-inducing game GunZ: The Duel. Whereas GunZ: The Duel was fast-paced gunkata action that would wreck your wrists and fingers permanently, GunZ 2: The Second Duel is a slower game that focuses on player classes instead of allowing everyone to customize their characters and kit them out with whatever weapon they liked the most. This is both good AND bad.
The Good: Every character has their particular quirks that makes them great against some and weaker against everyone else. Each character comes with a particular set of skills; passives and extra movement options are unlocked as levels are earned. You can feasibly unlock every character and level them up individually, but that's tedious and boring. You're better off finding the one character you click with and sticking with them through your journey into the disappointment that is GunZ 2: The Second Duel.
The Bad: Everything else. The game has HORRIFIC netcode. I mean, I had not thought it was possible to beat old early 90's FPS netcode meant for 56K modems, but GunZ 2: The Second Duel proves that they achieved what they'd set out to do. Expect to see enemies warping around the map, and dying to enemies you can't even see on a regular basis. The only time these problems are alleviated are if you are the game's host; then, your ping is non-existent and you pretty much win the game if you're even slightly competent.
The Ugly: It's a free-to-play game, so it attracts the worst kinds of people the internet has to offer. The game insists on upgrading your weapons, but there's ALMOST NO DISCERNIBLE DIFFERENCE between the weapons statistically, and some of the weapons you can upgrade to EVEN WITH USING REAL MONEY have LITTLE TO NO IMPACT on the game whatsoever, and some are even WORSE THAN YOUR BASE WEAPONRY. Admirable, but no-one cares what kind of flashy weapon or skin you're using, 'cause 90% of the time people aren't even looking at you. Similarly hilarious, some of the miscellaneous items for sale - such as a hat that looks like a cat cutely perching on your head, ready to pounce - are EXORBITANTLY expensive for a F2P game.
Honestly, steer well clear of this game. If you're even slightly interested in the game, at least wait for them to fix the netcode before playing, else you'll walk out of the game wishing you'd listened to me.

This includes the credits, upgrade kits, crafting parts, and grenades/ammo.  None of this is mentioned in the ads for the DLC.  This likely ties in with the microtransactions added to the single player, which want to sell you more of those very same items...

This game feels almost exactly like what a Deus Ex game should feel like, and after playing Human Revolution multiple times through, I have to say that this game feels like a significant upgrade in the right direction as far as gameplay goes. The maps are beautifully intricate and provide a lot of immersion while still being locked up enough to keep the player from getting lost. The new control scheme feels more modern and definitely steered towards those who play FPS games, but the simple fact that they left the ability to play with controls from the last title in the series is a big plus. The gameplay is fluid and feels very much like a Deus Ex game, allowing for lethal and non-lethal approaches to nearly everything and also heavily rewards those who explore. There are some minor glitches, and some funny ones as well, but performance-wise I am running with specs nearly identical to the recommended specs and am getting a stable 59fps on high quality options settings in 1440p. I haven't experienced any crashes or boot-up issues either, but I haven't put this game around the block yet.
The one thing I can't really stand behind with this game is how they approached the consumables in the DLC. The microtransactions are easily a cop-out for some extra cash. But you know what? If you don't want them, then, wait for it, DON'T BUY IT. Don't bash the game for having what is in essence paid one-time-use cheat codes. You can play the entire game and still have a great and unhindered experience without them! However, the DLC that sticks to a single save and is gone forever there-after is just downright distasteful, so shame on you for that Square Enix. But this game truly deserves much more credit for it's gameplay than it is being given due to the presence of these completely optional microtransactions. People, they aren't locking day 1 content behind a pay wall, just shortcut content you can get for FREE via ACTUALLY PLAYING THE GAME. Don't like it? Don't buy it. Simple as that.

This game is just great. It entertained me over 80 hours (well perhaps about 75 hours, the rest of my gameplay is menu idleing while reading guides or wiki). I saw many reviews comparing this with Skyrim, but be honest, they are very different.
Soundtrack is very nice. Background music gives great atmosphere, but sadly there are a lot of soundbugs. I didn't hear any background music in the last 20 hours of gameplay. Sometimes sound of my characters battle voices and those of my weapons disappear. Only fix I managed to think about was restarting the game.
The voice acting was nice. Although there are not that many voice actors, but they were doing a good job.
You can develop your character in different ways. You can chose between three different skill trees, basicly that is the decision between Knight, Rogue and Sorcerer. But you can play any combination of those as well. Your skill tree will determine what weapons you will use. I played with the Rogue skill tree because I like stealthy approaches, and the dagger and faeblades you find are really nice and very fast. Great in combination with a bow for range attacks.
You can make tons of side quests and task. After completing the game and both DLCs I managed to complete over 200 quests (including the main quest).
Combat is very repetitive. When you know how it works, it gets very very easy and you will fight almost the same every time. I played the game on hard. The first 10 levels were hard, because of bad equipment and stupidity ;) But after that it was very easy. Maybe I died 20 times during the remaing 30 levels.
Very nice was the fact, that NPCs you have to follow or are your companions don't run slower than you. They run at least as fast as you, sometimes even a little faster, but they are waiting if you get too far away.
The only thing I really hated in this game was the camera. You cannot control the FOV. It adjust automatically to your current situation. Zooms out when there is an enemy far away. Gets closer if not. But sometimes this stupid camera drops below earth and all you see is dirt.
Or in cutscenes you will see just a wall or a shoulder of a total different NPCs
All in all a very nice RPG. Go get it when it is on sale. Take your time doing all side quests and you will be entertained for a long time.

Bought it for $1.49 during Summer Sale. I'm extremely cheap when it comes to games (if it has no replay value, I almost always ignore it) but this game, IMO, is esaily worth up to $5. (Note: If I say $5, the comparable to a normal person that isn't as crazy cheap as me would willingly pay $7.50+ for it without hesitation). I only say $5 because I finished the game in one sitting and it took me about a total of 2.5 hours.
GAMEPLAY: It CAN be played with keyboard, but you might as well not even try it if you don't have a controller, it's just made for controller and has not even made an attempt to be optimized for PC/KBM. It plays like a very nice, fluid puzzle adventure. You don't get obvious neon arrows pointing you in the direction you need to go nor does it hold your hand through each challenge. If you're stuck, call on the big bro and he'll point out where to go, but that's about it. This is a huge thing for me, I hate how the new generation of games have become this baby-friendly style where everything is given to you, pointed out, or you have to just put down some more money to advance. Regardless, this game works nicely with a controller but it's up to the person controlling it, I had a hard time being consistent with controlling both brothers at once so sometimes my mind would confuse me and both brothers run the opposite way-happened about a dozen times throughout.
STORY: Extremely great story, I'd say it's more of an interactive movie rather than a game with a story. Plenty of cinematics and gameplay put side by side, alternating. I'm not a very emotional person but I definitely was saddened by the story.
GRAPHICS: I don't have a very nice PC but it played at a solid 60 FPS (with/without vsync) although I had some screen tearing throughout the ENTIRE game, just one horizontal blur going up and down my monitor the entire time, about 2cm tall. You can only change the resolution in the launcher and whether or not to have vsync, that's it.
Note: You can reassign the keys if you're using KBM but the controller keymapping is completely set, just plug n play for that.
All in all, great game, great story, meh graphics [options] (absolutely horrific PC port), very sad ending, I'd give it a solid 8/10 for being all those above but -2 for the bad port

This is more of a first impressions review, as I have just started my adventures on this game.
Many years ago, I got the original Mount & Blade on
, and by recommendation of friends, I decided to give it a go. While the concept of it really attracted me, back then I found the game to be a little confusing and couldn't quite understand the combat mechanics of it, so I gave up. Now I decided to give it a try again.
This is an awesome sandbox RPG. Set in medieval historical times, without any kind of magic or supernatural powers to back you up, you are an aspiring adventurer, whose background you can choose when you create the character (in a very RPG way). Even being a singleplayer game, this game focus strongly on roleplaying and making your own tale in a nasty medieval world. You start by building up a small force of mercenaries, usually untrained peasants from villageers because they are cheap. You fight bandits so that you can gain battle experience. You start running errands for kings and nobles so that you may gain their favor. Many of those errands will me morally ambiguous. For example, a king asked me to go to a distant village and collect tributes. Citizens complained about the tributes. I ignored the complaints, as it would hurt my relation with the king. Villagers attacked me. I beat the crap out of villages. They pay tributes. I get some of the cash. The king likes me. So yes, I had to be a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to earn the favor of the king, and I think this adds to a certain realism. You can be different though. You can be a complete robin hood, oppose the king and lead a rebellion. You can do whatever you want. This game is all about freedom, just like any RPG should be. You can be a looter, you can swear loyalty to a king and become his vassal, you can marry into a noble house, you can capture bandits and sell them to slavery. This game's representation of Medieval times, while being certainly romantized, does give you a nice ambientation of those  times. Is it realistic? Not so much. You can rise from a complete nobody to a noble or even a king, something that would never happen in real medieval times. But damn, is it an enjoyable adventure.
You can gather a party of mercenaries who will eventually grow into an army. Many of those mercenaries are actually charactes with backgrounds, stories, and particular sets of skills which you can take advantage of. For example, I'm still at the beginning but I already have the daughter of a nobleman who knows how to boost my party's morale and has connections to noble families. I have a merchant who is very skilled at trading and bartering. I have a daughter from a scumbag family who married into a husband who abused her, ran away, became very skilled at fighting and is proficient with every weapon in the game. All those different charactes with backgrounds and stories enrich the roleplaying experience. You can enter tournaments, defeat nobles and win the tournaments, and be invited to a feast with nobles in the castle. You can teach villagers how to defend themselves against bandits and win their favor - or you can be the bandit yourself and pillage the vilalge. All different ways to gain notoriety and rise in life. In the end, you will be leading a powerful army and will be able to do whatever you want.
As for combat, it is certainly unique. It is tricky to learn and more tricky to master, but it certainly feels very satisfying when you do it. You use a combination of different thrusts and slashes with swords, axes or polearms. You can block with your weapon or a shield. You need to learn the right places to attack, parry, and counter. If you are on a horse, you take advantage of the horse's momentum to deliver powerful swings or simply run your enemies over with a spear. Crossbows and bows are also available. It is difficult, but very rewarding when you do it right.
Graphics wise it is not really a good looking game. Characters are ugly as hell. The whole texture work feels like a PS2 game. But hey, when you have such a complete roleplaying experience, use your imagination. You can also download a lot of great mods from the workshop and improve you game greatly.
Very recommended game if you are a fan of classic, tabletop RPG and medieval times. Not recommended if you only  like games with a strong main story: this game does not have one, you choose your own path and you build your own story. If you thought skyrim was oriented to side quests, wait until you play this one. There are no main quests at all.

Shoppe Keep is very addicting, and satisfying.
The idea is that you play as the NPC you always see running shops in RPG games. You buy stock for items, choose the price  and profit you will be making from the item, build your shop, sell to customers. Sounds simple enough, but there are a lot of aspects that make the game very interesting.
You can actually set your prices too high, that way customers won't purchase your items, and sometimes even slap them off their spot. Why? Because they're ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
Occasionally you'll get a sneaky bugger that thinks they're smart, and they'll try to steal one of your items. If you act quick enough, you can slash at them with your sword, or zap them with magic. All the customers in your shop will run away at this point, but atleast you got your item back.
Keeping your shop clean is also something you need to keep an eye on. All these filthy NPCs don't wipe their boots at the door, so everywhere they walk, they leave filth. You will be inspected every now and again, so it's best you sweep all the dirt, and corpses off of the floor.
There are a lot of items to buy, each are sought out by differnt types of customers. Commoners, adventurers, mages, etc.
You can also upgrade your character permanently across all levels with points. You earn these points by leveling up, which is basically by doing everything. You can grab upgrades like "Gain 10% more money from purchases", "Faster delivery of items" or "Anti-thief barrier".
There are 2 modes to choose from as it is. You can choose "Scenarios" which is almost a story mode. You play one mission, and try to complete the goal set out. For example "Sell 5 leather gloves, 3 studded gloves and 2 mana potions". Each mission has something to keep the game a bit fresh. Everytime you complete a scenario mission, you unlock new items you can buy in the "My Shoppe" mode. This mode allows you to freely build up your shop from the ground up. No scenarios set for you, just you close in the evening, build furniture to showcase your items, and then open up your shop.
Overall, the game is really satisfying when you start selling loads of items, or catch dirty thieves.
Recommended!
