TL;DR version - fun, relatively balanced, great port, if you enjoy fighting games or Tekken as a series, buy it.
First of all, they've actually been listening to their fans, and put the effort into making a high-quality port.  This shows in almost every aspect of the game, and is greatly appreciated, many studios and development houses could learn a thing or 30 from this game.
Graphically, I wouldn't call it "advanced", but the art style is nice, graphics are more than sufficient for a fighting game, and the simplicity of the format/depth of Unreal Engine allow for some genuinely batshit character customization.  More on that in a bit.
Sound is great, love the musical score too, especially the title theme, impacts, moves, grunts, all informative and distinct, but not repetitive enough to be grating (exception: Lucky Chloe, jesus, her squeaking, make it stop), very strong audio presentation.
Technically the game is on point, my high end gaming rig runs everything well, but, more importantly, I tested the game on what is effectively a potatoPC, and it was still appreciably smooth, and what I'd term "more than playable".
Network/netcode/whatever you want to call it is also well-done, best I've seen in a mass-market fighting game so far, actually.  Only complaint is sometimes matchmaking can take a little longer than I'd like (~2m between fights range, even when there's plenty of people online playing the game), and sometimes the connection performance indicator on your opponent is not accurate (as in it would rate their connection to me very highly, then it would lag like hell upon play), this could be lagswitching, or something on my end, but it happened often enough I'm disinclined to believe that.
But with a good connection, while playing someone with a good connection, it's amazingly smooth and responsive, as in "you can actually low parry on reaction" responsive, while playing against someone from the west coast (I'm in Texas), so the netcode is good if you're on solid lines.
Story mode is typical Tekken fare, if you're buying it exclusively for single player, I hope cosmetic rewards and customization and just a flat out good fighting game are your schtick, the story mode...  I mean, it's not "bad", but it's not $50 good, but character costumes and such are actually really deep and flexible, and again, mechanically, it's a great game.  And some love/work went into the story mode, and it's fun, but it's quite short and some of the voice acting/storyline is "questionable".
Blah blah, buy it unless you hate fighting games/fun.

Pros:
Good graphics
Amazing level design (The game is linear but the design still makes the world seem big)
Good fantasy themed, walking through a wolf infested cemetery or the  remains of a giant battleground (seemingly recent given how much they're bleeding). Definitely good changes in atmosphere.
Main characters are brothers who I assume intended to one day join the circus given how athletic they are.
Achievements are neat hidden things to interact with rather than just stuff you do for beating the game, they also let you put an end to bunny prejudices.
Mix of emotion with areas. (Some more adventurous areas are shown to be exciting or joyful but overall the game has a sad overtone to most of the interactions you see.)
Cons:
Controlling two characters at once can get confusing. Makes you feel like an idiot when you forget which stick controls which brother and you end up running into walls.
Some graphical bugs, shadows in some parts would overlap in a weird way, textures for things that collapse didn't blend well sometimes, and occasionally around cutscenes there would be black silhouettes of where the character models would eventually be standing. These weren't too bad to be a major pain though.
The game is short as I said earlier, the only thing to slow you down is figuring out how to solve the little bit of platform puzzle the game has but they tend to be pretty easy.
Worth a buy for a lower price.

I will be reviewing the game and the condition of the gameplay itself. I will be comparing some elements to mortal kombat 9 in this review.
Mortal kombat x is based on the new generation of fighters as well the original cast that were invovled in the tournment, to participate in protecting earth realm and stopping the brotherhood of shadows.
Story Mode:
-Good-
I liked how each of the characters in the story mode bounced off each other well. The plot was fonded interesting as the new characters made their appearance and showed what they are capable of.
-Bad-
Was slighty disappointed as the story left out a considerable amount of plot holes that casual players and even Mortal kombat fans could not understand. It also can be completed within a few hours of game time depending on your skills. Certain returning casts from Mortal kombat 9 are invovled in story mode but can not be used in the game. My favourite kombatant in the game is stryker, but what im complying to is, why put him in the story mode cast if hes not playable? Id rather him not appear in the story. Same goes to all kombatants. All thats doing is annoying Mortal kombat fans. For mortal kombat fans that played this mode would find each character levels confusing comparing to the MK9 story.
Gameplay:
-Good-
Very impressive as the mechanics of the game is flexiable. When choosing a character you can be able to choose 3 different play styles that go with it. That gives you enough playing time to invest on what character and style is best for you or mastering the physics of every character in the game itself. More than happy with how the game is trying to do something different through the mortal kombat series. Fresh, brand new game. The graphics and the fatalities in this game is the best so far from the series and the graphics are on point. The Krypt mode is amazing. A whole new adventre unlocking things in the game and getting jump scares while exploring. Impressed with the design of the mode.
-Bad-
Factions is beyond the most pointless thing they ever tried to put into the game. Why create this feature in the game if you can use any chracters that are apart of their own affiliation? For example Sonya Blade. Her background is based on special forces. Why can I use her in any faction if she is meant to be special forces? Pointless and ridiculous! Another silly thing about this game is the fact that they didnt even put a tag team mode in it. If factions are based on team work why isnt this been mode been put in the game? I was hyped for it when I heard about it before released date imagining you could use jax and sonya in tag mode on a special forces faction. Netherrealms created an achievement stating you have to jump teams and gain the right amount of experience. So how can some players be loyal to their factions if the achievements are made like this?
If you are an fan of the mk universe, you will find theirs limitations to most returning characters. Like raidens teleportations can be used only in one variations and sonya's military stance can also be used in one also.
-Condition-
On release date, this game turned into a tragedy as it was almost unplayable, but months later it got patched up. Worry no more on that side of things. This game is CPU hungry so I would suggest getting the reccomended chip for the game. The netcode is not the best of things as Ive noticed delays compared to online and singleplayer. Players will always have a problem with playing smooth matches with opponents online nevertheless. Its something we have to get used too.
-Conclusion-
Very fun game to play and it will last for sometime. Nice to see that netherrealm is doing something different with their franchise and moving on up with the next generation of gaming. MKX was a huge let down compared to 9. Once again, the Mortal Kombat franchise is falling right back in line with its legacy; a great comback (MK9) followed by a plethera of mediocre follow-ups, until the inveitable rock bottom hits and the cycle begins all over again.
I'm not a fan of the new combat system. Chossing one particular fighting style essentially locks you out of the other 2/3rds of their special moves. It's not innovative or fun. It's just irritating.
I absolutely hate the majority of new characters, and the god-awful campaign pales in comparison to the standard set forth in 9. It's horrendously cheesey, badly written, and poorly acted. Most of the great classic characters appear in story mode, but aren't playable (they'll obviously release them later as paid DLC). What a joke.
The PC port has been a hot mess since launch, thanks in large part to WB's decision to outsource the job to a third party. It suffers visually due to the sheer laziness of the developer. Intro cutscenes are hard locked at 30fps, while the game runs at 60 fps, creating a jarring difference inbetween fights. For christ sakes, even MK9's character intro's were shown at 60fps.
Overally, the game is visually and sonically pleasing, with what little there actually is. Not a ton of levels or characters. Character designs and models are a mixed bag. The more human fighers are incredibly generic in terms of design and execution. The offspring characters (aka Johnny's daugher, Jax's niece, etc.) are some of the worst looking of the bunch. Sub Zero and Scorpion look great, as always, so it has that going for it.
MKX is a bargin bin title if I've ever played one. I'm lucky I didn't spend more than $45 when it released, but there were plenty of suckers who shelled out $90 for that awful Goro pre-purchase incentive bullsh*t.

Unplayable.  Game-breaking bugs.
Oh gosh, where to start.
The landscape from the country to the city to even the fire house is really nicely designed.  The graphics, however, do not do it justice.  The graphic engine has to be at least 15 years old.  Maybe more.  Think "Ultima IX" days.  The textures on the fire apparatus especially were continually heavily pixellated.
Being a sim, there is more to do than just "squirt the wet stuff on the red stuff."  It's all nicely detailed.  Pity you don't have time to do much of it as the calls come in so fast.  Fortunately, the game seem to be so buggy that anytime I was low on oil or had some other mechanical problem, the game conveniently forgot about it after a scene change or even if I just left the vehicle and got in again!
The game can be quite merciless.  The tutorial (it doesn't deserve the word) teaches you nothing about playing the game.  It's just a tour of the firehouse.  You get no direction, no hands-on experience before your first call comes in.  Better would be some free time to explore and play around and then manually initiating the call.  There is a communications room after all.  The game also doesn't allow you to save your progress aside from autosaves.  Sometimes those autosaves are only at the beginning of the shift.  If you fail your mission at the end of the shift, well enjoy starting all over at the beginning of the shift.
The vehicles are difficult to handle, driving consisting of jerky movements.  It takes some getting used to, but after a couple times it gets easier.  The controls are awkward though, with the turn signals especially placed in strange locations on the keyboard.
The worst -- the absolute worst -- is the collision detection.  Good luck putting out fires.  You can sit there and pour a Biblical Flood of water onto the fire and it won't go out because it isn't detecting the water hitting the fire.
Don't let's talk about the minimal effort put into the NPCs who wander the fire station or sit in your vehicle and spout the same two lines every 10 seconds.
I've played several firefighter games.  Real Heroes Firefigher for the PC was the most recent.  (Another game with game-breaking bugs.)  Firefighters 2014 has to be one of the most interesting in concept.  But its execution was the worst I have ever seen.
Laughingly, there is a choice on the main menu called "Credits".  I was surprised.  I can't imagine anyone wanting to be associated with this game.
I love firefighting games.  This one especially caught my attention since it promised more detail.  Sadly, this was the worst game I have ever played.

Amalur is a well-polished game with it's base game being extensive, easily offering up 40+ hours of gameplay and up to 70+ if you explore all side quests. Its colourful, with well scripted dialogue, some unique combinations of standard fantasy concepts without being too aggressively unique, and placed an interesting spin on the undying character (with an idea as interesting as Assassin's Creed's Animus). However it fails to maintain interest during the late game as quests and challenges become all too easy, leading up to a disappointing ending that would have been far more interesting if it had more impetus.
Boss fights are also poorly executed with a variety of standard RPG tactics being utilised, and no unique inventive ways to challenge the enemies provided. Many of the Bosses attacks, have been done in previous games before, not a problem if you're new to the genre, I suppose, but problematic for 3rd person action RPG veterans.
Amalur does provide an interesting levelling and skills tree progression, that allows for limited customisability, but does shine in its simplicity to understand, and ways to play around and discover effective combinations of skills from its three separate progressions.
It's most definitely a fun game to play and waste a few days on, but won't offer much depth either in combat or narrative, so will always be a rather dismal second to its far more developed and innovative competitors.

When I told a friend I had started playing Kingdoms of Amalur Reckoning, he told/asked me two things.
1) Do you like Fable?
2) Welcome to babies first Skyrim.
If you took fable (without all the fun) and it had sex with the Elder Scrolls Wiki, this is what you would have.
This is far from a bad game! It is fun to be way overpowered (I played as a mage) and right from the gate you obliterate enemies left right and centre. This is good! It is exactly what I wanted from a game like this. It played well, smoothly and looks great in a very stylised fashion. What I didn't expect however is how DEEP and STEEPED this game is in lore. I can honestly say 90% of my play time (no joke) is reading and remembering characters/NPC's. I thought this was a little strange until I found out that Kingdoms of Amalur Reckoning was originally intended as an MMO (something that I feel would have made for a totally different review!) and it changed how I played the game after that. I absorbed as much of the story as I needed and moved on in proper MMO style (and boy was I happier for it!) but it made for a hollow experience as it is (literally!) an MMO world and Lore with no other players...
So what do I think of this? Your experience will vary. It is a fun but very lonely experience with a ton of very cool story that you can delve as deep into as you like. Is it tedious? Yes. Is it huge? Yes. Is it fun? Yes. Was it designed for single players? Not really.

Kingdoms of Amalur: The Reckoning, is a very vibrant, detailed, and content-filled action-RPG. Although a few primative features make it frustrating at times, such as no auto-save functio, this is a very satisfying open-world fantasy experience that will keep you playing. Each side quest somehow feels intertwinned to the main story, which is great because it never feels like it's wasting your time. The upgrading system is quite excellent, although it is possible to become over-powered very quickly, if you choose to focus on one skill set, e.g Might, where you can hack a troll to death in a few swings. The combat is satisfying. Not too fast or too slow, and in most cases you can't just button mash. You must use a variety of weapons, magic and techniques to overwhelm your foe. And that's why I purchased this game, for a satisfying and rewarding hack and slash experience.

This game is, simply put, incredible. There are a few flaws, yes, but everything else is so brilliantly done that you can quickly forget those.
Pros:
Good graphics.
Great character balancing. One of the rare games that if you want to make a mix between the various skill trees it lets you do it, and gives you unique bonuses as well.
Good battle system. Haven't played much of fighter or mage, but the rogue's combat abilities are very good, and the combo system is easy to use.
Great story. Hard to give any example without spoiling anything.
Factions. There are a lot of factions, each with its own main plot and side quests.
Crime system. The crime system is very similar to what Fable had. Did a crime? No money to pay bounty, don't want to go to jail either? Get out of town and let things settle down. You can also turn off safety mode, to kill any civilian in cities (also similar to fable)
Map size. In my current (and most advanced) game, I have less than 1/4 of the map explored, with over 10 hours of gameplay.
And most of all... Quests. So many quests. Some very trivial, being as simple as going to see someone and talking to him, some much more elaborate and hard, such as clearing an area of all Ettins.
Cons:
In the case of the rogue, the sneak attack is not as relevant as you'd expect, due to the combat abilities you have. If you have the occasion (or want to challenge yourself), do try to kill a few enemies in stealth, but otherwise it isn't worth it.
Travel on long distances if you don't have a fast travel can be long, as there is no other mean of transportation than running.
Inventory system is similar (if not identical) to Dragon Age: Origin. 70 invetory space, each item takes one space, stackables take one space per stack. As I am someone that just loots everything, this can be quite a bother (especially at lower levels), and the price for backpack expansions are steep when starting.

For RWBY fans, this game is gold. It's fun, it can be addictive, and the fact that you can play alone AND with three other friends or players is just the icing on the cake. For anyone else, it's a decent hack-and-slash game with an attack combo that makes you feel as though you're actually dealing damage to enemies, and visually appealing special attacks.
With that being said, I wish there were a few more things added to the game, such as badges for your profile and achievements that you could unlock. I wish there were more characters to play as, though since it's early access, there still might be hope. I also wish that, in order to attack with a combo, you could just hold down the left mouse button, as well as continue to click. (My finger got rather sore with the constant clicking)
I also would like it if the targetting for the guns was a bit better, instead of lining up for the shot. Maybe a lock-on feature?
I do wish that playing solo would lower the difficulty down a bit, as while it's entirely possible to play through it alone, it's very difficult to do. The Ursa Major, in particular, can be quite difficult to deal with alone. Still, the game is enjoyable and it being in early access means there's plenty that could be updated and added in. If you're a RWBY fan, this is THE game for the series. If you're just looking for a decent hack-and-slash that's also co-op, give this a go!

As it stands, this is a (very) watered-down Dynasty Warriors, and I can't argue with gameplay I like. But unlike Dynasty Warriors, there's no real combo system. There's only two combo strings: the melee string and the ranged string. (which isn't really a combo, since you just fire your weapon repeatedly.) Since there's no shared experience system, co-op feels like "every man for himself" as you rush to get to the next group of enemies before the rest of your team does so you can get some experience.
That said, this definitely has some potential. I honestly think this game looks much better than the show! With some polish, this might flesh out into a really great game. The compliment I'll always give this series is the designs of the characters and weapons (AW SWEET LAWDY THEM WEAPONS), and they feel like they function roughly the same as (I assume) they do in the show. The character models are nice and neat and the animations are well done, with the exception of a prevalent lack of any "switch from movement to idle" animations.
TL:DR-
Pros:
*Interesting DW-esque gameplay
*The game looks beautiful
*Great weapon and character designs
*Kudos on making an early access game actually look playable
Cons:
*Lack of a combo system
*Character leveling feels pointless
*No "real" cooperative play
*The VOICES.
*Lack of a set level selection system, or anything thereof

At anytime the game allows you to command any tower and also includes playable tanks and airplanes to aid in your defense. Each level has its own unique design and offers a challenge. I was able to obtain General rank (no lives lost) on all the original and DLC levels by playing the level a couple of times to figure out all the spawn points and what the best strategy is. Paperbound is quite a polished title. It is a party game or party-styled, because I've been playing single player and still having fun, there are a variety of modes but the core gameplay is throwing scissors and ink bombs at your opponent while running around doing the objective. There is also a satisfying melee attack that you can use to block scissors at the right time.
The game is just very fluid, easy to grasp, and chaotic. You have the ability to switch gravity like in the game VVVVVV which can lead to some confusion and adds another aspect of crazyness to this fast-paced game.
The graphics are quite nice in motion, there is a 3d element to the stages, and the main menus are presented as 3D books. The whole presentation is really good, especially in motion. Another suprise is the music. It's a lot more epic than you'd expect, but it fits the game.
Worth playing for sure. Grab it if you find it for a dollar or two.

The theory behind it,  reaching a set score limit and then escaping works in theory, but the problem is that these matches can last for an infinite amount of time due to the fact that if you are killed, the portal goes away.  This is particularly problematic when playing with a partner as both members must reach the goal together.  This is tricky enough, especially when playing the campaign mode in single-player,  but it is compounded on certain stages.   For example, the Grinder, a stage from Dante's Inferno, ok, awesome idea..  touching the walls means death and moving platforms all over.. cool...  but when you ad in AI to the mix,  well my opponents were at a score of -81 when I finally had enough.   My team was able to reach the frag limit several times, but given that it takes a few seconds for the tear to open up, and that my partner was getting killed or killing me the moment it appeared, victory, while possible, seemed very unlikely unless I played for a very long time.
My other major gripe is that campaign mode does not posess a save feature of any sort for progress.  You could argue that other, similer games do not use this and are successful, but with the nature of gameplay (particularly the flaws in the above game-mode) being unable to stop and return to the book where you left off seems like a major problem.
In conclusion, this is a fun little game.  I enjoyed playing it despite the frustrations, but it would be a LOT better if these issues were dealt with.

If you've ever played Gunz: The Duel, you either immediately disliked it or gave it a chance and continued playing until you really fell in love with it. If you're someone who didn't like it, then this is most likely a better game for you, however, if you're one of those who fell in love with it and played using ANY of the styles (K-Style, E-Style, D-Style etc.) then you need to go into this game with a new frame of mind. This isn't the same game, this is essentially a reboot. The game is very different and very fun if you simply give it a chance. The mechanics that made Gunz: The Duel what it was are non-existent anymore but this game is fun. Keep in mind, it's still early access and there are always going to be balance issues, whether in specific characters and abilities, or just in mismatched matchmaking. You could get into a game on a team of 4 level 1s who have never played before against a 15 a 12 a 10 and a 13. Just know that there is potential for fun in this game, in the early levels it's very difficult to enjoy it as you are at a fairly large disadvantage, but as you learn and level up it gets more and more fun until you really know what you're doing.
TL;DR If you liked Gunz:The Duel, give this more than a few seconds to decide whether you like it. If you didn't, this is probably the game for you.

So firstly off the bat I should say I have WAY more playtime on this, but I recently bought it on Steam and haven't played that much, so don't go ''OMG u only haev 2 hrs, wtf m8'' on me.
So. Driver® Parallel Lines.
This was one of the first games I ever played on my computer and I absolutely adored it.
It is one of the most underrated Driver games, and I recently even saw some hate on it which was really unecessary to be honest, cus this is one of my favorites from the Driver series.

Now, let's go over the pros and cons:
Pros:
-Open World
Meaning you can explore the city of New York, which has neighbourhoods that exist in real life (Bronx,Queens,etc)
-A SH*TLOAD of cars
About 94/95 vehicles in this game, including bikes and cars.
-Customization
Well, almost all (if not all) of the 94/95 vehicles are highly customizable, ranging from 4 (5 in some cases) custom bodyworks with paintjobs (or without) , accessories (tinted windows, bulletproof tires and glass) , colours (4/5 default, also there's an option for custom colors, making it with the ''RED,GREEN,BLUE'' filter), nitrous, upgrades to engines,brakes,acceleration and such (almost like the pre-GTA V, GTA V)
-Loads of weapons
Well by loads I mean about 11 or 12. So yeah. Loads.
-Vast enviroment
The enviroment is actually giving a sense of life with people doing casual thing such as buying donuts at stands or jacking cars. No NPC police chases tho. Shame.
-Graphics
Now yes, graphics. This sh*t looks mighty fine for an '07 game dude, like really good.
-Cheats
There are some cheats which can spice up the gameplay. There is the usual godmode cheat, the ''all vehicles in garage'' cheat (same for guns) and it actually kinda makes the game better. About 9/10 great cheats, I think.
-Story
Now yes the story is divided into two different timezones. 1978 and 2006.Both offer new vehicles and weapons along with missions. The missions are both fun and most importantly not just stuff to fill the gaps in between the timezones. The cutscenes are quite a bit different from the graphics of the real game but they look nice so I don't really care
-Thrill Cam
So yea that's a cam which goes into this ''Thrill'' mode and just thrills the sh*t out of my cam. Nifty stuff.
-The soundtrack
Oh the soundtrack. One of the best I've ever seen. Its like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥ but for your ears. An eargasm.
Get it? Get it? Mah f*ck you too then.
Cons:
-Bugs
A few minor bugs such as getting stuck on a f*cking lightpost. Nothing game-breaking tho.

But be warned, the game is unfair, not difficult, UNFAIR!
There are 4 types of enemies:
- Green - the default shoot'em up kind
- Red - sticks to your horizon and you have to dodge
- Blue - Destroy your horizon
- Swarm - insta kill you if they reach your horizon
The problem is, once a red or blue enemy reaches the horizon (50% of the enemy types) you have 3 ways to clear your mistake
1- die...
2 - clear the wave (reach next stage)
3 - use a bomb
OK I can use a bomb! But you have to fill a bar to get 1 and if you die you lost your bomb or the current progress... So your only way to counter those enemies isn't reliable. The game got nearly impossible on wave 25/26, and when you finally reach wave 27 you'll probably have 1 life without upgrades or a bomb under your sleeve.

The Story:
I found out about this game after doing some late night googling on Salvatore. 20 years ago I started reading his books and was amazed that I completely missed the fact that he worked on a game and it immediately went on my wishlist. The main story was okay, I don't really have any complaints but I didn't really feel any Salvatore coming through and I am unmoved. Anyone could have written/helped write the world and I wouldn't know any difference.
The Art:
Simultaneously I found out Todd Mccfarlane had some play in the art and I have an entire box of Spawn comics. My favorite childhood artist and writer together for one game, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ The color is great in the game but the lack of detail is mind boggling. Todd put so much detail into spawn comics and seeing character models without fingernails was just disgraceful. The graphics and animations are rather plain and nothing here is an artistic achievement. At one cutscene I recall a female soldier being shot in the back with an arrow and I think they tried to animate blood coming out of her mouth but it just looked like it was pouring out her face. Mediocrity is the theme for the art.
The Gameplay:
Through and through this is a single-player MMO action rpg. You could take any free to play mmo, remove the multiplayer and nothing about this game would outshine any of the uncountable amounts of games in the genre. Pretty much each zone has a town, each town has npcs with exclamation marks giving out fetch and kill quests. Each zone is linked together by a passage. There are basic tradeskills with the classic WoW style herb gathering, jewelcrafting , blacksmithing (except the last two you get regeants from chests and not nodes) and you don't need to invest in any of them although healing potions are the end all-most powerful item in the game as you can just spam them like Diablo 1. The skilltrees are decent, on par with something like diablo 2. The combat is mediocre to bad for an action game but better than an RPG like Skyrim. The main storyline is about 12 hours long and "literally" 70% of the time you will be walking from one point to another like a really bad mmo, 20% of the time you will sit in inconsequential conversations and 10% fighting. The final boss was terribly boring/uninspiring/unchallenging and the entirety of the game was not challenging except at one point my main quest enemies became red (as opposed to neutral level enemies that are yellow, just like any mmo) and they were mostly unkillable. I went back to the surface leveled twice off yellow monsters (the 'open world' monsters scale to your level) came back and walked through the rest of the game without even trying.
Verdict:
Theres a lot of game here.. You could put 200 hours into fetch and kill quests if you wanted to and you can respec your skills as much as you want. If you (like me) have a history of playing mmos and you have no desire to grind out fetch quests ever again for the rest of your life just avoid this less than mediocre ftp-single player-mmo action game. If you have never played an mmo, or you love fetch and kill quests this game is ripe with them for many many hours.

If you don't mind the unhealthy obsession with virtual characters' lives and the inevitable God complex, then you should definitely buy this. I've played 125 hours in five weeks and I'm still not sick of it.

This game is ridiculously huge to begin with, but for some strange reason it doesn't seem to have enough of the essential content to create a good story with the sims. I mean, in some ways it's a lot like Sims 2 (which I have loved for so many years), but in other ways, its frustratingly different. For example, in Sims 2, I felt satisfied with the game that I bought -- even though I hadn't bought any expansion packs yet. The game was able to stand on its own and impress me without having any extra content. With Sims 3, I feel this horrible dissatisfaction with the content, dispite the superior graphics and the exciting new *live* neighborhood. Oftentimes I can ignore the feeling, but some times it is dishearteningly glaring.
There is always this subconsious push to run back to steam and grab up more DLC so that the game can achieve some kind of tolerable level of "rightness" -- almost as though EA was trying to do this on purpose. It seems awful, but I am starting to believe that they just broke the game up into pieces, called it DLC, and tried to sell it to people piecemeal!
An additional problem, and a rather gamebreaking one for me, is the sheer size of this game. Once you build it up to a reasonable level with "Pets" "Ambitions" and "Nightlife", things start to go seriously wrong. Bugs and glitches that once were just annoyances become major problems, lag that was pretty tolerable before is now making you mad, and loading times that were originally only a lengthy 5 minutes are now running into the range of 20 minutes -- and this is on the lowest settings possible! I have also begun to experience issues with the game essentially *growing* the more I play it. It automatically starts to get fatter and more sluggish every time. Not to mention the crazy amount of inconvienient game crashes!
All in all, I suppose coming so late to the game, I should have heeded the bad reviews and steered clear of it, but as you all know, sometimes, in pursuit of a dream, a gamer is tempted to try something that they know probably sucks.
I would only recommend this game to someone with a ton of patience and a 5 star computer system :P

Here's a game nothing short of amazing. Here's why:
The story:
It's a heartbreaking story about family, loss, caring about one another and overcoming impossible odds.
Environment:
Imagine the tales of Brothers Grimm, what the environment there must have looked like. Lots of wilderness, a sort of celtic society with dangers and monsters lurking around the next corner. That's what Brothers has to offer. A huge parise for the designer, the environment is overflowing with fantastic details which do not go unnoticed, a masterpiece.
Soundscape:
The music in the game is an unseparable part of the experience, one of the best adaptations of visual and sound that I recall. Besides that, the sounds of the game carry as little information as possible. They've actually come up with this interesting idea of letting the characters speak a made up language. Still, you do understand everything what they say, because the body language and the situations are so obvious. Huge credit for having pulled this off.
Gameplay:
Now here's a truly original element: you have to control two characters at a time. The jumping, climbing, running, all of it is just way more eerie and challenges your brain. The developers lend you a hand here by making the path itself quite linear + you can't fall off cliffs. I just hope future developers have the stomache to incorporate that idea as well because it's a kickass. If you're a seasoned player the puzzles in the game won't be a challenge, I'd be up for something even harder but the overall experience hugely make up for it.
Final word:
It's a true gem, a final product completed in every aspect imaginable. Such a big thanks for the developers, the world is a much richer place with this game.

Paperbound
Smash-up brawler
Dissident Logic
Dissident Logic
Paperbound is a four-player smash-up brawler developed and published by Dissident Logic.
The game has a really polished 2D comic book style. Each character has different skins, and the guest stars look like they were taken straight out of their respective game. There are five books, each one based on a different classic novel: A Journey to the Center of the Earth, Skull Kingdom, A Book of Five Rings, The Book of the Dead and Dante's Inferno. While most of them are well realised, there are a few levels that are too small for four players to fight in.
If you have any real friend, siblings, cousins or pets with whom you get along with, than Paperbound is for you. This is a
game with up to four players, and for those lonely you can play with up to three bots, which are really challenging. There are a total of 17 characters, including Captain Viridian from VVVVVV, the Goblin King from Tumblestone, Jonview the Protector from Cards and Castle, Juan from Guacamelee!, and the Locksmith and the Gentleman from Monaco. Unfortunately, all the characters play and feel the same, with the only difference being their attack animations.
This game is a one-hit kill brawler, and there are three ways to kill your enemy: by meleeing him, by throwing scissors or by launching an ink bomb. However, the selling point of this game is the possibility to invert gravity: this is a total game changer, making each round really fast paced.
There are two types of game mode: Free for All and Teams. In Free for All, you can play
, in which the first one to reach a certain amount of frags must escape from a page tear to win,
, in which the last player with any lives remaining wins, and
, in which the first player who gets a frag becomes the king and must try to survive, while fragging the king makes you become the king. In Teams, there is also
, a small variation of Capture the Flag. They are all a lot of fun to play with friends and family, especially the ones in Free for All. You can also change some options before starting a match, like Number of Bots, Number of Scissors and so on.
The controls are really responsive and intuitive with a controller, while the keyboard controls are really awkward, so be sure that everyone is using controllers for the best experience possible.
As already mentioned before, changing gravity makes the game more intense than ever, with characters and scissors flying all over the place. In case you don't have someone to play with, there are bots that make the game really challenging, especially in Free for All, and they are quite possibly the best AI I have seen in a brawler in quite some time.
Even though each stage has a different musical theme, most of them are quite forgettable. The only track I really like is the Main Theme, which reminds me quite a lot of Magicka. The sound effects are nothing spectacular and worth mentioning.
You will replay this game with your friends over and over. Unfortunately, there are no unlockables excluding the book of Dante's Inferno.
Overall, this is a fast-paced brawler that brings enough new ideas to the table to feel fresh. I highly recommend this to those with many friends and to fans of smash-up brawlers. If you don't enter in any of these categories, than you won't enjoy this game.

This First Impressions was done with a key obtained from the Developer.
Paperbound is for those who want a skill based party based battler, and are ok with it focusing on skill based combat rather then anything else.  Think final destination, no items from Super Smash Brothers. And while it's got a couple of twists to it, the game's variety will take a hit over time for people who really want powerups/change ups. The game is technically sound, that's for sure, and it can be fun with a bunch of friends. But for others, it's not going to hold up for them due to the lack of variety. It's hard to completely recommend over games like Towerfall: Ascension or Grand Class Melee 2 for my personal tastes, but the base combat is solid. It's not for me specifically, but
+:
-Technically Sound
-Options regarding settings for matches, to customize how you want it. The options really make sense given the game mechanics.
-Great for chaotic play, but without it being unfair.
-Controls are solid.
-Good variety of maps.
-Solid gameplay choices with survival, king mode, etc.
-:
- Twist with escaping through a page tear can lead to 3 on 1 situations that needs to be changed up, as it can extend matches for no good reason.
-No rebindable controller controls.
-Some combinations of characters and maps don't work because of blending in with maps.
-Some maps don't work personally, due to a too drawn back camera, despite it being designed (game level wise) well.
-It's sad that another game like this doesn't have online capabilities, but on the flip side they don't advertise as such.

Mount & Blade: Warband, is a game of many flaws, however I keep finding myself drawn to it and ending up sinking countless hours and spending sleepless nights playing it.
Mount & Blade : Warband is the sequel/expansion to sandbox RPG Mount & Blade. Mount & Blade is different to most RPG's as it is not tied down by a narritive or a story, instead giving the player an open sandbox to carve through and make a name for themselves in. Players start off with rags for apparel, rusty and bent weapons, a sickly horse, and a small amount of food, and are sent into the world. From there players start making their first choices, do I want to recruit some volunteers from a nearby village? Or do I want to do some quests for the local lord, to win his favor. Or do I want to enlist into the service of a general as a common foot soldier, to make some coin and a name for myself?. Whatever players do, is up to them, the game really does give an open feeling upon first impressions, a feeling which most games sparcely have. This is also where one of the games first flaws starts to rear its head.
Since the player starts off in an open world with many things to do, there are also many challenges in the way. Bandits have most likely taken down most beginning players within their first few minutes, causing frustration. The game's combat system is supposed to reward skill and timing, with players swinging in mutiple directions and timing their blocks, however to most players this system will feel clunky and unintuitive, and in those first few skirmishes, players will most likely feel angry and dissapointed. Now I am used to the combat system, however sometimes even I start to feel frustrated by the clunky animations and attacks.
By now players are now used to the difficulty of the game, and are starting to learn the ins and outs of the combat. This is when the game really starts to shine. Throughout the course of the game, players will be amassing a small army of peasants and mercenaries who serve loyally. Going to battle and seeing your army that you worked so hard for clash with the enemy is a enjoyable experience, and is made all the better when you exit the battle with minimal casualties. The game really gives you the sense of being a leader in a battle, ordering your troops right on the front, and charging in with them.
It is at this point when players start to align themselves with one of the six factions of Calradia, the fictional land where the game takes place. Each faction has a unique theme to them, and are each based on multiple medieval era kingdoms and countries that actually existed. Each faction is ruled by their respective leader, and has mutiple vassals that govern different towns and field their own armies. Players have to earn trust with the faction of their choosing to eventully become a vassal under them, eventully reaching the rank of Marshall, which gives them most control over the faction. Factions will constantly declare war with eachother, form alliances, or just stay neutral, with gives the feeling of a persistent world. However there is another option for more rebellious player...
One new feature Warband adds is the ability to create your own kingdom, that you manage and rule. First starting out as nothing more than a name under a banner, players can grow their kingdom to rival that of the strongest factions in the world. Players will be able to make their companions vassels under them, who begin to create their own armies and lead their own battles, and have vassals from other kingdoms defect to yours. Starting a kingdom however is no easy task, as player run the risk of going to war with the major players of Calradia. Kingdom management leaves a lot to be desired, however it is enough to give a sense of reward and gratification to the player, seeing their kingdom grow and their vassals  grow stronger.
This leaves me to one final point, mod support. When players have had their fill of the base game, they can dip their toes into the ocean of player created content for the game. Whether it be small fixes and tweaks to the game, or a complete overhaul, chances are there is something for everyone, and with the addition of steam workshop support, downloading these mods is as easy as clicking a button.
Now I haven't even gotten into the DLC nor the multiplayer, I will prefer to make those in a later date.
Even though Mount & Blade : Warband suffers from poor graphics, and clunky controls and systems, it is still a very enjoyable game and a fantastic RPG.

This arcade style fighting game has good graphics, runs well, and has a solid soundtrack. As for it being a fighter, it is fair, well balanced, every character feels different, and to top it off, the game's skill FLOOR is low with a VERY high skill cieling to the game.
As of a few months after release (and current as of October 2k17), the online ranking system is BAD.
1v1 games are arguably the easiest online competitive games to make matchmaking systems for, and Namco have failed in Tekken 7. The system shows you your next canidate to fight, which is a nice plus feature. The game also lets you accept or deny matches with players and shows their connection strength before you decide; the game will also indicate if a player has previously "unplugged" or disconnected in a ranked match before.
Also, the games ranking system could be done way better. The game doesn't give you better/worse opponents based on your rank falling or increasing. That is sad for a 1v1 game.
Most games throw you weaker opponents, or opponents your own rank if you are losing. The opposite is usually applied when you go on win streaks as well.
This game also gives you zero reward for beating opponents ranked higher than yourself (it actually penalizes you for breating someone higher ranked) AND to make that even worse, the game forces you to rank up/rank down faster when you fight opponents of the SAME rank.
Let me repeat that; if you are rank X fighting against rank X, you leave your rank faster, win or lose. If you are rank X and fight someone ranked X+2, you are penalized for beating that person.
To summarize this confusing section, you rank up AND down too fast in this game and it happens in an poorly planned manner, punishing you for beating better players, not adapting to your win/loss streak, and shooting you out of your rank when matched against players the same rank.
Tekken 7 is a GREAT game. It feels good to play, it's fun, the music is good, and the game is well optimized on both consoles AND on this Steam version. The netcode is pretty good for a fighting game too, it just is player dependent of course. The Steam version is pretty damn good and it runs so fast on good hard drives.
The only place this game FAILS, is in the matchmaking department. I HIGHLY recommend you find local players to play this game with if you want the full experience, because online leaves way too much to be desired for how well crafted this game is.
The game also lacks a perfect training room. That being said, there is lots of info in there, lots of things to learn, and plenty of features to accomplish what you need in the training room, you can't emulate (very few) certain very specific scenarios. To be fair, I have never seen or even heard of a "perfect training room" in any fighting game, and Killer Instinct has a great training room.
In my eyes, Tekken 7 is proof that perfect things don't exist. If the online system was a 10/10 and the game had the unicorn known as a "perfect training room", then Tekken 7 could be perfect. Alas, perfection is nigh impossible to find, and Tekken 7 is a seemingly perfect arcade fighter, with a poor matchmaking system and a good, but not great training room.

The music chosen for this game was perfect. Every single track is excellent. Pure hits! The soundtrack alone is worth what I paid for this game. At least for the 70s era part. The 00s era's music they chose is 95% garbage, but it does make it funny sometimes. New York has been created and rendered exceptionally well. The streets, the alleys, the cars, and all other parts of the environment are nicely done. The day and night cycles also look very nice. The cinematics are also done in a film-like fashion, that involves the player from the very beginning. All characters portrayed are quite interesting, and their voice acting is outstanding. Driver: Parallel Lines has the perfect mood, atmosphere, setting, sounds, and interactions to make you feel like you are truly in the game. Controlling any of the vehicles can be close to impossible without crashing them and eventually making them a complete loss. You will lose control of the vehicles easily. This makes the idea of spending money to upgrade cars you own almost completely wasteful and pointless. The game is extremely difficult. I've had to do missions many, many, many times over until I was successful. The untameable vehicle controls are to blame, in conjunction with the sometimes necessary simultaneous shooting. Repeating many of the missions over, and over, and over gets frustrating, repetitive, and extremely annoying. Often, it is infuriating how unforgiving the game is, with its control and handling issues. The speedometer keeps track of the total amount of miles you have traveled in-game, which is not useful, but pretty cool. Mouse sensitivity in the menus is horrible. Making changes in the settings will do little to make the menus useable by your mouse. Expect to choose menu options with the keyboard. The save system is based on completed missions. So, if you quit during the second part of a five parts mission, for example, you will be forced to start the mission from the very beginning next time you load the game, which is ridiculous. All vehicles take visible damage as you drive around the city like a complete lunatic, with very little care for public safety or your own. The chases and crashes are intense and look straight out of a Hollywood movie. The missions are diverse, challenging, exciting, and agitated even though this is primarily a driving game. Investing money into your owned vehicles and altering them is not forced upon the player, with the exception of one mission. Certainly, if you do buy upgrades, your driving will be temporarily made easier and better, but this is totally optional. Especially because money is hard to come by, and the upgrades or parts are expensive. Spend your money on ammunition instead. Several missions involve precision vehicular platform gaming. This means that you will have to slowly and carefully steer your car on ramps and other on ground structures. There are often hilarious AI controlled accidents that occur throughout the game. Because the missions are so difficult to complete successfully, you will develop hate for your enemies and the police. When you finally defeat them, you will rejoice in glory and relief. If you have much patience, and can forgive the game's excessive difficulty and problematic controls and handling, this is a great game. You will experience excitement, variety, and lots of fun. After the campaign is beaten, several vehicles are unlocked and put into your garage. You are also free to roam New York in both eras and do the money making side missions.

Don't buy this game if you plan to play this game online. I've played my fair share of fighting games (Blazblue, SF4, DoA4, SFxT, Tekken, classics on fightcade/GGPO) and this game has by far the worst online I've ever seen. The matchmaking is absolutely horrbile, because all you get is a "green bar".  I'm using quotation marks because the game is apparently as tolerant as it gets when it comes to these bars. Most green bar machtes play like underwater, 1.5-2 seconds of delay isn't uncommon, in fact it's completely normal.
1) There is no ping.
2) There isn't even a country flag, you wont know when you're up against some mud hut dweller who uses a water wheel for internet. This is complicated by the high threshold for "green bar connections" which makes them rather deceptive.
3) There is no benchmark rating like in USF, you wont know if you're matched against somebody with a potato pc or not, running the game below 60fps. Edit: We have a benchmark rating now, but it's semi worthless if you can't filter bad ratings out. The playerbase is very low due to a rough launch - think Arkham Knight bad. You can now decline those kinda players, but you will consistently get matched up with them, so you spend more time declining their sorry asses than playing the game.
Just to give you an example, the game matched me up with 20 different opponents, and a whopping 16/20 didn't pass the benchmark. I got 5 solid matches in 60 mins which is pathetic for a game barely 6 months old. 60 mins of online matchmaking in USF4 equals 25-35 matches.
Online just isn't fun and a total crap shoot. It takes ages to find matches and when you find them, there's still a decent chance that they wont be enjoyable. It's just not worth the hassle.
If you can get the game for cheap the offline content may be worth it, it certainly isn't worth the steam price, because fighting against the AI gets stale pretty quick. The story is about 6 hours depending on how well you do. You get your run of the mill single player modes like classic tower, survivor, endless etc. where you can grind koins to unlock new brutalities, fatalities, fan art and so on. The AI is also your typical fighting game AI, training dummy on lower difficulties, but reading your inputs on higher difficulties. You wont learn much fighting against the AI as is with most other fighting games.
The game isn't bad, it's probably a good entry game for beginners who are looking to get into fighting games. The execution barrier is quite low and the mechanics are rather simple, at least compared to most other fighting games like Blazblue, Guilty Gear (game mechanics) or even Street Fighter (option selects). But the online is balls, and that's where you put your training to a test (or not), so unless you're fortunate enough to have an offline scene... pass up on this.

The Story:
I found out about this game after doing some late night googling on Salvatore. 20 years ago I started reading his books and was amazed that I completely missed the fact that he worked on a game and it immediately went on my wishlist. The main story was okay, I don't really have any complaints but I didn't really feel any Salvatore coming through and I am unmoved. Anyone could have written/helped write the world and I wouldn't know any difference.
The Art:
Simultaneously I found out Todd Mccfarlane had some play in the art and I have an entire box of Spawn comics. My favorite childhood artist and writer together for one game, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ The color is great in the game but the lack of detail is mind boggling. Todd put so much detail into spawn comics and seeing character models without fingernails was just disgraceful. The graphics and animations are rather plain and nothing here is an artistic achievement. At one cutscene I recall a female soldier being shot in the back with an arrow and I think they tried to animate blood coming out of her mouth but it just looked like it was pouring out her face. Mediocrity is the theme for the art.
The Gameplay:
Through and through this is a single-player MMO action rpg. You could take any free to play mmo, remove the multiplayer and nothing about this game would outshine any of the uncountable amounts of games in the genre. Pretty much each zone has a town, each town has npcs with exclamation marks giving out fetch and kill quests. Each zone is linked together by a passage. There are basic tradeskills with the classic WoW style herb gathering, jewelcrafting , blacksmithing (except the last two you get regeants from chests and not nodes) and you don't need to invest in any of them although healing potions are the end all-most powerful item in the game as you can just spam them like Diablo 1. The skilltrees are decent, on par with something like diablo 2. The combat is mediocre to bad for an action game but better than an RPG like Skyrim. The main storyline is about 12 hours long and "literally" 70% of the time you will be walking from one point to another like a really bad mmo, 20% of the time you will sit in inconsequential conversations and 10% fighting. The final boss was terribly boring/uninspiring/unchallenging and the entirety of the game was not challenging except at one point my main quest enemies became red (as opposed to neutral level enemies that are yellow, just like any mmo) and they were mostly unkillable. I went back to the surface leveled twice off yellow monsters (the 'open world' monsters scale to your level) came back and walked through the rest of the game without even trying.
Verdict:
Theres a lot of game here.. You could put 200 hours into fetch and kill quests if you wanted to and you can respec your skills as much as you want. If you (like me) have a history of playing mmos and you have no desire to grind out fetch quests ever again for the rest of your life just avoid this less than mediocre ftp-single player-mmo action game. If you have never played an mmo, or you love fetch and kill quests this game is ripe with them for many many hours.

Really fun game! This is my first foray into the action-rpg/dungeon genre, and I love it.
+The art style is gorgeous, and they've done a great job of making so many armours and weapons not look fugly.
-When it gets really hectic it can be difficult to see what's going on through all the bright colours and effects.
+The New Game system is cool; you won't be near max level after you finish the story, so you can start NG+and do the areas over again, but with your character at a higher level and all the loot and mosters have been scaled appropriately
+Mapworks feature adds some good replayability. Adds many different dungeons with different stats (eg, monsters drop double gold, monsters immune to crits, double exp, double gold, etc)
+Having the pet is handy! It has its own inventory, and you can send it to town to sell or pick up certain items. You can also get gear to boost their health and damage, which is nice for ranged builds!
+Amazing amount of build versatility. Not limited by your class to any weapon or play style, so there's a tonne of fun to be had in making a ridiculous or strange build and rolling with it.
~ Not all builds are viable though, and sometimes you have to remake a character a couple hours in because you've built poorly. (Or, yay respec mods!)
-even with many play styles available, the overall gameplay can get repetitve after awhile.
+Multiplayer is a lot of fun. Definitely a game I prefer as a multiplayer game to single player. The difficulty scales according to how many party members are around and it's a lof of fun going crazy with your friends,
+The ability to switch your character very easily between single player, multiplayer (LAN) and multiplayer (online) is great, other games do do this but I've found Torchlight's simplicity is really helpful.
-It can be difficult connecting to online games some times, and lag does happen where your friend freezes on your screen but you can move, but vice versa on theirs. Makes for confusing runs sometimes.
This game is a tonne of fun. I picked it up on a suggestion from a friend when it was $5, and it's probably the most I've ever gotten out of five dollars. I'd not hesitate even for the full $20!

Though not completed in full, I do believe a lot of the critisism surrounding this game (mostly here on Steam) is somewhat out of proportion.
The game itself is not bad, it's not great either, but lets get to the bad things first; Documentation and tutorials are scarce and it took me a good while to figure out just the basics (and every result Google gives when looking for (GAME) Firefighters 2014 not being related to the game in any way sure didn't help either). Missions begin to get repetetive real fast and you spend most time driving around the world or walking around the station. Add to that items that you occasionally cannot return to storage (which results in you being unable to pick up a different item), terrible civilian driver AI (worse than GTA 1...YES 1) and reflection not functioning properly (brightness of mirrors and such is way too high, game settings changes have no effect) makes this a frustration from time to time.
But I can live with most of these problems, because the game looks really nice, even when everything is set to minimum levels. The introduction is one that makes you really feel like your a rookie firefighter just joining the force, and playing the tutorial first, you are shown around your workplace in a way that I can honestly say I haven't seen in any simulation game ever, and it was such that I'd imagine would go like in real life. The campaign basically is one big tutorial with a free mode unlocking afterwards (I'd imagine, not quite there yet), and things are simple but clearly explained as you need to perform certain actions. And last but not least, something that I really feel I need to mention here, is that the hoses do not actually roll out as you connect them to something and walk away; This is a good thing, because a lot of these simulators have tried to implement that and utterly failed seriously bugging the game. I'd rather lose that little optical detail and have a smooth game than fighting the hose during an emergency situation, and you are responding to emergencies (in most cases) after all...
I can honestly say that, despite most comments I've read online I can actually recommend this game, but with a fair warning;
It is a Firefighter simulator. It is at minimum levels running on a game engine that could have been written a decade ago. It is not a racing game, if you feel the vehicle slide away underneath you, release the gas pedal. Different countries put different priorities in the balance between speed (responsiveness) and utility (weight and ability) of the vehicles, so if you have played a similar game set in America for instance, don't expect the vehicles to handle the same, this is Germany (or virtually interpretation thereof), in case you're wondering.
A word for the developers:
In a future version, don't focus so much on visual quality, you clearly have that covered more than enough, and in my opinion, it is not nearly as important as the actual simulation elements, AI, physics, etc. I did not really get that team-spirit feeling when at a car crash with 5 firefighters around me and just me and 1 other guy actually doing something and the rest just standing around. You could, for instance, improve on the civilian traffic AI and give the traffic cones an actual function... Just some thoughts...

Horizon Shift is a surprisingly good shooter game which can be easily omitted due to its look - it is stylized for old arcade games and, in my opinion, looks pretty dull.
But when it comes to gameplay it is way more entertaining than it looks, though rules cannot be simpler - defend the line on which you stand and don't be hit by enemies. But the line has two sides, so you have to care about both of them.
Simple look and simple rules does not mean the Horizon Shift is easy. Actually it is difficult as heck. Sadly there is no way to change its difficulty for more suitable for non hardcore players.
There are several game modes, but all of them keep difficulty very high.
Music used in this production is not my type, though it is not bad, I think.
Summarizing, I was surprised about this game and I like it. However, due to its difficulty I can recommend it only to those with a lot of patience or master skills in 2D shooters.

It controls very well and it plays fair, though there are a couple minor puzzles with instant failures that don't have obvious solutions. Don't buy this game if you plan to play this game online. I've played my fair share of fighting games (Blazblue, SF4, DoA4, SFxT, Tekken, classics on fightcade/GGPO) and this game has by far the worst online I've ever seen. The matchmaking is absolutely horrbile, because all you get is a "green bar".  I'm using quotation marks because the game is apparently as tolerant as it gets when it comes to these bars. Most green bar machtes play like underwater, 1.5-2 seconds of delay isn't uncommon, in fact it's completely normal.
1) There is no ping.
2) There isn't even a country flag, you wont know when you're up against some mud hut dweller who uses a water wheel for internet. This is complicated by the high threshold for "green bar connections" which makes them rather deceptive.
3) There is no benchmark rating like in USF, you wont know if you're matched against somebody with a potato pc or not, running the game below 60fps. Edit: We have a benchmark rating now, but it's semi worthless if you can't filter bad ratings out. The playerbase is very low due to a rough launch - think Arkham Knight bad. You can now decline those kinda players, but you will consistently get matched up with them, so you spend more time declining their sorry asses than playing the game.
Just to give you an example, the game matched me up with 20 different opponents, and a whopping 16/20 didn't pass the benchmark. I got 5 solid matches in 60 mins which is pathetic for a game barely 6 months old. 60 mins of online matchmaking in USF4 equals 25-35 matches.
Online just isn't fun and a total crap shoot. It takes ages to find matches and when you find them, there's still a decent chance that they wont be enjoyable. It's just not worth the hassle.
If you can get the game for cheap the offline content may be worth it, it certainly isn't worth the steam price, because fighting against the AI gets stale pretty quick. The story is about 6 hours depending on how well you do. You get your run of the mill single player modes like classic tower, survivor, endless etc. where you can grind koins to unlock new brutalities, fatalities, fan art and so on. The AI is also your typical fighting game AI, training dummy on lower difficulties, but reading your inputs on higher difficulties. You wont learn much fighting against the AI as is with most other fighting games.
The game isn't bad, it's probably a good entry game for beginners who are looking to get into fighting games. The execution barrier is quite low and the mechanics are rather simple, at least compared to most other fighting games like Blazblue, Guilty Gear (game mechanics) or even Street Fighter (option selects). But the online is balls, and that's where you put your training to a test (or not), so unless you're fortunate enough to have an offline scene... pass up on this.

It's about time I left a review here, having quit the game as of probably over a year ago.
Rockstar and Take Two don't give a single♥♥♥♥♥♥about you as a customer. I know from firsthand experience. This latest thing about them not wanting people to mod the game with OpenIV is just icing on the cake. Their game and practices have been invalidating users' purchases since it was released on PC, and they aren't doing a thing to fix that.
My original issue was with their built-in anti-cheat. Instead of using a tried and true anti-cheat mechanism like VAC or PunkBuster or EAC, they decided they'd do better, and added something of their own to the game. Somehow, they screwed it up way, way worse than any of the other solutions out there. Surprising, huh?
Their anti-cheat not only doesn't ban uses who are quite obviously using cheats, but it also bans users who aren't doing anything wrong at all! That's what I paid $60 for! They took a brute-force console-style approach to anti-cheat. Anything that's running on your system that might even LOOK at the game's memory while running will get you flagged, and that includes: streaming software, chat overlays, FPS counters, virus scanners, hell even steam's own FPS counter was doing it at one point. The real kicker is they won't admit that their system makes any mistakes, let alone tell you what on your system is setting the anti-cheat off.
That point is hammered home when you try to contact support about the issue. Any and all tickets even mentioning the word "ban" in them are automatically closed with an automated response, and calling their support line and saying the same thing results in an aggressive script-reading and disconnected call. If you think I'm joking, just try it for yourself. This review will still be here for you to read, I'll wait.
Back already? Good, because there's just a bit more left. See, a large portion of the community is so blindly entranced by the game series that they assume Rockstar can do no wrong, and swear that anyone that has a problem is either a liar, an idiot, or both. I've been falsely banned TWICE from the game, and just about every response I've gotten when mentioning it has been "you cheated, you got what you deserved." Productive bunch, eh?
So let me just say that this latest anti-consumer move from the GTA giant comes as not even the slightest inkling of a surprise for me, someone who LOVED this game, someone who was waiting for its release, someone who doesn't have a ton of money and saved up for it, who feels completely cheated and betrayed. I won't be buying another Rockstar product again. I hope the company hits such dire times that they get dismantled and the property is sold off to someone who can do the customers justice. Lastly, I hope the people who are making these actively harmful decisions step on a lego, have it fly into their mouth and then choke on it.
By the way, you should all go into the tags for this product and report the one that says "Moddable". It doesn't apply anymore. Thanks for reading.

Possibly the best game I've ever played.
My play time on Steam probably tells the verdict (even though it's inflated by leaving the game paused on the background).
The game is a mix between a RPG and a grand strategy game, that leverages a sandbox where factions, kings and lords dynamically wage wars, make friends, forge alliances, etc.
You play one character and not a faction, so even if you're the king of a faction, you do things by actually traveling to places on the world map and speaking with people; in the same vein, in battles, you don't give orders on a top down view, you're actually in there, either moving to safe positions with a good view to order your units around, or actually leading a charge to the enemy's flank.
When the game starts you play as a lowly mercenary, and even though the way to achieve fame and fortune is very open-ended, generally speaking you'll go through these 3 phases:
1. You try to get by as a mercenary, fighting bandits, selling loot, trading between towns and recruiting peasants. Eventually you'll offer your services to some king which will make you a part of that faction.
2. Eventually, if you prove yourself worthy, you can ask your king to become a lord and own land, and from that point on you'll start owning settlements, improving them, collecting taxes, you may marry a daughter of some other lord, you will defend your land and your kingdom from its enemies.
3. At the end-game, if your power grows to rival your kingdom's, you may decide to declare independence; you'll employ vassals, giving them land and managing your relations with them, and you'll fight other factions for the recognition of your right to rule, until you eventually become recognized as another king, forging your own alliances and declaring your own wars.
This is one of the most replayable games I've ever played, probably due to the sandbox and the way the game changes depending on what stage you are. Also, you can choose very different playstyles, like a horse archer in one, or a knight in another, or even concentrate on having great leadership skills and little fighting aptitude. You can also decide to be a ruthless, cruel leader, or a honorable, good samaritan, which will determine which lords and companions will put up with you. Add to that some amazing mods that either expand or overhaul this fairly old game, and you'll probably end up going back to it every so often, like I do.
Couldn't recommend this more.

Solution to everyone complaining about Day 1 DLC: Don't ♥♥♥♥ing buy it. You can get by in the game without it...
As for performance issues, TURN OFF MSAA, SWITCH VOLUMETRIC LIGHTING/CONTACT HARDENING SHADOWS to either ON or OFF. ULTRA WILL KILL YOUR PERFORMANCE.
As for the game itself, I'm still in the process of completing it. Having completed DXHR multiple times and knowing of how the game is played, this feels right at home for me. It's different at first, especially when you get into using experimental augs, but it is very easy to get used to quickly. The only thing that bothers me is how Malik is canonically dead (EVEN THOUGH I SAVED HER!) but it's still not going to make this a bad game. Give it some time. It's very awkward at first but like I said it's something you get used to.

Mankind Divides is somewhat of a "human revolution 2.0". Almost every single aspect of the predecessor was improved, to varying degree. Gameplay is smooth as ever, augs are fun to use(with new additions complementing the old ones, not replacing), side quests don't leave you bored and the main plot is a web of conspiracy and doubt. With an obligatory plot twist at the end. Naturally, visuals are great too, lighting effects are outstanding and very natural. PC port by nixxes so no issues whatsoever.
Most importantly, the game is full of pleasant small details and little moments, again, like the previous game, but even better.
Now, to the cons. Mankind Divided is very rich with detail and character but somewhat lacks variety. Unlike to the previous game, the whole story here revolves around only once city. It was almost comical, when some major characters that traveled all over the globe before would very conveniently just decide to arrive at Prague, the Capital of the World. There's also only one boss in the entire game. The Final Boss. A bit of a letdown, and a step down from the previous game.
But overall, pros outweigh the cons here. This thing actually has a soul and definitely lived up to expectations. Very interesting, beautiful and fun game. Finished it in a single 27-hour sitting. I regret nothing and give it a solid recommendation.
And adressing the whole DLC "controvercy", it doesn't affect the game one bit. It doesn't matter. Yes, you can open the shop and buy stuff, but it's simply an option. It's not required. Infact, there is so much of this "stuff you can just buy" lying here and there in the game, by the end of it, you collect so much you might start selling it yourself.
First story DLC is alright, I guess. It's no Blood and Wine, but hey, few things are.

It's got to be hard to make a shooter that gets some attention these days. There's just such a huge glut of them that they need something really special to stand out from the crowd. Horizon Shift goes in a direction that I've certainly never seen before, mixing in platforming elements of all things to an otherwise Geometry Wars-y design. And while it still might not be hugely groundbreaking, it can keep you busy with some quality shooting.
Horizon Shift has you commanding a simple rocket-looking thing against waves of neon wireframe baddies. You're not flying up or right or all around to fight them, though. Your ship is glued to a horizontal line in the middle of the screen, the "horizon" previously mentioned. The ship slides along it left or right but can also flip to the top or bottom of it, useful when enemies come from both the top and bottom halves of the screen. If that sounds too restrictive you can also double-jump off the line to dodge particularly pesky attacks.
Enemies creep in from the edges of the screen in slow patterns before taking aim or dive-bombing you, giving you time to flip and slide into position. While most enemies attack you directly, others attach to your horizon or blow chunks out of it, and a few can kill you instantly by reaching the horizon. The ones that attach to or remove pieces of your horizon add a multiplier to your score, so if you want to live on the edge and let them draw near you can rack up extra points. It's pretty risky though, because waves get pretty hectic pretty fast.
There are a few scant upgrades to grab during your battles, like faster movement and more powerful shots. Chaining kills also builds a meter that gives you a screen-clearing bomb when fully charged. Enemies get pretty creative, including scuttling space crabs and bounding space lobsters (not sure why stellar seafood is such a thing here). There are bosses as well that range from large to crazy huge and edge up towards bullet hell territory without really crossing over. Oh, and there's even a little Breakout-style bonus round between stretches of waves to change things up a bit.
Aside from the horizon mechanic, these elements form a pretty typical space shooter. The graphics are simple outlines for the most part, some empty and some with gradients, so nothing particularly attractive. The backgrounds are kinda neat and remind me of my Dance Dance Revolution days, with a soundtrack of thumping electronica to match. There's a whole mess of game modes and modifiers as well but that might be my one knock against the game, I never managed to unlock any and the game gives no indication of how you access them. Outside of that there's nothing wrong with Horizon Shift, just nothing that really stands out. If you want to shoot some stuff and attack some scores, you'll get that here along with a little twist to keep you going a bit longer.
