I think this was one of TellTale's first games, along with BTTF. As with that game, I will say that this is a very linear game, unlike their later attempts. If you're expecting the same choices and branches, you will be disappointed.
Tales of Monkey Island is... different from the older Monkey Island games, holding a very strange position in the franchise. This is, I suspect, the first game that wasn't made by LucasArts. Many of the people from the original games are involved, but there is a strangeness about the game that wasn't in the others.
The graphics aren't bad. If you've seen any other TellTale games, you'll know what they're like. The art direction is reminiscent of Curse of Monkey Island which is no bad thing. Voice acting is top-notch as always, with Alexandra Boyd, Earl Boen and Dominic Armato doing splendid work as Elaine, LeChuck and Guybrush. Music isn't bad, with some eerie voodoo music tied in with the usual Monkey Island themes.
Tales of Monkey Island, however, seems to rely very much on shock value, going to places where none of the previous games had gone to. The humour is still there, as are the quips and the fun puzzles. But it's darker, particularly the final episode, and while it did its job in shocking me when I first played the game, it's a bit jarring now that I know it's coming (and I'm in a position to compare it with Curse of Monkey Island).
Tales of Monkey Island is significantly better that the Remastered versions of the first two games (which I returned because of how uncanny valley I found the graphics), but not as good as Curse of Monkey Island. I'd rate it at about the same level as Escape from Monkey Island, which I rather enjoyed, but found a bit frustrating because of the inventory controls.
There's a pretty blatant sequel hook at the end, I wonder if anything will ever come of it. I have yet to see TellTale bring out a second season of any property.

I originally got this game back in one of the Humble Bundles a little while ago, but I never got around to playing it because I was preoccupied with other things. It's unfortunate, because Brutal Legend is actually a very entertaining game with a solid direction of humor mixed with a nostalgic blend of 80's metal and aesthetic.
The game plays like an open world action-adventure game, but instead of your usual assortment of weaponry, you use the brute power of a wicked axe and a plethora of magical metal licks that can help enhance your units or kill multiple enemies in the blink of an eye. Unfortunately, the game play is rather repetitive, with combos being anywhere from three to four hits and using approximately three comobs for the entire game, but that's the nature of the open-world genre, so this isn't anything out of the ordinary.
You might have noticed I said units up above in that last paragraph, that's because this game also implements an RTS-like game mode that gets played around with in the main campaign. You'll spend some time gathering resource nodes to create units and upgrade them accordingly, but the system isn't too complex. As a matter of fact, it's very basic and you could probably get away with just popping out two varying units on Brutal Difficulty.
Brutal Difficulty wasn't bad at all, there were a few parts that were mildly irritating, but it's a smooth sail in terms of game time, which for my playthrough was about 13-ish hours?
The game is relatively short, and the story itself feels rushed. It felt as though the devs wanted to include more somewhere when you hit about 80 percent-ish in to the story, but didn't know how. Whether or not this was intentional I'm not certain, but the game was brief. The ending itself is also disappointing, leaving a lot to be desired for; unfortunate considering that there will never be a Brutal Legend 2.
The soundtrack for this game is amazing, however. If you're a fan of older metal ranging anywhere from the 80's to mid 90's, this game hits the nail on the head with perfect precision. Cruising in a hot-rod painted car while dashing through hordes of enemies whilst listening to such bands as Judas Priest and Motorhead has never felt as satisfying until Brutal Legend showed up and exemplified it perfectly.
The game's about an 8 out of 10 from what I played. While Brutal Legend struggles to find a solid identity as an RTS or action-adventure game, it compensates and rises above all doubts with a legendary soundtrack and a great writing team. I'd highly recommend it if you got some time to kill. It's got a pretty good amount of humor and 80's cheese, but if you're expecting a complex fighting system or a heavy micro-managing RTS, Brutal Legend won't be your game.

I'm hopping on the Take Two "♥♥♥♥ you" wagon, but in a more different and detailed way. At the time of writing this I've played action packed, loading screen full, hacker full 700 hours. I got the game the same week it came out on PC. That being said, I think I have had a good experience on the changes, the negatives and positives that have evolved and died out during this period. To put it down simply these are the pros and cons:
Pros:
Amazing graphics
Loads of content
Big and diverse community.
Cons:
Loading screen
Drop out session
Modders
I'm no diehard GTA franchise fan, but I've played GTA:SA and I fell in love with the whole concept of running around in an open world and doing what you or your buddies desire ( SAMP comes into play here ). Because of previous successful games I decided to get GTA V as soon as it would come out for PC. If you are like me, a guy that likes to go through the story line without worrying about the collectables and side stories, the game will take you approximately 35 hours to complete. Which is fine, because I bought the game for the multiplayer, the heists, missions, races and free roam.
Pros:
For starters, this game is absolutely awesome to play. It has tons and tons of content and if you are creative you can expand upon the tools that are given and create even more content for you and for others. The game is optimized and graphically astonishing ( with graphical mods you can enhance the graphics making it  even more enjoyable ). If I managed to milk 750+ hours from online, a guy that has little to no creativity, imagine what a person with creativity can accomplish.
I'd like to mention and talk about the sheer number of diversity that the community has. By diversity I mean sheer number of crews. There's a crew for everyone. Whether you like racing, drifting or just chilling, there's a crew for almost everything.
Cons:
The two problems I experienced at the beginning were the loading screens that sometimes could last a good minute or two before loading you into online mode or crashing you back into single player and the occasional kick from an online session. It's not a game breaker, but sometimes these issues would get me quite annoyed, and by quite annoyed I mean uninstalling GTA V, because sometimes they were just too much. And I'm sure it wasn't coming from my end, because all the other multiplayer games I've played have ran silk smooth. I've done quite a bit of research in this problem and I found out that it has to do with their net code and how they manage the online lobbies. The thing is, Rockstar are letting players host the lobbies themselves whilst putting filters, such as spikes in the packet loss. To keep things smooth, they limit the packet loss so that people with even the smallest problems get kicked out. Because of this, the loading screens are 9 years long meanwhile in third party multiplayer applications like FiveM, connecting between player and the server happens 10x faster, because the servers are hosted separately from the game.
At the beginning of the PC GTA V lifespan the modders were not as prominent, they were there, but they weren't as many and a big pain in the♥♥♥♥♥as they are now.
The game breaking problem for me are the modders in this game. They started getting annoying about three months into the lifespan of GTA V PC. Money started dropping and people slowly didn't even bother to play heists or missions that give money, because, why should they? They can just enter a lobby, cry for money, and the next thing you see is money bags dropping everywhere. If I would compare this problem to an irl thing I'd look at it as a growing tumour, because it had this snowballing effect that creates even more problems, the longer you let it grow. With every month, the game lost a bit of its richness and beauty it had. The few months into the game you could see people exploring, grinding heists and creating content via the content creator tool. Now almost everyone has the top 3 fastest cars, best skyscraper and garages full with random cars. Granted you could get all that stuff by now, but it leaves me confused, when lvl 20 has all this plus more.
Now the so-called tumour has gotten big and cutting it off is not going to help at this current time period, because of the mentioned things above.  This could've been prevented if Take Two or Rockstar acted much ♥♥♥♥ing faster instead of patching the game with useless patches that would later get exploited again. It's not only Rockstar to blame, it's also the creators at Youtube, the creators that spam videos that include ways to further exploit the game, instead of enjoying it. Most of the channels don't understand the consequences, the consequences in promoting something that could potentially ruin the game for others. All they see is money from those Youtube views.
TL; DR
The game had a huge potential but due to things like modders the possibilities are slowly dying out. At the very start of GTA V PC the pros outweighed the cons by A MILE, but now it's getting worse and worse with every coming month. If I was writing this game a year ago I'd recommend it, but now it just feels like it's lived its life and just gasping for the final days. I do think Open IV removal was not the correct option, not because of the single player mods or whatever, but because it could potentially put end to modders in online. Granted they should've done it much ♥♥♥♥ing faster, but I guess it's better to do it later than never.

Would like to start off by saying I have played both the original Deus Ex and Human Revolution. This game is getting negative reviews for FPS because people for some reason don't understand how to use graphical settings and expect a game with a very beautiful graphical design and a lot of moving parts to run at 60+ FPS on ultra everything with a GTX 970(or worse) or with 4GB of RAM. I also have to just point out all these negative reviews for the in game shop IT IS 10000000000% OPTIONAL! I just don't get the frustration. I haven't bought a single in game item with $$ and my experience is perfectly fine. In fact I have so much spare crap from just running around searching every corner I just sell it to NPC's and buy gun parts. Now onto the game itself. If you enjoyed Human Revolution then I promise you will love this one. It's bigger, prettier, smarter, smoother, and just all around better in every aspect IMO. They removed the horrible forced boss battles(yay). The map area is much larger. The map seems to have way better flow to it(vents don't seem ridiculously placed and in every corner in this one. The stealthing feels great but I will say it feels much more difficult to pull off some of the stealth stuff which I am enjoying. The gunplay is much much much better this time around and it doesn't feel like a ridiculous struggle to fight back(provided you have guns and ammo) if you fail the stealth in this one. They offer a tremendous amount of tools and gadgets/guns to help with both loud and stealth. The NPC's will actually ask you a different question depending on if you went somewhere or talked to someone that involves the quest line before talking to them. I am floored by how smart this game truly is.
I have not even come close to finishing this game but what I have played and experienced puts this game in a great place. It shines in a gaming industry that is now all about minimal effort with game design and more about reskinning everything and throwing it back out there for $60. Best $60 I have spent this year.

Deus Ex Mankind Divided is the direct sequel to Human Revolution, which was a game I enjoyed a lot. Mankind Divided continues with roughly the same design, but with a mostly nicer engine and some new augmentations to play around with. There's more creeping around and collecting stuff to do (in other words, robbing people blind) and loads of alternate routes and side missions to explore. I personally find the story and the acting a bit weak, but it's not so bad as to be offputting. The menus are a litle clunky and I actually had to google what I was supposed to do to disable augments. I was just expecting better, I suppose.
At release the game was buggy, plagued with performance problems and crashes and to add insult to injury, came with one time use DLC tied to your save game and microtransactions. Real classy that. Patch three seems to have fixed my main problems. As I wrote in the original review, performance is actually good on my system with high settings plus a few extra features enabled. A few bugs still annoy, but I haven't encountered any game breaking problems.
The microtransactions and the companion app can be ignored (which I think you should). The one time use DLC however makes me very suspicious of what the publisher has planned for the season pass. I cannot recommend buying that pass until we known what it includes, and how much of it you actually get to keep.
As the game is now, I can finally recommend it. The release wasn't perfect, but at least the patches came within days.

This is my edited review now that the game has had some time to age. I have changed my review from Recommended "Yes" to Recommended "No"
My reason for this was because of a number of things I was blinded by and have remained in game since my initial beta review. It is obviouse that there are a number of classes within this game that are Over Powered and have remained as such. They have increased the character roster from four to six but compared to the original gunZ it feels constrictive. Game modes have increased plus one adding in gladiator mode from the original gunZ which is a nice feature to see. But this game is pay to win...That alone should make any person walk away from this title. All worthy items must be rolled for with a small percentage of gaining an epic item. To roll for these items one must grind through levels and unlocks to obtain the proper amount of material to roll. Once one does so you can see if you get the item and if not grind through another hand full of hours and try, try, try again. Or throw money at the game and get as many rolls as you want for that perfect little item...
I hate to say these horrible things about this game because it does come off as fun but it is A problem when the majority of matches you one faces the same 2 characters over and over again because they are just so damn easy to get kills with. Of course as most games go one will see a few good players running other characters and owning the field with them. But in this caase that is a rare sight indeed. The newer characters seem to simply add in a weaker bunch to show case how OP the older characters are. Hell I can say that the new character. "Wayne" Has a primary weapon that shoots just a little bit faster thn the sniper rifle, does less damage, and has no zoom, His secondary carrys the lease bit of ammunition, horrible fire rate, medium ammount of damage, and extremely poor accuracym his melee weapon unlike every other characters cannot do combo attacks and do not stun enemies as long or throws them to the ground. The good thing about this character...Hes a cowboy, that is all.
There is a lot less tactics in this game compared to the first gunZ thanks to wall running and extreme mid air dash all one has to do is constantly dash around with their OP character and hope to land a melee combo, which really is not that hard to do with most characters. Which is just great since if you do not block in time there is no way to parry an enemy in mid combo simply sit back while mashing buttons in hopes to do something to repel the enemy. But all one can do while in the mists of an enemy combo is fall to the ground. Now the game does have a counter system while down but it rarely ever works! Most of the time the counter system is simply pressing the LMB which should be the easiest thing in the world except one can mash that LMB all they want and if the game wants to it will allow you to counter. That has only happened for me once in all my play time with all characters I have played.
When it comes to the limited modes it is nice to see that there are a decent amount of maps the only problem with that is the fact that most of the time you will be put on the exact same map over and over due to high community voting. It will quickly get gold fast as you simply try to play just one other map. But even if you roll a different map there is player hosting involved. That is right player hosting one of the worse things to ever happen to online gaming! If you are not close to the host you are going to have a bad time. Pings will steadily stay at over 200 all through the match and the host himself will have a jolly good time racking up the kills as one struggles to do any and all to try to survive. I had fun with this game but not enough fun to get me to continue playing for more thn a hand full of matches running in to the same problems over and over again. I say go play the first GunZ if possible and steer clear from this pay to win mess of an unbalanced connection difficulty game.

Featuring pretty landscapes and simple, relaxed gameplay, "Brothers" is a game you should check out. You'll walk, climb, and jump through the wilderness using only 25% of the buttons on your Xbox360 controller (plus the two joysticks). A couple of complaints: the gameplay is somewhat overly simplistic and repetitive, but the fact that you're advancing into completely different surroundings helps keep it fresh as you go along. There's also not a ton of exploring to do, just keep moving in a linear straightforward direction that the game points you towards. In this sense, it's almost the 3D version of a side-scroller.
UPDATE: I just finished the game, one day after writing my initial review. I had read some negative things about the final chapter of the game, but I didn't mind it at all.
Here's my advice: view this game as a night at the movies. The game reminds me of a movie (specifically a certain Peter Jackson trilogy) and it's like you are controlling a part of a bigger story in a beautiful atmosphere- so it's like you're becoming part of the movie while you're playing the game.

I wasn't here for the bad start to Mortal Kombat X, so that's not going to be a part of this review.
This game is very addicting, especially when you're trying hard to master combos, beat the AI on Very Hard, beat really good players. The key to this game is technicality. The more you know about your character and your opponent, the better set you are.
Varying your moves and never being predictable are key factors to a good offense. To have a strong defense, look into you opponent's moveset, try to perceive any potential blind spots.
To counter, use the moves that can bypass your opponent. It takes practice to notice these things though.
If you're new to Mortal Kombat X, I would recommend that you don't play PVP unless you're able to beat Very Hard difficulty with you desired characters. That way you don't humiliate yourself when you fight other players.
The only complain is that this game is not worth this much money. I got it on sale, thank goodness. Never buy for full price. Look for deals. I'm still looking for bargain prices for the Kombat Pack. Still, a very good game that keeps you playing.

Kind of a mixed bag.  I'll get into that more below, but first some tips.
Tips:
Right mouse button will skip dialogue.  It will also run when you're using the mouse to move.  In general, I found movement with wasd or the arrow keys better than the mouse movement.  Shift ill run when using these keys.  A lot of the time, I did everything with my right hand, including moving using arrow keys and shift and then using the mouse the interract.  Middle click will open the inventory.
It will help quite a bit to have played other adventure games, because adventure game logic is something that isn't always intuitive, and sort of has to be learned.  Every time you enter a new screen, make sure to find all of the interactable objects on every screen and at least use the basic interact with them. That should give you more information about the object, because you will probably need to come back to it at some point.   A lot of the time I was stuck happened because I missed an interactable item.    Pick up everything you can and also try combining items, when you're stuck.
Amost every time I got good and thoroughly stuck in the game, it was because I missed something.  In the first episode, I completed one action, and then had a limited amount of time to complete another, action.  I tried one action during that time, but it didn't work.  I tried other actions, but they did nothing.  In the end, what I needed to do was so simple, I just never thought of it.  The hint dialogue did vaguely hint at what I needed to do in this case, but it was too vague for me to comprehend until after the fact.  I often found the hint dialogue was too vague to be helpful when I was really stuck or didn't, or gave me a hint for an action I needed to take in the future but not the action/actions I needed to take before then.
In the second episode,  I noticed something during a cut scene, but then promptly forgot about it.
When I was stuck, I would end up spending a lot of time travelling so that I could try different things and the travel time was frustrating and time consuming.  I kind of wish there had been a map so I could just skip to the area I wanted to go.  Particularly frustrating were a few areas where I had a limited amount of time to do an action.
I was able to make it through episode three without too much issues.  I really enjoyed Murray.  This was probably my favorite episode for Murray alone.  Additionally,  there was very little walking I needed to do, since everything was relatively close together.

When I say "great platformer," what comes to mind? For me, I would think of Donkey Kong Country, Super Mario Bros. and maybe Super Meat Boy. And what exactly do these great platformers have in common? Many things of course, but most importantly, tight controls. These games may be hair-pullingly difficult at times, but they're fair because not only have they actually been play-tested, but they allow the gamer to feel like the death was their fault. Does "Egg Returns Home" have tight controls? No. Does "Egg Returns Home" have fair deaths? No. This piece of garbage relies wholeheartedly on luck as the basic mechanic between failure and success, and that is the last thing any platformer (a game genre based on skill), should ever resort to. I'm no diehard GTA franchise fan, but I've played GTA:SA and I fell in love with the whole concept of running around in an open world and doing what you or your buddies desire ( SAMP comes into play here ). Because of previous successful games I decided to get GTA V as soon as it would come out for PC. If you are like me, a guy that likes to go through the story line without worrying about the collectables and side stories, the game will take you approximately 35 hours to complete. Which is fine, because I bought the game for the multiplayer, the heists, missions, races and free roam.
Pros:
For starters, this game is absolutely awesome to play. It has tons and tons of content and if you are creative you can expand upon the tools that are given and create even more content for you and for others. The game is optimized and graphically astonishing ( with graphical mods you can enhance the graphics making it  even more enjoyable ). If I managed to milk 750+ hours from online, a guy that has little to no creativity, imagine what a person with creativity can accomplish.
I'd like to mention and talk about the sheer number of diversity that the community has. By diversity I mean sheer number of crews. There's a crew for everyone. Whether you like racing, drifting or just chilling, there's a crew for almost everything.
Cons:
The two problems I experienced at the beginning were the loading screens that sometimes could last a good minute or two before loading you into online mode or crashing you back into single player and the occasional kick from an online session. It's not a game breaker, but sometimes these issues would get me quite annoyed, and by quite annoyed I mean uninstalling GTA V, because sometimes they were just too much. And I'm sure it wasn't coming from my end, because all the other multiplayer games I've played have ran silk smooth. I've done quite a bit of research in this problem and I found out that it has to do with their net code and how they manage the online lobbies. The thing is, Rockstar are letting players host the lobbies themselves whilst putting filters, such as spikes in the packet loss. To keep things smooth, they limit the packet loss so that people with even the smallest problems get kicked out. Because of this, the loading screens are 9 years long meanwhile in third party multiplayer applications like FiveM, connecting between player and the server happens 10x faster, because the servers are hosted separately from the game.
At the beginning of the PC GTA V lifespan the modders were not as prominent, they were there, but they weren't as many and a big pain in the♥♥♥♥♥as they are now.
The game breaking problem for me are the modders in this game. They started getting annoying about three months into the lifespan of GTA V PC. Money started dropping and people slowly didn't even bother to play heists or missions that give money, because, why should they? They can just enter a lobby, cry for money, and the next thing you see is money bags dropping everywhere. If I would compare this problem to an irl thing I'd look at it as a growing tumour, because it had this snowballing effect that creates even more problems, the longer you let it grow. With every month, the game lost a bit of its richness and beauty it had. The few months into the game you could see people exploring, grinding heists and creating content via the content creator tool. Now almost everyone has the top 3 fastest cars, best skyscraper and garages full with random cars. Granted you could get all that stuff by now, but it leaves me confused, when lvl 20 has all this plus more.
Now the so-called tumour has gotten big and cutting it off is not going to help at this current time period, because of the mentioned things above.  This could've been prevented if Take Two or Rockstar acted much ♥♥♥♥ing faster instead of patching the game with useless patches that would later get exploited again. It's not only Rockstar to blame, it's also the creators at Youtube, the creators that spam videos that include ways to further exploit the game, instead of enjoying it. Most of the channels don't understand the consequences, the consequences in promoting something that could potentially ruin the game for others. All they see is money from those Youtube views.
TL; DR
The game had a huge potential but due to things like modders the possibilities are slowly dying out. At the very start of GTA V PC the pros outweighed the cons by A MILE, but now it's getting worse and worse with every coming month. If I was writing this game a year ago I'd recommend it, but now it just feels like it's lived its life and just gasping for the final days. I do think Open IV removal was not the correct option, not because of the single player mods or whatever, but because it could potentially put end to modders in online. Granted they should've done it much ♥♥♥♥ing faster, but I guess it's better to do it later than never.

Deus Ex Mankind Divided is the direct sequel to Human Revolution, which was a game I enjoyed a lot. Mankind Divided continues with roughly the same design, but with a mostly nicer engine and some new augmentations to play around with. There's more creeping around and collecting stuff to do (in other words, robbing people blind) and loads of alternate routes and side missions to explore. I personally find the story and the acting a bit weak, but it's not so bad as to be offputting. The menus are a litle clunky and I actually had to google what I was supposed to do to disable augments. I was just expecting better, I suppose.
At release the game was buggy, plagued with performance problems and crashes and to add insult to injury, came with one time use DLC tied to your save game and microtransactions. Real classy that. Patch three seems to have fixed my main problems. As I wrote in the original review, performance is actually good on my system with high settings plus a few extra features enabled. A few bugs still annoy, but I haven't encountered any game breaking problems.
The microtransactions and the companion app can be ignored (which I think you should). The one time use DLC however makes me very suspicious of what the publisher has planned for the season pass. I cannot recommend buying that pass until we known what it includes, and how much of it you actually get to keep.
As the game is now, I can finally recommend it. The release wasn't perfect, but at least the patches came within days.
---
Original review: Even after the patch the game still crashes at the explosion in the Prague station scene. And as a bonus you have to play the end of the opening mission again to retry. Well done, Eidos and Squenix. I recommend you wait until this game gets properly patched. I don't recommended it at this point in time. (Yes, I comfortably meet the hardware requirements, and yes, I have the latest drivers, and otherwise the game runs smoothly.)
Original Edit1: Finally got past the Prague station cutscene after multiple tries. I so hate the sandstorm section now. Unfortunately it's still not smooth sailing. Patch 2 did something about the screen aspect ratio (I have a 16:10 screen, and before it was locked to 16:9), but introduced a new bug where the interface will constantly flicker between 16:9 and 19:10 layout making most menus unusable. Does this stuff even get tested? Waiting for patch 3. Still not recommended.

Put simply, Oceanhorn is an audio-visual feast with an emotionally driven, heartfelt narrative. While not groundbreaking in terms of originality, it succeeds at plunging you into a magical fantasy world and keeps you anchored there on account of its rich lore, thought-provoking puzzles, and sheer volume of environments that are ripe for exploration. Oceanhorn might be a love-letter to Zelda, but perhaps the question should not be whether it rises to Zelda's level, but rather, whether it is able to forge a path of its own that players will remember. In that regard, the answer is a resounding yes. If you are a fan of Zelda games and have been searching the oceans high and low for a similar experience, do yourself a favour and play this now. Oceanhorn: Monster of Uncharted Seas is as close to 3D platforming perfection as it gets.
Good things:
+ Gorgeous art
+ Excellent, clear onboarding
+ Breathtaking music
+ Touching narrative
+ Effortless, intuitive controls
+ Highliy Immersive
Bad things:
- Boss fight camera angles disorienting
- Final boss too easy

Oceanhorn is a nice mixture of Landstalker and Zelda.
There's some puzzles that depend on being observant, some that depend on the obfuscation of the isometric viewpoint and others which depend on your improving skills/items.
It's charming, solidly built and with an easy going pace which will suit older gamers looking for a bit of nostalgia, who are looking for something to take a couple of weekends of relaxed play time and for younger gamers who might not have played the aforementioned games and for whom this might be their first action adventure.
This isn't for hardcore gamers, expecting a big challenge or some incredible story or innovation.
It's just a simple, point A to point B, stab a few monsters and solve a puzzle or two inbetween, game. Not an insane platforming, button-mashing, bullet-hell test of nerve between bits of dialogue, game.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons will only appeal to people who want to watch a tragic story unfold. It's almost comical how many things go wrong. Every 'level' (if you will) revolves around a subject or person or object or whatever, and you can always predict how each one's going to end. I always had these moments where I bet myself how bad it's going to go, and in the end I was laughing about how over-the-top the tragedy is.
Normally, I would have started this review by talking about the Gameplay, but ... I mean, the game revolves around a single gimmick: You control two characters at the same time, each with each thumb stick. Sounds cool? Well, it kind of is, but it never feels all to satisfying to solve the puzzles, in my opinion. The challenges you face are forgettable because the designers obviously don't want to stop you from experiencing the 'deep' storyline.
Sorry, I am undermining the game so much, but I am really angry about this game, as dumb as that may sound. I just like to have fun, and I hate it when a game's sole purpose is to show me how terrible life can be, or something like that. If it had solid and memorable gameplay, I would have recommended it. The forgettable 3-4 hours of simple puzzle solving and comically tragic story just don't add up to an interesting experience to me.
All in all, it's basically what some would call 'Oscar-bait' in the movie industry.

My overwhelming feeling after finishing Amalur was that it was all the things I've enjoyed about MMOs (especially World of Warcraft) without any of the downsides.
Just like MMOs, Amalur has a vast 3D world for you to explore and do things in, all realized in a consistent art style that eschews the overly gritty visuals we often see in other games. It features a heavy focus on loot as a progression mechanic, just like many MMOs, and there's a strong attempt at building a cohesive lore, just like in WoW (at least in the early days). On the other hand, Amalur doesn't force you to play with others, doesn't put you at risk of being ganked, doesn't force you to think about an in-game economy, and is just generally more hassle-free than most MMOs. Unlike most MMOs, it also has a reasonably fun combat system, although the auto-targeting can be frustrating at times. So in many ways, Amalur feels like the game I wanted WoW to be.
It's not perfect, however. That fun combat I mentioned is marred by the surprisingly low number of skills your character can learn. I dual-specialized in two of the game's three skill trees (Finesse and Sorcery; I ignored Might), and by the end of the game, after hitting max level, I only had seven abilities in my ability bar, which can fit significantly more than that. Now, abilities often have secondary modes, and weapons have a variety of attack moves as well, but I still felt like the skill trees were very sparse, with most of my points improving current abilities rather than unlocking cool new things.
Inventory management continues to be terrible, just like almost every other RPG. So much crap piles up in my inventory - little bits of crap, too, like potions or garbage or books, and keeping a lean inventory is a constant chore. It doesn't help that the inventory has a gamepad optimized UI that feels horrible and slow as hell to use with a mouse.
The narrative is an interesting mixed bag. On the one hand, they clearly thought they were being different, and in some ways they are. There are a surprisingly big number of female characters playing roles that are not in lock-step with gender expectations. Even more interesting to me is how humans are basically an afterthought in this setting - the main conflict is essentially a war between elves and fae (humanoid nature fairies with Irish accents), and humans exist only on the sidelines as mercenaries, missionaries, and migrants. It's quite refreshing in that regard. There are even some really interesting themes surrounding freedom and fate that do a surprisingly good job at justifying the whole "Only the player character can do this!" schtick that most games play with.
On the other hand... we still have a pseudo-medieval world populated with humans, elves, gnomes, and fairies, throwing fireballs around and summoning demons. Amalur feels derivative in that sense, despite what other uniqueness it might bring to the table.
Overall, I would say Kingdoms of Amalur is a good RPG, but flawed enough not to be great. It scratched the WoW itch for me and was good enough to keep me playing through till the end, but there are a lot of areas in which it could have been improved upon. Sadly, we'll never see what an improved sequel might have looked like.

TL; DR: If you like fantasy RPG's this is a game you must play. solid 9/10.
Now i actually want to adress some things i like/dislike about the game,by the way i have about 100 hours in game, half of it was offline.
First of all, unlike in some reviews i saw, i will say professions are a big deal. My main has max blacksmithing and sagecrafting(gemcrafting) at max and my custom made armor and weapons are unmatched, i haven't found any weapon/armor pieces that is better than my gear yet. I like this, but there is a downside too, i have been running with same looking gear for more than half of the game. I mean, i craft new gear from time to time but in the end they look the same. Which is sad considering there are some great looking items in the game and i would like to wield them.
And potion crafting is almost necessary in early game because you can just get locked from 2-3 enemies simultaneously attacking you and you die after 2-3 hits in early game on hard. But when you get some good gear it's almost useless.
Also, there are TONS of things to do, sidequests and errands(quests you can do over and over again) you can do, achievements to hunt, different playstyles you can try (for affordable money you can reset your skills/stats anytime in game), tons of lore to read (or listen from lorestones), huge world to explore. I love this, but yet again it brings something rather unpleasant too, you can pretty much get overpowered in midgame if you like to do any kind of quest/errand you find, which i tend to do. This makes the game really easy even on hard, specially if you craft your own gear.
Artstyle of the game, i think, is fantastic. Voicework is too good (specially Alyn Shir). Enemies are mostly unique. World design is superb.
I think the thing that could put a lot of people down is the level design, and game design in general. What i mean by that is, you can't jump, you can only jump from certain jump points. This actually is a big deal when you think about it. lets say you are on something that is about 30cm above ground. You just can't jump off or walk off and go on, minor things like that. Game design is, lets say, "linear open world". Map is consisted off very clear and distinct areas, which are again divided by sub areas, if you take a look at the map you will see what i mean.
Story is cliche but somewhat original too. I'd say it's a fresh take on the whole chosen one saves the world thing. I don't want to spoil much but it's just good.
Solid controls and a good combat system, almost all spells/weapons have at least 2 styles of attack, if not more. Like longsword has a basic swing if you just tap, a dash if you long press, if you double tap and pause and attack again it lifts the enemy up in the air etc. there are lots of combos and since you can equip two weapons at time to switch between, you can get a lot of cool interactions. There is also reckoning mode which has really cool finisher moves. There is also stealth in the game which i can not comment on because i never felt the need to use it since my character is a tanky beast.
There is also a twists of fate system which i find really cool, let's say you finished a long questline,main or side, that means you will probably get a twist of fade card, which will boost some effects on your character permanently. And sometimes actions you take during the questline will change the card you will get, and also will effect your game (for example in warsworn questline you can end up making them hate you or praise you, so they will either attack you on sight or be your allies.)
There is room for a lot of customization since there is no distinct classes in game, you can choose to spend your skill points in three skill trees without limitations, kind of like warrior,rogue and mage skill trees. You can make a rogue/mage, a warrior/rogue or so on. When you put enough point in a skill tree, or a combo of skill trees, you unlock destiny cards which will have effects varying from +% attack damage to changing your dodge roll with a shor ranged teleport.
There are 9 weapon types(sceptre,staff,chakram,longsword,greatsword,hammer,dagger,faeblade,longbow), lots of unique weapons with cool effects and looks (for example i had a pair of daggers which did fire damage at day and ice damage at night called 'shine and shadow'). Lots of armor types (leather, trollhide, sylvanite etc.) and lots of accessories with cool effects.
I want to talk about the DLC too, Weapons&Armor bundle is almost completely useless, i mean, it does give you a head start but it will only last about an hour or so. Then you will start to find better gear. I just made a character in which i rush the main quest, no sides, no exploring just straight marching on the main quest line. Even tho it means i neglect main means of getting gear, in about 2.5-3 hours i replaced all the gear i got from the DLC.  So i will say pass on that. But Dead Kel and Naros are actually quite good. Both come with completely unique areas, enemies, lore, stories, characters and gear. Which i dig.
It's definetely a must play for Fantasy RPG fans.

To say I love the show RWBY would be an understatement. When I heard that an actual game based on the show was being made I of course freaked out like every other fan out there. After getting a gaming PC I could use to play the game, I immediately bought an Early-Access copy and jumped right into it.
So, after a couple of games, here is what I think of RWBY: Grimm Eclipse.
The Good: Right off the bat, this game is visually great. The environments are rich in color (minus Mountain Glen) and is very refreshing compared to brown and grey most AAA titles seem to stick with when it comes to levels. The character models also look like they came straight from the show itself and do each of the characters justice.
The controls are also solid. Minus a few odd button placements, such as the jumping into air dashs button combination, I found use of a keyboard and mouse with this game easy and not a struggle at all. Response time is also top notch, where my character attack with virtually no delay. Overall, for a PC gaming rookie such as me, this game is easy to pick up and to have fun with.
The bad: This game will get repetitive very quickly. New game modes and missions are needed if this game is going to have any longivity whatsoever. Killing Grimm is fun, but at the core, they're all about the same. This game needs variety either by new characters, enemies, or game modes ASAP.
The voice acting is... okay? Except for Blake (I'll give her a free pass since her voice actor hasn't recorded lines for this game), the cast still captures the characters well. My problem is that there isn't any banter between the four playable characters. To me, this is a missed opportunity. I want to hear dialogue between each character after clearing a wave of Grimm and interact with one another. The more dialogue there is, the more I can see people play just to hear it all.
Also of note are some small graphical glitches in the game. Mountain Glen has some trees that don't load the textures on their trunks and some frames cut out during combat. I haven't experienced any crashes yet, so that's good.
Overall, I'm very happy to see RWBY get a game. I hope to see more characters in this game soon, like team CFVY, as well as new Grimm not seen in the show. Now if you excuse me, I'm going to play some more games.
Thank you.

This game is a mindless hack and slash at the very core and nothing more. I suspect most will buy due to the show being awesome, but my advice is just watch the show because none of that is in the game.
It was fun to try, but I'm getting my Steam refund as I can see where the game is headed and it's in the wrong direction.

Sure they are there and you can waste your money on them but this isn't a pay to win game. It's mainly a single player experience. But with graphics set to low i sometimes see extreme slowdown in fps. Optimization is pretty good but sometimes running through the HUB city drops my framerate.
I enjoy the story, as i was playing it was definitely the driving force to me completeing areas. I wanted to see what happened next, see who would betray who and how much better (or worse) the world, and Prague, the hub city could get. Throughtout the game events that Jensen and other interpol agants undertake affect Prague and the surronding areas. Its cool to see Prague in varying scenes of catastrophe and hear news reports about the mission you were just on and how they have affected the world for better or worse. Their are a few twists and turns along the way mosty revovling around who the major bad guys are as they continually change as more information is being divulged and Jensen puts together the pieces. I like Adam jensen as a character, he's a bad♥♥♥♥♥super aug, his motivations are murky but thats becasue you as a player kind of get to decide. Is Jensen trying to save all lives equally? Is he only out for the Augs, or is it Just an Adam Jensen first world where he is only concerned with becoming a super powered aug god? The side quests are fun, it takes a little digging to find them but they are very engaging and change up the pacing of the game.
Gunplay is overall improved from Human revolution. Guns feel better. Might be some mouse acceleration but it hasnt bothered me so far in the few shootouts i have been in (most of that has been fixed with a patch). The new augments are nice, I haven't had a chance to try them all but im excited to experiment with some of the cooler ones. They have added a blink like dash that reminds me of the teleportation from dishonoured, and a titan shield that you can activate that makes you much tougher, reminiscent of Crysis. Their are a few other new abilities, a focus that slows down time, a few different weapons that Jensen can have to stun enemies integrated into his arms, as well as a nano blade launcher that fires...well the giant nanoblades Jensen has built into his wrists. The stealth elements are still awesome, i think the invisibility makes staying undetected too easy however. Stealth revolves around Hacking, knocking guards out, and dragging their bodies around, you can distract enemies with thrown itmes, and pretty much be the invisible, invicible master assassin that Jensen is. A more straight-forward approach is much more enjoyable this time around however with improved gunplay and better cover mechanics. The dialogue is interesting and well written. Jensen can still be a little over the top with his cheesy replies or ideals.  There are many paths that you can take to accmplish each objective. The levels are huge and varied, and the multitude of paths allow for different character builds. Hacking is still very much the same, a simplistic time based mini-game.
Overall i feel like Mankind divided is a very good sequel to the Deus Ex universe. The story is engaging, the combat and stealth systems are superb, customizing jensen's augments is fun and allows for varied play-styles. The game could be considered a little short but still took me 30+ hrs and will probably play again for NG+. The levels are huge and have a more vertical sprawl to them than Human revolution did. Eidos Montreal got rid of most of the boss fights but one complaint that i do have is that the one boss fight they still have in the game sucks, its terrible. Deus ex doesnt need bosses.

A decent port of an iOS game. To most this is a Zelda clone, however, it's missing something that Zelda is known for: the Boomerang. Other than that... well, there's bombs, bow and arrows, a fishing rod, magic spells, and so on. To compare this to Zelda, though, isn't fair. Zelda is a much better game, but this is still enjoyable.
The graphics are decent for a mobile game, and the controls are pretty good. I recommend playing with a gamepad. Puzzles are fairly easy though it's easy to get stuck sometimes as well. Thankfully there's a reset switch in almost every puzzle. I did get stuck at one point due to having used a key in the wrong place, so I had to reload my save entirely.
The game has crashed on me a few times, though I'm lucky I didn't lose a lot of progress due to the fact that there's checkpoints everywhere. Combat is fairly basic, there's blocking and attacking. I mentioned bombs, bow/arrows, and magic. Aiming kind of sucks with the latter two, and magic isn't used too often to really care about it. Boss battles are easy enough though some can be frustrating. Especially a certain one later in the game. The story is rather bland but pieces together nicely in the end. The music isn't anything to write home about, either.
I've played over 18 hours and I'm barely at 85% completion. The game features a quest to collect 55 bloodstones scattered throughout the world, up to 9 heart containers, 7 types of fish to catch, and 16 adventurer ranks to obtain. Too bad there isn't an achievement for getting 100%. But there is a sense of satisfaction in it, at least.
tl;dr A decent Zelda clone with many hours of gameplay. Best to get on sale.

A poor man's Zelda, by every stretch. From combat to flare, it doesn't just fall flat, but feels like a two dimensional biege mimic of an actual Zelda game's design. The items are unfun to use, the puzzles are nowhere near as fun as a zelda game, and unfortunately, there isn't really a redeeming factor outside its average monster design which, as it is just okay, can't really redeem things. Breaking things down for the game is hard, because each bland piece is connected to each other bland piece of the sub par jigsaw puzzle.
Combat itself is probably one of the first things you'll notice, as it somehow lack that magic zing that makes it fun. Throughout my relatively short time with the game, none of it really felt either interesting or fun. The sword doesn't feel long enough to feel like I'm a swordmen, and the monsters both take too many hits and are annoying due to the short range. This probably is linked to how crowded the game is. There doesn't feel like any breathing room for flair, an entire town feels like a single street corner instead of an actual town. Dungeons feel like small hallways, and the fighting room just isn't there. Item use, what I have gone through, just isn't creative enough to break the mold and give me something new to work with.
The worst part isn't really the gameplay, though it is linked to the cramping issue. The game just doesn't have any flavor. The first few shots of the island don't feel any different from each other due to the way the game is set up with its blocks, and there isn't enough small tidbits to make islands feel different. There isn't room outside of the small zelda clone box Oceanhorn has been crammed into.
It may have worked for a game on a mobile platform, but it doesn't work for a larger and more diverse game competition. If you want a zelda experience for your computer, all this game will do is remind you of everything zelda manages to get right. On the other hand, if you ever managed to convince yourself that what zelda does is easy and there's no thought to it, you should buy this game and realize everything zelda does right by seeing what oceanhorn does wrong.

I’m not going to say what happened in the story of this game. To borrow from another review that I read, Brothers – A Tale of Two Sons is a game best experience blind. The story is the driving factor so it’s best not to know it beforehand and experience it as it’s meant to be.
But without spoiling the story, I can still give you a few other reasons as to why you should play this game. The first I can think of relates to how the game looks. Basically, the game design is beautiful. The landscapes are gorgeous and there’s so much detail put in the background. As well as the story and art, the music is nice and the puzzles are good. They’re not too difficult and they don’t feel too repetitive.
Things to note about the game: it’s fairly short. You can play it in about 3-4 hours and because it’s story driven with simple puzzles, there’s not too much reason to replay the game multiple times. You need a controller to play the game as well as the game involves controlling both brothers at the same time. The left side of the controller controls the older brother and the right the younger brother. It feels awkward at first but you get used to it.
The most important thing to note about the game is that there’s no dialogue. Well, there is in that the characters speak a gibberish language, kind of like the Sims, but you get used to that as well. It actually adds a lot to the story, I think. Despite the lack of understandable spoken language, you always know what is going on by the tone of voice and character gestures.
Overall, Brothers – A Tale of Two Sons is a great game and I urge people to get it if they can. It’s €15 at full price is a bit steep for a game that’s so short and doesn’t have much replay value, so I suggest adding it to your wishlist and waiting for it to be on sale.

I have always really enjoyed dungeon-crawling RPG's (diablo and the like) and so I am also a very harsh critic of them. To that point, I HATED Torchlight 1, but I am actually a big fan of Torchlight 2. More so than Diablo 3 (pre-Reaper of souls) and more so than dungeon siege 3.
This game really did impress me though. The action is fast-paced and quite consistent as well. Gone is Torchlight 1's horrible scheme of 100 levels of same-dungeon-different-layout; now the game plays in more of an open world, where there are connected regions which have various side dungeons (and 'side-quests') within them. You can fill it all in and search for better drops or you can just move foward with the main questline if you like.
I am also quite fond of the skill and ability systems. It is very reminiscent of Diablo 2, more so than the third. You can select which character stats to increase, as well as which skills to level up. You don't really have a skill 'tree' as you are free to select them at your own whim. However, there are 'ranks' for each skill which give you a bonus trait or added effects once you hit certain levels with each ability.
All in all this game can be very addicting. The visuals and text can be a little too cartoon-y for my taste, but it is very easy to lose track of time while combing a new map or thrashing your way through a dungeon and it is fun to take the (short amount of) time to build your character. Plus there's multiplayer, so fun with a friend!

TL; DR: If you like fantasy RPG's this is a game you must play. solid 9/10.
Now i actually want to adress some things i like/dislike about the game,by the way i have about 100 hours in game, half of it was offline.
First of all, unlike in some reviews i saw, i will say professions are a big deal. My main has max blacksmithing and sagecrafting(gemcrafting) at max and my custom made armor and weapons are unmatched, i haven't found any weapon/armor pieces that is better than my gear yet. I like this, but there is a downside too, i have been running with same looking gear for more than half of the game. I mean, i craft new gear from time to time but in the end they look the same. Which is sad considering there are some great looking items in the game and i would like to wield them.
And potion crafting is almost necessary in early game because you can just get locked from 2-3 enemies simultaneously attacking you and you die after 2-3 hits in early game on hard. But when you get some good gear it's almost useless.
Also, there are TONS of things to do, sidequests and errands(quests you can do over and over again) you can do, achievements to hunt, different playstyles you can try (for affordable money you can reset your skills/stats anytime in game), tons of lore to read (or listen from lorestones), huge world to explore. I love this, but yet again it brings something rather unpleasant too, you can pretty much get overpowered in midgame if you like to do any kind of quest/errand you find, which i tend to do. This makes the game really easy even on hard, specially if you craft your own gear.
Artstyle of the game, i think, is fantastic. Voicework is too good (specially Alyn Shir). Enemies are mostly unique. World design is superb.
I think the thing that could put a lot of people down is the level design, and game design in general. What i mean by that is, you can't jump, you can only jump from certain jump points. This actually is a big deal when you think about it. lets say you are on something that is about 30cm above ground. You just can't jump off or walk off and go on, minor things like that. Game design is, lets say, "linear open world". Map is consisted off very clear and distinct areas, which are again divided by sub areas, if you take a look at the map you will see what i mean.
Story is cliche but somewhat original too. I'd say it's a fresh take on the whole chosen one saves the world thing. I don't want to spoil much but it's just good.
Solid controls and a good combat system, almost all spells/weapons have at least 2 styles of attack, if not more. Like longsword has a basic swing if you just tap, a dash if you long press, if you double tap and pause and attack again it lifts the enemy up in the air etc. there are lots of combos and since you can equip two weapons at time to switch between, you can get a lot of cool interactions. There is also reckoning mode which has really cool finisher moves. There is also stealth in the game which i can not comment on because i never felt the need to use it since my character is a tanky beast.
There is also a twists of fate system which i find really cool, let's say you finished a long questline,main or side, that means you will probably get a twist of fade card, which will boost some effects on your character permanently. And sometimes actions you take during the questline will change the card you will get, and also will effect your game (for example in warsworn questline you can end up making them hate you or praise you, so they will either attack you on sight or be your allies.)
There is room for a lot of customization since there is no distinct classes in game, you can choose to spend your skill points in three skill trees without limitations, kind of like warrior,rogue and mage skill trees. You can make a rogue/mage, a warrior/rogue or so on. When you put enough point in a skill tree, or a combo of skill trees, you unlock destiny cards which will have effects varying from +% attack damage to changing your dodge roll with a shor ranged teleport.
There are 9 weapon types(sceptre,staff,chakram,longsword,greatsword,hammer,dagger,faeblade,longbow), lots of unique weapons with cool effects and looks (for example i had a pair of daggers which did fire damage at day and ice damage at night called 'shine and shadow'). Lots of armor types (leather, trollhide, sylvanite etc.) and lots of accessories with cool effects.
I want to talk about the DLC too, Weapons&Armor bundle is almost completely useless, i mean, it does give you a head start but it will only last about an hour or so. Then you will start to find better gear. I just made a character in which i rush the main quest, no sides, no exploring just straight marching on the main quest line. Even tho it means i neglect main means of getting gear, in about 2.5-3 hours i replaced all the gear i got from the DLC.  So i will say pass on that. But Dead Kel and Naros are actually quite good. Both come with completely unique areas, enemies, lore, stories, characters and gear. Which i dig.
It's definetely a must play for Fantasy RPG fans.
A very underappreciated game, fun story and the DLC's are actually worth it.

I wish I could say I've enjoyed this game, but for the most part it's been a huge letdown.
-NetherRealm has maintained their consistency in terms of the quality of the online multiplayer experience for their fighters; absolutely abysmal and unplayable.  Input lag makes execution of relatively intermediate techniques. such as run cancelling or fuzzy blocking, very nearly impossible.  This reduces online play to picking characters who have abusable and usually unsafe moves that are powerful, because the lag makes them extremely difficult to consistently react to.
-As usual with MK games, most of the strategy for the entire roster lay in connecting with a chainable normal that allows you to follow up with a combo.  Zoning is extremely weak and defense is often a poor choice, as most of the offense boils down to forcing your opponent to guess right in 50/50 mixup scenarios.  Guess wrong 3 times during a match and you lose.  The execution threshold is so low that this sort of gameplay isn't difficult to master, but doesn't feel rewarding when successful because it really just comes down to a glorified coin-toss.
I realize that's more an indictment of MK's tradition as it's always been that way, but when you add this sort of a system to the lag fest that is MKX's online multiplayer, it's worsened by the fact that even if you called the coin toss right, lag may have still rendered you unable to act in time.  It's unacceptable for a fighting game of any competency.
-Single player is extremely lackluster and not compelling.  Story-mode is full of the inane nonsense you've come to expect from MK, except this time with more tactical bro-dude crap that makes it even more cringeworthy than normal.  I've always hated story modes in fighters, but this might just be the worst one I've played, and I REALLY hated MK9's.

Compared to MK9's AI, this is phoned in tripe; you either choose AI that's mindnumbingly stupid or incites controller breaking rage; there's no in-between.

Toy Soldiers is a game set in a World War I Diarama where models of soldiers fight each other in a fresh tower defense style. As the player, you set up nests of weapons to deal with oncoming waves of infantry, armoured vehicles and aircraft. After you've placed your nests, you can choose to control them yourself. On select maps, you're even given the chance to control sniper towers, bi-planes, bomber planes, and two different types of tanks. You gain cash for each kill you get, this cash can then be spent on upgrading your weapons, which you unlock as you play the campaign. There's currently three campaigns where you fight as the british, americans and french, and the germans. The game is stylized to fit the Diarama style, so soldiers explode into plastic-y peices and giant rooms where the diarama is set can be seen in the sky. Overall, Toy Soldiers is a very enjoyable game, and I've gotten more than $10 worth of enjoyment from it.

To say I love the show RWBY would be an understatement. When I heard that an actual game based on the show was being made I of course freaked out like every other fan out there. After getting a gaming PC I could use to play the game, I immediately bought an Early-Access copy and jumped right into it.
So, after a couple of games, here is what I think of RWBY: Grimm Eclipse.
The Good: Right off the bat, this game is visually great. The environments are rich in color (minus Mountain Glen) and is very refreshing compared to brown and grey most AAA titles seem to stick with when it comes to levels. The character models also look like they came straight from the show itself and do each of the characters justice.
The controls are also solid. Minus a few odd button placements, such as the jumping into air dashs button combination, I found use of a keyboard and mouse with this game easy and not a struggle at all. Response time is also top notch, where my character attack with virtually no delay. Overall, for a PC gaming rookie such as me, this game is easy to pick up and to have fun with.
The bad: This game will get repetitive very quickly. New game modes and missions are needed if this game is going to have any longivity whatsoever. Killing Grimm is fun, but at the core, they're all about the same. This game needs variety either by new characters, enemies, or game modes ASAP.
The voice acting is... okay? Except for Blake (I'll give her a free pass since her voice actor hasn't recorded lines for this game), the cast still captures the characters well. My problem is that there isn't any banter between the four playable characters. To me, this is a missed opportunity. I want to hear dialogue between each character after clearing a wave of Grimm and interact with one another. The more dialogue there is, the more I can see people play just to hear it all.
Also of note are some small graphical glitches in the game. Mountain Glen has some trees that don't load the textures on their trunks and some frames cut out during combat. I haven't experienced any crashes yet, so that's good.
Overall, I'm very happy to see RWBY get a game. I hope to see more characters in this game soon, like team CFVY, as well as new Grimm not seen in the show. Now if you excuse me, I'm going to play some more games.
Thank you.

It looks good, has the same style and graphics as the show, smooth combat, framerate, and voice acting.
But, none of the unqiue abilities or special/cool moves in the show are in the game. For example, no sniper gun mode for Ruby. In the show she can anchor the rifle with the scythe portion and snipe for better accuracy, in the game you just get a single shot ability. In the show she can propell herself with the gun recoil, none of this is in the game, none of that really matters in the game.
Then there's Weiss, her abilities in game sort of coincide with the show, but you can't make glyphs where you want, you can't jump around on them, the glyphs are mainly just graphics for the 3 abilities that you get. The unique support role and moves in the show are just not there. Weiss' weapon also is able to switch dust types in the show, none of that is in the game.
ALSO: No Semblence for any characters, a key ability for all characters in the show.
Same goes for the other characters, and if they add new ones. The reason the show is good is because of all the unique ways they use their weapons and team ups. This game is just a plain hack and slash with none of that special flavor you get from the show. No special aerial attacks, limited mobility, none of the innovation we see from the show is there. If this game was called anything else or had a totally different IP it wouldn't sell.
I call this a wasted opportunity because it's a great IP to build a fighting game/hack n slash game but with limited skills, no unique abilities, low skill cap, there's no way this game comes close to emulating what the show has done.
The game could have been great for PvP as well, if they implemented blocking, counters, better controls, more skills, etc. However, I just don't see them going in that direction.
This game is a mindless hack and slash at the very core and nothing more. I suspect most will buy due to the show being awesome, but my advice is just watch the show because none of that is in the game.
It was fun to try, but I'm getting my Steam refund as I can see where the game is headed and it's in the wrong direction.
tl;dr: Game has shallow gameplay with 2-3 button mashing hack and slash, low skill cap, with none of the special moves that you see in the show. I advise do not buy

Saw this game on sale for 19¢ and saw the game had generally positive reviews on Steam, so I decided to give it a shot.
Graphics: D-. The first thing that stood out for me was how bad the graphics are. We're talking PS2-era graphics here, complete with low resution textures, poor lighting, the whole bit. It doesn't seem like a lot of effort was put into them. Especially with subtitles that use a basic Arial font with no style added to them whatsoever. But, graphics like these are typical in most Unity-based games and they did the job I guess.
Sound: B+. Apart from the sound effect when picking up items (that sounds like someone hitting a Quarter against an empty bottle of Coke), the sound effects & music were both well done.
Story: C-. Nothing fancy here, I won't go too far into it because of spoilers.
Gameplay: C+. Apart from the first room which teaches you how to look for items (by listening for them), there is no other tutorial so to speak. The objective is to find all the pages to your Daughter's lost journal and to solve puzzles using certain items to get past obstructions. The rooms are randomly generated so there is no map, while this may make it confusing it ultimately doesn't matter, the game still progresses in linear fashion. I haven't quite figured out how to avoid Hat Man, but you'll know if he's close by when the screen flickers, your heart starts pounding, and the wind nearby sounds all distorted. As for scariness, I personally did not get too spooked even when getting caught my first time. In fact I was more♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off than anything. Results may vary for others, but for me it just didn't freak me out at all. Overall the game can be completed fairly quicky once you find out what to do (I suggest reading a walkthrough, it helps).
Performance: C. It's a unity game, so don't expect too many graphical issues like low framerate or glitches. I'm pretty sure just about any PC made after 2003 would be able to run it smoothly. The movement controls are fine, but using items and performing actions seem to have a considerable lag. There were times where left-clicking a door to open it took several times for it to work.
Presentation: F. As with the issues with the graphics I mentioned earlier, It doesn't seem like a lot of effort was put into this game. Although it looks like a considerable amount of people worked on this game according to the credits, this game feels like something a dev team of 3-5 people could've made in about a month. Also, it seems like most of the achievements are broken and unobtainable due to bugs. Forum members brought this up back in May 2015 and they have not been addressed as of October. So it seems like support this game has been abandoned.
Overall this game is barely worth it at 19 cents and I definitely would not recommend paying full price for this title.

Disclaimer: As I am writing this review, I have gotten to Stage 4. I have yet to beat this game.
As a big fan of C64 shmups I was really excited to play this game and it didn't disappoint at all. Some might recall that earlier this game started life as Katakis II, and Katakis may just be my favorite shmup out there. However, upon playing this game it becomes clear that while there is Katakis influence to be had here, this game is more like if you took the shmup sections from Rendering Ranger (Super Famicom) and made a full game out of that. Not that this is a bad thing, I personally love the shmup sections from RR, so I was very happy about this. Either way, there is some Manfred Tenz-esque fun to be had here.
One area of skepticism that people had when the game was announced as Katakis II, and one that I've seen even now is the early levels looking "too easy" and "too empty". In all fairness, I had that to a degree but I was still optimistic. Now that the game is out I am overwhelmingly happy to announce that they're not only significantly more challenging than they look, but they serve as a great entry point to the game. This game isn't going to beat you into the ground out of sheer sadism right as the game begins like some of the other games of this Trenzian design philosophy but instead opts for easing the player into it more...before beating you into the ground out of sheer sadism. The game may start off mildly challenging, but it doesn't take too long before it gradually shifts that into complete brutality.
Because of this, I would gladly recommend this to people who might be interested in this style of shmup design but have never played a C64 shmup before, but I wouldn't recommend it to more casual players looking for an easier variant. This is a very hardcore game at heart.
The game was a bit more memory intensive than I thought it was going to be, but thankfully, once you find settings that have the game running well even in the comparatively emptier sections- the game seems to run just as well when things go crazy. The game runs very consistently once you find that sweet-spot between visuals and performance (unless you have a really good PC).
As far as controls go, the keyboard layout I found to be a bit odd. It also doesn't tell you in the options menu but rather in text on the title screen if you wait a bit.
Arrow Keys to move
Space for Special Weapon
"A" for Fire.
It's not too bad, but I kind of just jumped into the game and I ended up scrambling to find the fire button when the game started.
Xbox 360 controllers are supported and I used a PS3 controller emulating a 360 one and this has worked favorably for me. However, do note that the controller doesn't do anything on the title screen and you'll use the mouse to interact with the menu interface and the keyboard for typing in names for high scores. The controller comes into play in-game with self-explanitory controls and the start button allowing you to pause. I could imagine this throwing off newer players, but gamers familliar with playing games on systems like the Amiga probably won't mind too much (and I'd imagine that being a good portion of the audience for this game anyway).
Overall, I'm having a lot of fun with this and given the lack of reviews, that leads me to believe that not a lot of people are playing this game. I think that seriously needs to change so if you're a fan of this kind of thing- play this game and tell your friends. Spread the word.

Does anybody here remember Crush for C64? It was a decent shmup on that machine, an inofficial sequel to Katakis/Denaris.  This new Crush game strongly reminds me two other games of the Katakis-Creator Manfred Trenz: Enforcer and Rendering Ranger. Personally I am a fan of this era of shooters, oldschool presentation and controls, but tbh not really of Enforcer. My expectations by watching previews were more or less optimistic.
First of all: The music is awesome
Speaking for myself I find the game pretty enjoyable. Gameplaywise it really nails Amiga vibes, like a mélange of Enforcer and Z-Out. The attack waves are slower paced compared to the classics, but same time challenging but fair. Graphics are okay, but... don't know. kinda generic. Maybe it is just me, but pixellated graphics would have been a better match IMHO.

Nobody is a bigger fan of these old school retro tryle games than I am, being a owner and lover of my Commodore 64 back in the 80's...  And this game is exactly the type of game that I have always loved.
But NO.  Just NO.  No, No, No, No.
I want to thank the developers of this game for handing me a free key for evaluation, and I hope my brutally honest feedback and review can help them either make this game a better value or give us customers better games in the future.
Bottom line.. There are 1,000 free games just like this that play, feel, and look better.  There is nothing unique or special about this game, and to ask $12 USD for a game like this where I honestly feel only a week or maybe two was spent making this game gives me a bitter taste.  I may have received this game for free, but I feel dirty somehow playing this game on my channel, just knowing the developers are trying to gouge customers for $12 for this thing.
47% is my first impressions score, mostly hurt by only getting a 7 out of 40 on the value aspect of my scoring.  And at $!2, a 7 out of 40 was probably too generous of a score there.
Not recommended, unless maybe you just love this type of game AND this game goes on sale on Steam for about 80% off or more.
Sorry devs, you can do better than this.  I know you can.  Give us a good value for our money, not try to leave us feel beaten up and robbed.  Best of luck with your future games.

Spelunky (also known as Spelunky HD), is an amazing remake of the classic indie title Spelunky with a ton of new features, originally released on Xbox Live Arcade in 2012; I recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of indie platformers and roguelites.

There is also a deathmatch mode and daily leaderboards which will bring you coming back for more every time.
The artstyle is gorgeous and the entire game oozes with atmosphere, coupled with an adorable cast of characters and many unlockable ones which all have so much charm and wonderful designs.
This game is best played with a controller, however it's fully playable with just a keyboard. I do, however, believe that at least one controller (in addition to a keyboard, although just playing with 2 controllers is recommended) is required for the local multiplayer.

I'm a fan of the Mortal Kombat franchise, and was looking forward to this game since it was announced. I saw a great sale on it recently, so I decided "what the heck" and picked it up.
I avoided preorder, as a principle, and later decided not to buy the game during the Summer Sale due to all the horrible reviews it had, claiming it was broken on PC, has terrible performance, is a poor console port, etc.

I am able to run on high settings, with a nice solid 96fps, with no bugs and no issues. Furthermore, there are a whole lot of options to customize; more in fact than most PC only games! It handles alt-tabbing just fine, etc.
The game works, it is fun, and it is a worthy successor to MK9. If you like fighting games, specifically Mortal Kombat, and your computer isn't a
toaster, there is really no reason to avoid this title at this point. The game might have had issues in the past, but people really need to get off the second hand hate train - there is nothing wrong with the game today.
