An Honest Aussie Review:
Is this game beginner friendly?
Yes and no in a way, its easy to spam moves against the cpu and other low leveled players online however that changes when you rank up online so then it becomes more of a challenge in blocking and punishing moves that take long to recover from. I'd rather go and try something like Marvel Vs Capcom or Street Fighter which is probably a litlle easier to understand as the move list is rather small in comparision.
Player Base?
Player base isn't that big as you can imagine, if you have a console i'd recommend you play on that instead if you want to find a quicker match, however the matchmaking or 'NetCode' is fairly good for the PC version as you would imagine.
Story good?
Story is meh, personally im not found of story modes in arcade fighters but if you are theres enough button mashing and content to keep you entertained for a while but dont expect hours as it is a fighting game of course and Tekken isnt really known for its full long story gameplay.
Bruh Roster Trash?
Tekken 7's roster is great in my opinion as it brings new fighters into the mix, meaning new moves and play styles to make online fighting more interesting and difficult. You of course have some of the iconic characters like Jin, Yoshimitsu,Kazuya, Eddy, Kuma, Law, Paul while also bringing new fighters such as Master Raven 'Similar to Raven in a sense' Claudio, Lucky Chloe, a new Jack, Akuma from Street Fighter and many other uniquely designed characters.
Gameplay?
Similar to all the other Tekken games before however it now has the new Rage system which acts similar to Street Fighters special bar but instead is only gained once throughout a round when your health is low enough. You can use it to extend a combo or create an opening or just use it to gain some space getting away from a wall and so on. Moves are updated from Tekken Tag 2 and some new moves have been added along as well.
Overall i would recommend this game to all Intermediate fighting game players and potentially Beginners depending on much time you are willing to spend in order to get familar with the mechanics and long move lists and no be scared away from the game due to move spammers and silly loses.

Tekken 7 is incredibly complex, as someone who is new to fighting games the first few hours were really hard, but it is fun to learn more about how the game and the characters work.

The only thing that I really don't like is the speed mode in the trasure hunt, it really dumbs down to button mashing.
I hope they'll improve the online play in the next months, otherwise the characters are fun to play and learn and it's great to make people salty online ;)

This game is quite beautiful and sad. It's sort of a fairy tale of two brothers who must journey together to find a cure for their sick father. They've already lost their mother to an accident. What's really unique about this game is how you control the brothers simultaneously using the two thumbs sticks of your game controller (I used an Xbox controller). The left control stick is how your maneuver the older of the two brothers and the right one controls the younger. The left and right triggers act as action buttons for getting the brothers to interact with the world. The brothers have various strengths and weaknesses. For example, the older brother is stronger and so can lift heavy objects and activate heavy levers. But he can't fit though bars like the younger brother. The younger brother can't swim so he has to hold on to his older brother in water. The game comes up with many unique puzzles and challenges, however contrived,  where you will have to get the brothers to work together to advance through the various scenes of the game. This game has some very high production values; the sound, music and graphics are all very beautiful and evocative. Everyone in the game speaks some unknown language which I feel wasn't necessary for this game, but it does, however, give the world a very alien feel to it. Come to think of it, it really also brings focus to the other storytelling aspects of the game which create a good atmosphere and can also bring out the emotional aspects of the tale (yes, I did cry). The unique control scheme was pretty gimmicky but very cool and the controls felt right; never frustrating. It only took me 3.5 hours to go through the game and you know what, that length feels right for this game. I have limited gameplay time, so I sometimes prefer these sorts of shorter games. I really recommend this game for a unique experience and a good, though basic narrative.

I had been looking forward to playing Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning for quite some time. The action-RPG style was very appealing as most combat in this genre is point-and-click clunkiness.
To my initially great pleasure, the combat was just as I expected, similar to Darksiders but as I played further, I found it to be very boring and repetitive. The same attack sequences, the same types of enemies, the same thing... over and over. So while the combat was good to start, it failed to hold my interest in the long run... even after unlocking the full tree.
The stories (main and side) of KoA are extremely bland. Only towards the very end did the main story line get somewhat interesting then it felt completely rushed and overlooked in the interest of ending the story. If you play RPGs for a deep story, you will not find it here.
I was very disappointed to find a level cap of 40. If you most of the side quests, you will hit this well before the end-game. Sure you can respec any try a different playstyle or character build but in the end, you will still be maxed at 40 which truly only allows for one specialization.
The amazing choice/consequence of alternative games was non-existent in KoA. You have dialogue options but none that really affect the story or outcome... so while the game says you decide your fate, this is hardly the case.
Graphically, the game looked decent. Some of the textures (especially grass) looked awful but it ran very smoothly. Music was good and very fitting.
The crafting aspect allows you to create any kind of weapon/amor you want. This is a pretty nice feature as it does allow you to customize gear according to your playstyle.
On the plus side, the DLC (Teeth of Naros and Dead Kel) were both excellent. They are fully developed and not quick to complete. Both were definitely worth the extra money.
Overall, I was disappointed with KoA. The repetitive nature and linear choice/story made for a bland experience. My rating is 6.5/10.

Okay. Hello, if you are reading this, then you may be wondering why I gave it a thumbs down. It's simple.
Though I love the game, it is in need of some early design changes and more development.
First of all, the script. I feel that the character interactions are pretty genuine "for the most part" with some cheesy lines here and there but the problem is, is that the conversations are very brief and there's a lot of silence. I'm not talking about the bugs where some of the audio doesn't play or the filters don't turn off, I mean those moments where your running around and theres nothing. Though the world is expansive, I think there needs to be a lot more cutscenes and conversations. That would be the same with battles as well because there isn't a "WOW, it's battle time" or "OMG, so many grim, quick get ready", it's just "grim, fight, defend." so I feel a lot more should be added there in how they are presented and to show off the characters relations more.
Next is the battle system. Combined with hints of RPG elements, I honestly think it's a bit bare and very much hack and slash. I would say it needs to be changed up a bit more and there should be options for stance changes so that guns have a use in the middle of melee combat rather than just being "a thing" and so players can focus on dealing with groups or an idividual enemy in a style that suits them.
A minor issue I have with this game is that despite being a team, RWBY doesn't do much other than hack at the same enemy so I think more Utility should be added in with the abilities rather than "USE TO WIN" because said abilities honestly feel weak after a while, make health pick ups/life steal a thing and also, reduce the amount of staggers the enemies have on you and make them a genuine threat. I would also suggest adding a system so that teammates can shout out commands to guide each other but also so they can shout at the grim to lead them away and have an alley sneak of to help their downed friend.
So far, it feels like a 6/10 but it could be much better.

So, I have to preface this game by pointing out that I was given this game for free by one of the only marketers that isn't an idiot in the industry, who handed keys for the game out free of charge to drum up press for the price drop and the free update.
Ignoring that, the game isn't actually bad, but it IS something you've probably played before; this game is a slightly more involved version of Slender.
If you weren't scared by Slender, or games like Slender, you won't be scared by this.
This is half of why my review may or may not be something you should listen to, because quite frankly this sort of thing is fairly distant from what I consider my affair.
You're chased by numerous ghosts and the HatMan, all of whom look like the bad guy from Ferngully. Also, you can find the credits to the game in a room, killing most of the atmosphere that's set by the idea that the game is based on a true story.
Aside from that, the environments are very enclosed, dark asylum settings, so it raises the question of whether you'd get this for cheap, Slender for cheaper, or Amnesia/Outlast for a bit more than this.
I do have to say if nothing else the game is actually reasonably priced when it's on sale for 20 cents, although five bucks may be a bit much.
I'm actually a bit torn, because I don't actually see this doing too well outside of 20 cents to a buck territory, because the entire presentation is fairly amateur and ends up being something I'd compare to free unity games, but damn that marketer was nice.
Can't say I can recommend this past a sale, because the actual content just isn't the sort of thing you'd usually see charged for.
Also, for the half a person that cares, I think I bugged achievements so... There's that?

The Hat Man: Shadow Ward is a survival horror game where you play as a parent trying to find your daughter in an insane asylum. Along the way, you collect items, pages from your daughter's journal, and avoid the Hat Man. At first, I was impressed with the graphics, sound, and voice overs. Once the game began however, my enthusiasm was drained to find out it was just another Slender style game. I was disappointed by this because the idea and concept of this game was so great. It could have become a great adventure, survival horror game, but by modeling the game play of a Slender game, it just becomes a "spin off" of Slender. I wouldn't abandon the concept at all, but instead work towards making a bigger game with the concept. As much as I like the concept however, I just can't recommend this game I'm afraid.

As an avid lover of horror games and resident scardey-cat, there's no better combination than a good, old-fashioned, spooky indie horror puzzle game to get the blood pumping.
Although the game is quite short and doesn't have the most intricate story line, it manages to maintain a spooky atmosphere throughout the playthrough.
The rooms and corridors are somewhat repetitive, but do shuffle themselves around, so back-tracking is simply not that simple. The straightforward design is accentuated by decent graphics and a very eerie atmosphere. Despite collecting (what seems like) hundreds of diary entries from your daughter, very little is actually revealed about the Hat Man, adding to his mysterious allure. The puzzles aren't exactly rocket-science, more of a "find-the-object-and-use-it-on-another-object" type of scenario. Nevertheless, this just adds emphasis on the fact that a creepy shadow fiend is chasing you and you can't spend time strolling around taking pictures and making mental notes of how good the wallpaper would look in your own house.
Overall, I would recommend this game, especially if it happens to be on sale. Simple, effective and the voice over is hilariously awkward.

Although this game is somewhat different from the original I feel that it's a very solid game. The combat flows nicely, there is some decent customization, and everything has had a graphical upgrade. There are 4 characters that play drastically different depending on one's play style, all of which are very balanced (despite most people saying they aren't). All of the characters also have there own arsenal of weapons and skills which adds some depth and progression to the game. This game is skill/knowledge based which makes it extremely fun and gives it a reasonable learning curve. The skill is mainly dodging and gunplay while the knowledge is how to counter certain characters/playstyles. The game also has a decent story through The Campaign Mode which is also fun and challenging. They currently only have one campaign but by the looks of it they plan to add more along with some challenge modes (which I am looking forward to).
However, there are 3 minor issues that I have had with the game which I pressume are being worked on. The first problem I have is lack of PvP game modes. There are currently 3 (being Team Deathmatch, Team Elimination, and Time Assualt) all of which are very basic (i.e. Kill enemy team). The Second problem I have is lack of map variety. There are currently 7 maps most of which, although funtional and good looking, are very bland in design. Basically all maps have 3 ways to get to the same area which makes maps seem very small (I assume this is to keep up the hectic and fast paced action of the game). My final issue I have with this game are the coins for the Campaign. The coins are extra lives for when you die and you only get 3 a day, which dont get me wrong is more generous than most games, but I think the vast majority of people would have prefered 3 per level or checkpoint revives.
Overall I find this game enjoyable but, slighty lacking in variety. I would reccomend this to any fan of the original Gunz, or someone looking for fast paced enjoyable gun combat.

In some ways, this game isn't realistic enough.  I have an Irish wolfhound, and a burglar broke into my house and stole my things, all without a peep out of the dog!  Seriously?!  The dog had already been told to guard the house several times - which let's face it, you wouldn't have to do with a real dog, especially a breed like this, we're not talking chihauha here!  The dog should be programmed to automatically guard, and the burglar should be afraid of it.  Also, your dog runs away if you only feed it for a couple of days or so, and don't hug it, or play with it, or walk it, treat it, brush it ....
In other ways, the game is eerily realistic.  By the time my Sim gets up, showers, brushes her teeth, makes some breakfast, feeds the dog, plays with the dog, hugs/treats/or brushes the dog, takes out the trash, and recycles the newspaper, it's time to go to work.  And my sim only has a part-time job!!  Then she has to come home, make dinner, do the whole dog thing again, maybe find a bit of time to read a skill book, and go to bed.   Way, way, way too much like real life.  Except that I have a full-time job in real life.  Why on earth would I want to play a game that was as filled with mundane tasks and routine as my own life?  People play games to escape from that!
I know, you can change the time speed.  But shouldn't the devs have already set it up as a default that the routine things don't take so long to do, so you don't have to constantly play with the time settings?  and shouldn't they have set it up so your sim knows what to do after you've done the same routine at roughly the same time on the same days, and your sim just goes and does it superfast, leaving you more time to go off and do other things in the game?  am I supposed to set this up, making routine lists and feeding them to my sim?   If I leave my sim alone to do things, she does stupid, pointless things like reading and re-reading Where's Bella, over and over again.
Maybe I just don't know how to play this game, I know it's a popular game, and maybe there's a way around these problems that my 20  hours or so of playing hasn't been enough for me to find.   I get bored quick, though, so if a game can't me interested within that 20 hours, forget it.    Sims3 gets a big thumbs down from me.

PROS:
*The PC Port is damn near perfect. No issues with gameplay whatsoever. Buy it.
*Gameplay has improved with new mechanics (rage art, cinematic transitions during game, bullet-time last hits, etc) Buy it.
*The Gallery has a section to view all the Nostalgic Cutscenes from the first game all the way up to the present. Buy it.
*Customizability is vast and is very Reminiscent of the Tekken Tag Tournament 2 version on Wii U. Buy it.
*New Game modes like treasure Battle allow u to acquire said Customizable items more easily. Buy it.
*The system Requirements are slightly Over-Estimated. This thing can run even on the mere specs of a Surface Pro 3. Buy it.
CONS:
*Audio Driver issues sometimes present usually when connecting to a tv using HDMI. Check Community for workarounds.
*Hard to connect to stable Multiplayer Matches. If you tend to opt for a ranked match, secure a fast NET plan from your ISP.
*The Back-Stories of characters in story mode are Gone. Instead, the story mode is explored through journal entries. This game focuses mainly on the Mishima-Kazama feud. So be warned.
BOTTOMLINE: If you're an avid fighting game fanatic, tekken will introduce you mechanics that are much more fluid and challenging that makes it one of the best compared to other fighting games out there.

False Advertising about DLC - It's one use only.
DLC (downloadable content) is additional content that can be purchased and added to a game, typically adding weapons/levels/in game currency or other features to the game.
The DLC for this game apparently is artificially subdivided into 'durable' (multiple use) and non-'durable' components (restricted to single use). Nowhere in the advertising material is it made at all apparent that this is the case. In the attached advertisements, 'durable' and non-'durable' components are listed together with no distinction, and no information whatsoever on 'durability'.
Non-'durable' DLC of this nature is completely unprecedented in the long history of DLC in this industry, and thus this is entirely unforeseeable and unexpected on the part of all buyers.
As far as I can tell, this information has only been released by the manufacturer on a single social media post AFTER release of the product, which many customers had pre-ordered (myself included). This behaviour has led customers to use the single use non-'durable' DLC without any indication that it would be single use.
It is clear the manufacturer meant to conceal this information and deceive buyers.
- I have reported this to my national equivalent of the Advertising Standards Agency.

It's finally here! The newest installment of the Deus Ex franchise is a lot of fun. The gameplay is fun and pretty well done, there's a lot of exploration to be done and secrets to be found. The game feels a lot less linear than Human Revolution, and so far the story is well told. Gone are the clunky boss fights that ruined HR, playing a pacifist playthrough is very fun and finding a shortcut or alternate path to an objective feels very rewarding.
Graphics wise, the game looks like a more polished version of its predecessor. Some people are reporting significant graphical issues, however I have been pretty lucky and have had no trouble running the game on ultra (GTX980). Your mileage may vary.
However, none of this matters because Square Enix has absolutely ruined the game with their disgusting microtransactions. As you have no doubt heard by now, SE has included microtransactions not just for multiplayer, but for ammunition, grenades and praxis kits (used to unlock abilities) for SINGLE PLAYER. The fact that somebody approved this sheer idiocy to be part of the game is a staggering condemnation not just of Square Enix, but the modern video game industry as a whole.
DE:MD could have been such a good game. Unfortunately, it now exists solely as a beacon highlighting the utter contempt we as gamers are held in by Square Enix.
Shame, shame, shame.

The sad part is... I've played scarier games for free. I'm pretty sure this *isn't* the scariest game of 2014.
This *was* a fifteen dollar game that made Daylight look good. It's dropped to five and I suppose that's more reasonable than Daylight.
The game itself is an obvious Slender clone, where you're running around grabbing pages while avoiding the monster. Unlike slender, however, the monster doesn't ever teleport. No, he just follows you around endlessly, and phases through walls. So if you get cornered, you may as well die then because I waited five minutes staring at him while crouched with no movement, whatsoever. It would seem like a breath of fresh air, since you can obviously outrun but not hide from the Hat Man, unlike in recent horror games where hiding is key. In this, you're running around to get pages with no places to hide, much like slender.
The voice acting is pretty hilarious(ly bad), but the sound quality is alright. This really is just your average run-of-the-mill indie-horror game, with the same graphics, same UI, and same gameplay, except it's longer. Oh, and the layout of the hospital changes. It doesn't exactly randomize scares like Daylight, so there's not as much replay value (which implies loosely that there is some small replay value to Daylight, which is up to your interpretation)
If it were any shorter than it already is it wouldn't qualify for the price it has. If it were any longer, I'd be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and begging myself that this goddamn game would be over.
All in all, it's a fun... half-hour, and I can say it was worth the 19 cents I paid for it. maybe even worth $1.50-2.00.
I can recommend the game to you, but not at the price. In fact, almost any price, unless you want to do it to support the devs. The game itself is really not worth it.

Purchased this game after reading about who was involved in its creation. Left it in my library for a while and wasn't motivated to install or play it. I finally got around to it!
Firstly, the world is huge! There are many places to explore if you're into that. Secondly, there are a lot of quests to gather. So far I have not seen any consequences to the decisions your hero makes. The story doesn't seem to be too much about the hero, but those around the hero, which, in my opinion, caused me to disassociate with my toon. I didn't feel particularly important. I mostly felt like some lackey who needed to fetch this or go slay that.
The audio of the game bothered me a bit, particularly the character speech. In a lot of instances I could barely hear the NPCs speak and had to rely on subtitles to know what's going on. I looked for an adjustment that catered to headphones (if that was the problem) but found no such option in the menu. I understand that the sounds should be directional (ie the dialogue should sound softer when camera is turned away from the NPC), but this occurs in cutscenes as well and I found it annoying that I could not hear the voice actors.
The camera action in the game is also a bit wonky. In some situations the camera just...leaves you, as if you dropped it and you watch your toon run away. The sensitivity of camera movement, if you're using a mouse to look around, is way too sensitive. A light movement from the mouse could swing the camera really fast at odd angles. That sort of thing made combat a little frustrating for me, where one second I am charging at my target and the next I'm looking at the wrong direction.
All in all, it's a beautiful game with a LOT to do and has a deep customization factor for your hero, but those little problems I noted above just takes the immersion experience away from me. To be able to be immersed into the world and its lore is why I like RPGs in the first place.

The Hat Man: Shadow Ward is an indie "horror" game that adopts many game play features from Slenderman, but expands on them to bring you a some-what-suspenseful-page-collection-puzzle-game, and far more fair to you then Slenderman ever was.


You play as either the father or mother searching for their daughter in an insane asylum, after stumbling across your daughters journal, the book is ripped asunder. You now need to puzzle your way through the labyrinth of the asylum and collect pages of your daughters journal and tools to help you progress to the next series of rooms.
The voice acting is pretty amusing, it's
combination of "expressive" and "emotionless", probably first-time-voice actors. If nothing else you need to play just enough to hear some of the ridicules things they say.

As I've already eluded too,

I haven't played very many horror games so I won't pretend to well versed in the art that is "scaring people", I do know that whenever I play a scary game my whole goal is to keep myself from expressing it. This game succeeded in keeping me in suspense and catching me by surprise a few times.
Potential key game play feature spoiler:

The achievements are fairly straightforward; finish the game fast (30 minutes is the fastest achievement), finish the game without saving, and then the rest are pretty simple or obvious repeat-to-get-this-achievement.
Ruh roh, it looks like three of the achievements are bugged, the counters for: Paranormally Active, Cheating Death, and A Good Book are broken and not adding up properly. This maybe fixed someday, but judging from the forums the achievements have been broken since at least May 1st 2015.

The Hat Man: Shadow Ward is priced at $4.99, I was gifted my copy by one of the developers (thank you!), the price is pretty fair, considering the effort put into the game. However you probably won't put more than a couple hours into the game.

When it comes to Indie games, I tend to prefer to show support for up and budding game developers. This game might be a skip for most people, but it does have promise and takes a few steps in a different direction from the original inspiration.

It's a pretty standard Fantasy Action Game experience - you pick from a couple of Totally Unique Racial Categories, make some basic cosmetic changes (hair, skin tone, etc.) and then you go smash the crap out of things.
Character progression is somewhat reminiscent of Torchlight with a bit of The Witcher for good measure.  You can "multiclass" between Tough Smashy Style, Sneaky Stabby Style, and Explody Magic Style.
The lore is more-or-less your standard fantasy novel business - there's good (not-)elves and bad (not-)elves and the bad (not-)elves are going HAM on your homeland.  Good thing you're a Chosen One and can stand up to those naughty naughty (not-)elves!  Did we mention that you have a Mysterious Past that you have to uncover?  Of course you do.
It's going to be tainted by comparison to Skyrim, as they're both Epic Fantasy Smashy Smash games.  Skyrim excels in having a truly open world (much of KOA is pretty much linear - the old invisible fence is full in effect here) and near-limitless modification capacity.  KOA excels at having a much more enjoyable combat system - lots of fancy combos and trick moves.  There's a "rage meter" mechanic that's kind of neat in a silly "Mortal Kombat" way - you charge up your murders and then you go into Super Murder Mode, where you get, of all things, a quicktime event where you have to mash buttons to Extra Super Duper Murder someone for bonus XP.
It's silly, even for Epic Fantasy Gaming, but it's probably worth snagging on sale.

I figured it was about time I rewrote this review now that I've gave this another chance after around 1 year since my last attempt at the game.
A year has passed since this game's release date it has since exited early access and has become a full fledged game, hence why I don't think I can reccomend it even now. RWBY: GE is set in a interlude period after team RWBY's first mission. It is a hack and slash game. The game consists of about 10 chapters with around 9 different enemies (Not types just enemies). This game had great potential but now that it has left early access allow me to go into detail as to why I can not reccomend this game in it's "finished" state.
When you think of a hack and slash game you think of combos, button mashing, waves of enemies, and while you do get this, you can see that it is incredibly barebones for it's price of 19.99. You have 1 set of combos for each character, light attacks, heavy attacks, and ranged attacks. The amount of different combos in the game is incredibly limited, and you are stuck with that set of combos for the entirity of the game. This can make combat feel dull at many points after the first few levels.
The upgrade tree is nearly worthless except for one or two upgrades. They offer a few bonuses, but quite a few of them are only useful/unlockable in multiplayer which considering the game's playerbase has been rapidly declining makes them useless in general. You only get a total of 10 skill points for their incredibly small tree. The tree fits the size of the game, but that points to an issue with the game as a whole with it being so short.
The combat on higher difficulties can be completely random thanks to wonky hitboxes at certain times. I've had my heavy attacks miss altogether or have had an enemy a huge distance away from me still manage to hit me. It appears randomly but frequently unfortunately making higher difficulty solo runs frusturating.
Now this is where I have my biggest gripes about the game. I know that Rooster Teeth can make a great story capable of grabbing my attention for 4 seasons of their show, but somehow they manage to make a complete miss of a story that fails in several aspects. When I think RWBY I think a good story, and I could've forgiven the unintresting combat if it managed this.
Note: This next section of my review will contain spoilers (Not that there is much to spoil, but still)
This is a summary of the story
You enter in the emerald forest finding a hint of some type of shadow organization, and find even further hints of them in the next chapter and something indicating that they may be trying to trap grimm. You see a mutated grimm which perplexes Dr. Oobleck. You find a ship which appears to belong to the shadow organization, and "Accidently" enter a crate which goes to an undisclosed island. The bad guy reveals himself and a breif past with Dr. Ospin. Bad guy then summons you into his lair, and acts nonchalant about you destroying his hardware for a good two minutes, and then a minute later freaks out for nearly the exact same reasons. After freaking out after you defeat the same enemies (Actually same waves even) that you've seen 10 times before he unveils the big ol boss of the game. 10 minutes of cheese later you beat the boss, and he self destructs his base.
Now what are the problems I have with this story?
The pacing is really terrible, there are only 10 chapters and each level is obscenely small. There is no room for anything at all to develop. The bad guy is also the worst shallow cliche villan I think I have seen in most of my time gaming, and I've been gaming since the pre PS1 era. He pretty much has no backstory except being a villan who likes to take science too far. He acts nonchalant at your first attempts and quickly breaks down into panic at the first sign of actual danger. His backstory is all but non existant except for what you can infer, and that would only be speculation. This was the most dissapointing and attrocious bad guy I could've ever expected rooster teeth to make. He can't even begin to compare to Cinder, Roman Torchwick, or Salem. Rooster teeth has shown they can make a good villan and that is what makes this game's antagonist all the more dissapointing.
I could've backed off from this a little IF they decided to change the artifacts in the game. When the game first released I thought the "Artifacts" were simply placeholders for actual world building/lore, but nope they function as nothing more than easy to obtain EXP bonuses. When they could've been actual artifacts, reports, collectables, how cool would it have been to see research documents from the antagonist? They would've given insight and much needed back story to an empty game. Instead they are Dr. Ospin's "Artifacts" that he used to define the teams at the beggining of the show.
There are a few DLC items for this game, but none of them add anything except for costumes or fanservice. They added team JNPR, costumes, and dances. This is a really crappy buisness practice only beneffiting from the RWBY IP, it's dissapointing that instead of writing a better story or making more enemies they go for the cash grab strategy. I don't think I will ever purchase another game from the affiliated companies again after this.
RWBY as a show will always be cherished by me, but as a game it was unbelievably dissapointing, don't buy this game and have Rooster Teeth stick to what they know.

In some ways, this game isn't realistic enough.  I have an Irish wolfhound, and a burglar broke into my house and stole my things, all without a peep out of the dog!  Seriously?!  The dog had already been told to guard the house several times - which let's face it, you wouldn't have to do with a real dog, especially a breed like this, we're not talking chihauha here!  The dog should be programmed to automatically guard, and the burglar should be afraid of it.  Also, your dog runs away if you only feed it for a couple of days or so, and don't hug it, or play with it, or walk it, treat it, brush it ....
In other ways, the game is eerily realistic.  By the time my Sim gets up, showers, brushes her teeth, makes some breakfast, feeds the dog, plays with the dog, hugs/treats/or brushes the dog, takes out the trash, and recycles the newspaper, it's time to go to work.  And my sim only has a part-time job!!  Then she has to come home, make dinner, do the whole dog thing again, maybe find a bit of time to read a skill book, and go to bed.   Way, way, way too much like real life.  Except that I have a full-time job in real life.  Why on earth would I want to play a game that was as filled with mundane tasks and routine as my own life?  People play games to escape from that!
I know, you can change the time speed.  But shouldn't the devs have already set it up as a default that the routine things don't take so long to do, so you don't have to constantly play with the time settings?  and shouldn't they have set it up so your sim knows what to do after you've done the same routine at roughly the same time on the same days, and your sim just goes and does it superfast, leaving you more time to go off and do other things in the game?  am I supposed to set this up, making routine lists and feeding them to my sim?   If I leave my sim alone to do things, she does stupid, pointless things like reading and re-reading Where's Bella, over and over again.
Maybe I just don't know how to play this game, I know it's a popular game, and maybe there's a way around these problems that my 20  hours or so of playing hasn't been enough for me to find.   I get bored quick, though, so if a game can't me interested within that 20 hours, forget it.    Sims3 gets a big thumbs down from me.

While this game is undoubtedly fun and charming, it has a number of rough edges that make it fall short of the franchise that it unashamedly mimics. A few examples:
1) Generally low difficulty and complexity in puzzles.
2) When destructible terrain comes into play, the "weak points" in a wall or structure are often only vaguely hinted at, ultimately encouraging the player to pepper entire areas with bombs in an attempt to uncover secrets.
3) Outside of boss fights, combat is usually a cakewalk, with lost health being easily and switfly replenished when you do make a mistake. Yet there are a few isolated instances in which a single mistake during a boss fight will kill you outright, regardless of how many hearts you have collected.
4) When fighting certain foes, a projectile counter-attack mechanic can (and some times MUST) be used. But the accuracy/efficiency of this counter-attack is based entirely on luck, rather than skill.
Ultimately, you will get more quality and longevity out of a genuine Zelda title, but Oceanhorn is still a fun and engaging romp that will keep you entertained for a few days.

This game was originally released for the ipad and now ported to PC. In general I tend to find those two things normally equate to that of total crap. Surprisingly however, Oceanhorn stands out as a shining example of how a solid port should be done.
No hiding the fact it's a total Wind Waker clone. Pretty much everything in this game draws direct connection from much of the Zelda series. Trying to fill those shoes can be a pretty huge task, which it at least does a pretty good job of emulating. It manages to capture the nice open colorful world in the same fashion as Zelda. The characters, monsters and bosses are fairly creative. Most of what you encounter tries to mimic the art style of Zelda quite closely. Not quite as charming of course, although to be fair it'd be hard to live up to some of the most beloved games of all time completely.
Sometimes you can sense a bit of the restraints from this game originally being intended for the ipad. The combat is good, but I feel like it's not quite as fluid or polished as it could have been. Had it not been originally designed around the ipad. For the most part at least it comes off rather well on the PC using a controller. It also allows for the use of mouse an keyboard controls.
Unlike Zelda, Oceanhorn features a leveling system. Gaining a level can result in earning coins an item refills, increasing the number of bombs you can carry, but it also serves to unlock other things such as a cannon item for your sail boat early on. The boat is your main source of transportation for island hopping around the world. Travelling by boat is done on a rail system unlike the free roaming in Wind Waker. I guess to try to make the travel portions a bit less dull, they decided to add in things like explosive mines and enemies along with crates and things you can shoot for experience and coins as you travel along. This portion can become a bit tedious at times.
The music is nice and the game looks good enough for what it's intended to be. Saving is done either automatically when entering a new area or when activating checkpoints. Not having the option to save manually however can be a little annoying. The game itself is pretty forgiving however. If you find yourself being killed, you're automatically transported back to the location of your last checkpoint save, while retaining any items and exp you collected beforehand. For the most part the difficulty is rather mild.
In the end for what faults it does have I would still recommend this to any fan of the Zelda series. All in all it's bit like a smaller Wind Waker lite. It does do a pretty good job in filling a nice niche, in which it's hard to find many similiar games on the PC. If you're looking for something to fill that Zelda-esque desire you probably won't regret buying Oceanhorn. Overall I'd rate this game at maybe a close 7 out of 10. Probably won't wow you, but enjoyable enough to be worth the time.

Brutal Legend is a game with identity issues. It can't seem to decide if it wants to be an open-world action-RPG, a real-time strategy game, or a driving simulator and due to that indecision none of those elements feel fully thought out or completed. The only thing that is thoroughly fleshed out is the Heavy Metal theme. There's sections that look like they were ripped right off of a Metal album cover, units that embody (or mock) fixtures of Metal culture, and a deep mythos that melds Norse mythology (the most Metal of all known mythologies) seamlessly with all that is Metal. Of all the shots Brutal Legend takes that just miss the mark, the commentary and the love of Metal is dead on. The game has the rare quality of producing lore that is instantly humorous but on a second look, is equally as capable of being taken seriously. That quality, and the fact the gameplay is switched up so often, makes it difficult to get too annoyed with its shortcomings. The familiar faces and voices of a couple stars in the world of Metal doesn't hurt either, even if they are overused to the point of parody.

: Despite being a game that's almost 7 years old, they still hold up and look great. The design of the characters, vehicles, weapons and the surround world all fit perfectly together. Great effects throughout.
:  In my opinion, it's the best video game soundtrack ever. Over 100 different songs from 75 bands (according to Wikipedia) in all different subgenres of metal. It's just fantastic.
: I played the game using an Xbox controller and found the controls very easy and intuitive. Whether it's fighting or commanding troops, the control scheme is easy and doesn't require a lot of unnecessary movement. The only issue I had was sometimes during battle I couldn't pull up my song list unless I hit the RT button multiple times in a row.
: The game was not quite what I expected. I thought this was going to be an action-adventure game where you solely control Eddie and fight with him. That's partly true. I did not realize the RTS-like elements of controlling and directing your crew throughout the game. It works well and is quite enjoyable, I just didn't realize it was part of the game. I will say that at times the combat feels repetitive and the RTS parts of the game all feel identical for the most part, but never to the point that it becomes unenjoyable.
: The voice acting in this game is incredible. All of the actors do a fantastic job, especially Jack Black. The story is fun and has a few twists and turns that keep you guessing. I really enjoyed all of the different characters introduced throughout the game, especially the metal legends.
I would say this is an absolute must play game if you're a fan of metal, but even if you're not I would still highly recommend it. It's another fantastic example of what makes Double Fine such a great studio.

Brothers is something special. I do not believe any review could do judgement to the sheer creativity this game has. Two brothers have to save their father and embark on a journey to find some magical medicine from a tree. While the premise may not sound most interesting, its simplicity combined with the extremely clever narrative create gamings first true artistic classic that will likely be credited as an inspiration for many generations to come.
One can see from the screenshot that the world is gorgeous and epic. When actually playing it this breathtaking feeling keeps recurring, and the game offers more than enough moments to truely take the environment in. The gorgeous music also adds to this.
The characters itself, while speaking gibberish, are animated with great attention to body language and tone of voice, to make it really easy to identify with them. They come across some very interesting scenarios, and the differences between the two brothers are made clear using the aforementioned techniques.
Instead of stripping a lot of gameplay to tell a story like many other narrative focused games, Brothers manages to offer well-designed challenges that synchronise very well with the narrative itself. At no point does one feel like there is a divide between the narrative and what you do in the gameplay, like in many, many other games.
I could go on for hours, as there is no game that got me thinking as much about gaming as a whole as Brothers. The ending is by miles the most memorable event any game has offered me, and it still lingers to me to this day.

I figured it was about time I rewrote this review now that I've gave this another chance after around 1 year since my last attempt at the game.
A year has passed since this game's release date it has since exited early access and has become a full fledged game, hence why I don't think I can reccomend it even now. RWBY: GE is set in a interlude period after team RWBY's first mission. It is a hack and slash game. The game consists of about 10 chapters with around 9 different enemies (Not types just enemies). This game had great potential but now that it has left early access allow me to go into detail as to why I can not reccomend this game in it's "finished" state.
When you think of a hack and slash game you think of combos, button mashing, waves of enemies, and while you do get this, you can see that it is incredibly barebones for it's price of 19.99. You have 1 set of combos for each character, light attacks, heavy attacks, and ranged attacks. The amount of different combos in the game is incredibly limited, and you are stuck with that set of combos for the entirity of the game. This can make combat feel dull at many points after the first few levels.
The upgrade tree is nearly worthless except for one or two upgrades. They offer a few bonuses, but quite a few of them are only useful/unlockable in multiplayer which considering the game's playerbase has been rapidly declining makes them useless in general. You only get a total of 10 skill points for their incredibly small tree. The tree fits the size of the game, but that points to an issue with the game as a whole with it being so short.
The combat on higher difficulties can be completely random thanks to wonky hitboxes at certain times. I've had my heavy attacks miss altogether or have had an enemy a huge distance away from me still manage to hit me. It appears randomly but frequently unfortunately making higher difficulty solo runs frusturating.
Now this is where I have my biggest gripes about the game. I know that Rooster Teeth can make a great story capable of grabbing my attention for 4 seasons of their show, but somehow they manage to make a complete miss of a story that fails in several aspects. When I think RWBY I think a good story, and I could've forgiven the unintresting combat if it managed this.
Note: This next section of my review will contain spoilers (Not that there is much to spoil, but still)
This is a summary of the story
You enter in the emerald forest finding a hint of some type of shadow organization, and find even further hints of them in the next chapter and something indicating that they may be trying to trap grimm. You see a mutated grimm which perplexes Dr. Oobleck. You find a ship which appears to belong to the shadow organization, and "Accidently" enter a crate which goes to an undisclosed island. The bad guy reveals himself and a breif past with Dr. Ospin. Bad guy then summons you into his lair, and acts nonchalant about you destroying his hardware for a good two minutes, and then a minute later freaks out for nearly the exact same reasons. After freaking out after you defeat the same enemies (Actually same waves even) that you've seen 10 times before he unveils the big ol boss of the game. 10 minutes of cheese later you beat the boss, and he self destructs his base.
Now what are the problems I have with this story?
The pacing is really terrible, there are only 10 chapters and each level is obscenely small. There is no room for anything at all to develop. The bad guy is also the worst shallow cliche villan I think I have seen in most of my time gaming, and I've been gaming since the pre PS1 era. He pretty much has no backstory except being a villan who likes to take science too far. He acts nonchalant at your first attempts and quickly breaks down into panic at the first sign of actual danger. His backstory is all but non existant except for what you can infer, and that would only be speculation. This was the most dissapointing and attrocious bad guy I could've ever expected rooster teeth to make. He can't even begin to compare to Cinder, Roman Torchwick, or Salem. Rooster teeth has shown they can make a good villan and that is what makes this game's antagonist all the more dissapointing.
I could've backed off from this a little IF they decided to change the artifacts in the game. When the game first released I thought the "Artifacts" were simply placeholders for actual world building/lore, but nope they function as nothing more than easy to obtain EXP bonuses. When they could've been actual artifacts, reports, collectables, how cool would it have been to see research documents from the antagonist? They would've given insight and much needed back story to an empty game. Instead they are Dr. Ospin's "Artifacts" that he used to define the teams at the beggining of the show.
There are a few DLC items for this game, but none of them add anything except for costumes or fanservice. They added team JNPR, costumes, and dances. This is a really crappy buisness practice only beneffiting from the RWBY IP, it's dissapointing that instead of writing a better story or making more enemies they go for the cash grab strategy. I don't think I will ever purchase another game from the affiliated companies again after this.
RWBY as a show will always be cherished by me, but as a game it was unbelievably dissapointing, don't buy this game and have Rooster Teeth stick to what they know.

All I can really say is that I can't wait to get into this game, since at the moment I want to play the tables and buy them all, but all I can see is a black screen with loud music. I will edit when I get into the game.

Hats off to Farsight. They managed to take their excellent pinball simulation and wrap it up in an interface that is somehow even worse than the abysmal front end they have for The Pinball Arcade. It's also more unstable and the lighting on the tables defaults to a horribly over exposed look.
Still, once you manage to navigate your way through a menu created by some alien life form not used to the expectations of the average human and get the lighting setup to your liking, you will be able to play some excellent reproductions of real life Stern pinball tables. Like Pinball Arcade once you get to actually playing the tables, everything is great. You'll just have to wade through what may just be the most un-intuitive menu conceived in the modern era and maybe a few crashes to desktop a long the way.
I'm not a big fan of Stern tables, though people seem to really like the AC/DC table. You aren't able to try out tables you haven't bought as you can in Pinball Arcade. The free table, Frankenstein is quite good though and this game is worth downloading to play it.
If only Farsight could sort out their QA I could happily recommend this. Hopefully they get that sorted at some point.

I am a great pinball fan, so to be able to play modern tables is just a great fun and I could easily forget about the bugs, that are still in the client (I must press Alt+Enter twice to play fullscreen in full resolution). AC/DC and StarTrek are great fun. I can only recommend this game to every pinball fan who already played every table from the PinballArcade. This is the new stuff and I will enjoy to learn all modes of the new tables and play the game. Great fun. I've been a pinball fan for a long time, TPA was a fantastic product and I was happy when Farsight announced the Stern PA, at the beginning it was a bit confusing to have two separated products, but I guess it has to do with licences and Mr Stern betting strongly for the future of pinball in all areas, real tables, VR and emulation on the maxium platforms, PC, tables, mobile etc.
The good news is, that now we are going to have newer pinball tables to play, and Stern wants its name its promo, and get some profit of it, so it is normal.
Yes, I was eager to see the realsease of SPA before xmas, I have a virtual Pinball table I build myself, it's where I normally play my fabourite tables, the surprise was to see at first, no portrait mode support, buggy resolution and worst, no keyword mapping, luckily 3 days later an upgrade was released, but still the game was playing very slowly.
The slowlyness is mostly because this is DX11 engine game, so if your lcheck the requirements you'll see that it demands a higher specs PC in order to play it propperly, so I decided to upgrade the graphics card in my pin cabinet, I got a low profile nvidia 750ti, it is actually a lowend card but it does the job, now I can play in portrait mode in pin cab with all the glorious graphics, lighting, 7 ball multiballs with lo lags! the graphics are now similar to the highend consoles and the game is fully playable.
After playing a little with Mustang which honestly I find it a bit simple and boring I decided to go ahead and spend 20 bucks for the pack which contains STAR TREK, and OMG what a wonderful table, it is worh all the wait and money, it is probably the best table I've ever played, it has such an intense gameplay, sounds music, effects, very easy to understand, easy to start the missions, and the missions dont' end when I miss a ball, it reminds a little bit Attack from Mars, and it has lots of features, actually it has 800 pages of instructions. Yes, Steve Richie is behind this fantastic table. I haven't got the luck of playing the real table, in my country, Catalonia, pinball tables are hard to see nowadays, so virtuall pinball and the work of Farsight is great so fans can enjoy these great modern pinball tables.
So, yes as most you guys, I was a bit upset, but now I'm enjoying this game, I hope in the next coming days upgrades will pop and positive reviews will grow, because maybe it has a bad interface, but the emulation is so great it makes you forget it.
I guess the problem was the release date, the programmers had to rush to get it released before xmas, and well,♥♥♥♥♥♥happens when you relaase a game that has not fully tested.
just a couple of things i wanted to mention, I find the price is a bit excessive, 9,99 for a table, I know they are pretty new, but 6 buck would be ok. Last but not least, the second monitor suppord would be much apreciated.
Also as the music in modern tables is so good, it would be nice in future uptades, to have sfx and music controls separated so you can adjust the volumes at your own taste.
with all this being said I just want to thank Farsight for your work, and I hope this release is gonna be good for you after all,  I'm pretty sure they are going to learn from this mistake.

Decent story - relatively satisfying conclusion - and enjoyable gameplay with gorgeous scenery throughout. Immense customization is available and the combat is fast paced, intuitive, and rewarding. It is easy to change your "fate" and try a different play style at any point in the game - I switched back and forth from magic and finesse more times than I can count - and the different unlockable options for combat are really enjoyable. More than just a hack-and-slash, this game encourages you to consider particular approaches for particular enemies based on their weapon type and behavior. At the upper levels you have four or five different moves for any given weapon, all executed through a simple interface - click, pause click, click while dodging, click while blocking, click after parrying. Combined with a wide variety of spells and special abilities, you have numerous options for engaging with a particular enemy, or multiple enemies at once.
It was hard to really get a feel for my character, though, since it is clear that in order to complete quests and gain experience, there is a very particular sort of person your character is supposed to be. More options for how to complete certain quests would have been nice.
Overall though, it was a great experience and my first playthrough lasted 78 hours. And I'm thinking about playing through it again because I know I missed so much and never even gave the "might" skill tree a chance! 8/10 would recommend.

This is a horrible representation of the Japanese logic puzzle "Gokigen Naname".
Unfortunately, "meleng" does not follow the the rule that forbids any loops.
Without this rule, all the puzzles become pointless without any challenge.
Worse yet, after solving many of the levels, your progress keeps disappearing.
So you're forced to replay the same inane levels over and over again.
Instead of wasting your money, I recommend a free version which follows the correct rules of the game and provides a logic puzzle that requires some actual thought.
This one allows you to create any size layout. And since it's randomly generated, you'll have more than the 66 levels offered here.  You'll have an endless supply of new puzzles every day:

32 minutes to completion for me, 1 achievement per level and you get 53 achievements for free at the start. There are 66 levels.

All-in-all I had my share of entertainment for its tiny price. If you are (like me) into graphic puzzle games such as Klocki, Meleng might be easier, but it's as good. Actually I'm looking forward to the next project or updates. Greetings devs! Nice job

Hmm where to start...
Well lets start off with some background info.
This game was created by an indi group called  'Modern Paradise gaming'. This is their first game so don't expect triple A graphics like Battlefield 4. However graphics are only 1 point of a video game. This is also not the 'full game'. Its a mini game for those of you who are waiting on the story driven part. This is more like testing out the water before you jump in.
First thoughts
Well the game can be fun, however it has a long way to go. The textures seem bland'ish, but they work for a sturdy foundation, but will need some improvement. Think of the graphics as a mix between half-life 1 and Unreal tournament. The maps can be pretty fun, from multiple levels (1-5 stories high) to maps with 1-2 stories, however i noticed the game will start to stutter and drop fps if you look towards the middle of the map...or at least on 1 of the maps called 'Devils run".
The physics are quite funny, which i mean most of the time they work well, other times you fly off of an object and die, or by jumping on top of your teammate and some how die from taking damage. Fall damage is kind of borked since you can die from only falling around 2-3 feet.
The guns work well and sound decent, but atm the GL launcher is a bit broken since it only kills by direct damage, not splash. Other then that the guns work normal.
The gamemode is a mixture of capture the flag and control point. Well you capture a flag and you get a set amount of points. Then the flag will spawn at a random location. The team with the most points win. This is really fun to be honest.
The main menu.....hmm.....it needs so...urm a lot of work. You can't change controls atm, but they work well. Options, which are limited can only be changed in-game. You have to type your name in the 'player name' box. The game has no dedicated servers, its more like call of duty, one person hosts, then the rest dog pile in.
When picking teams you press 'tab' not 'esc', this is thrown on the 'menu', a seperate menu would work better imo.
Final verdict for this...
It has bugs and optimization issues, but it feels like all those classic games back in the 90's. At the moment $15 might be too high, but I would pay around $7 easy. I think a better move for the devs would be to make it into early access instead of full release. They have a long way to go for improvement, but hey not too bad for your first attempt at making a game.
I rate this as a mixed. Some parts are bad, others are good. With time, i'm sure it will improve greatly.

You are either the father or mother (you get to choose) of a daughter who has been put into a mental ward for her own safety. The thing is something has happened there, and even though you were told to stay away you have decided to check up on your daughter. That's where things start getting even stranger. You leave the elevator and can't seem to find anyone around. You locate your daughter's room and find a journal with a strange looking face on it. Upon touching it you are transported into the Shadow Ward.
The journal's page scatter in a strange wind that pulls through the mental ward when you touch the journal. You will have to collect the pages if you are ever going to find out what has happened to your daughter, and perhaps find a way out of this situation for yourself. You see once you enter the Shadow Ward you will find that you are no longer alone.
In The Hat Man: Shadow Ward, you will find that there is a shadow being that goes by the name of the Hat Man. The Hat Man seems to be stalking the halls, and if he catches you you will be paralyze, your soul stolen, and if you wish to try your luck again, you will have to start from scratch.
On the outside this looks like a very scary game where there's going to be tons of jump out of your seat scares, and to be honest when the Hat Man catches you, most of the time it will make you jump out of your skin. The only problem is some of the mechanics. When I talk about mechanics I'm talking about several things in the game.
The first mechanic is the randomization of the game layout. I'm all for changing things up through each playthrough, but that being the case I feel like this game would have GREATLY benefited from a checkpoint system. The way I would have done it is that you have to collect the pages in groups of five. I do understand that this would probably screw up the random locations of the pages, but I think there is a level of frustration that starts to creep in, especially since the Hat Man's location could literally be in the wall in the room you start your adventure into the Shadow Ward.
The second mechanic is the inventory system, maybe it's my computer, but it took an act of God to change items that were currently equipped. Now thankfully you're going to be spending the majority of the time with the flashlight in hand, but it would have been nice if the game would have allowed a smoother transition between items.
The third mechanic surrounds the journal pages. Part of what makes this game creepy is what is written in the journal pages, and currently the only way to actually find out what are in the pages you picked up is to go into the journal. Why not just have the audio start to play upon picking up the page so that the player isn't taken out of the game to find out what is on the pages? Oh and if you have to go into the journal to find out what is written on them, the audio should probably match up to ALL entries. There's at least one case that I can think of off the top of my head where the page had something other than what was being said to me.
The thing is this game has that spookiness to it that will keep people on edge, but with just enough randomness to cause people to get frustrated. I know its a race against time as you try to stay 2 steps in front of the Hat Man as you try to recover all the journal pages, but when his location seems to be randomized, and the first playthrough I met my demise without ever really getting into the game, it kind of kills the want to play again.
I'm going to be totally honest, I have yet to fully complete the game, but it isn't from a lack of trying. The only way that I've been able to get anywhere in this game is from constantly sprinting through the entire game, and listening for the whispers, that's when you know you are close to another journal page. I appreciate that there are items hidden in the game that cause you to have to really search the area, but without a map to refer to and the fact that you have to stay constantly on the run, there's a really good chance that a player could be doing a large loop over and over again not knowing what to do, scared that if they slow down and start to really investigate the Hat Man will appear, and you'll have to start all over again.
So here's the deal, this game has its moments, and I think it is possible, if all the stars align that this could be the experience that I think the developers are hoping the player gets, but with all the random variables, and the fact that the Hat Man can strike right off the bat, this game is too much of a game of chance to really enjoy. This game gets a 6.2 out of 10.

Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is a very moving, powerful game. This is a game that will in a sense, keep you on the edge of your seat, not so much due to QTEs, or huge set pieces ala Tomb Raider, where your adrenaline is pumping, rather more in the vein of the emotional sense. Brothers is a puzzle game at its core, but one that is highly story driven, despite the game only taking three to five hours to complete; it is one of the games that I have played that has left such an impression that I don't think I am like to forget this game anytime soon...or ever.
Set in the Medieval Ages, this game finds two brothers who set out on an adventure (I can't stress this word enough adventure! This is no mere quest as we so often find within RPGs today and of yester-year.) The two brothers embark on an adventure in order to save their father by journeying to the tree of life. Along the way these two brothers will face many obstacles, they'll encounter great beauty and many dangers. The two often go hand in hand, which makes this adventure feel even more like an epic adventure. I think I liken this to the 1984 film “The Neverending Story” in many aspects. The two brothers will come across and meet many people and creatures along the way. Some of these moments are more memorable than others, like passing through a village with a little girl who has a ball. You can take the ball and pass it back and forth or play keep away, you can even drop it down a well if you're feeling mischievous. The human element in this game is one of its greatest strengths, I would say it is its greatest strength. As I have said this game focuses on emotions. You'll feel a wide array of emotions. I personally never really ever felt anger or the need to kill anyone in the game. If such a part came up, I only felt that I had to for self preservation. Starbreeze Studios captured that emotional pull very well, all while managing to never invoke that feeling of vengeance, anger, or hatred. What you will fell is sadness, joy, excitement, compassion, and a slew of other emotions swirling around in a pot. The language is akin to what you would hear in the Sims, so while you aren't able to understand what is being said, the body language and facial expressions more than make up for it. This, I feel adds even more so to that layer of emotion.
Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is a game that everyone should play once at the very least. Mind you this game doesn't really have any replay value, still it should be experienced by everyone. This is a game about humanity and human interactions. The way you interact, the choices you make (which are few) all coalesce into the overall experience of what this game is about rather well. It is a jaw dropping experience!
I'd  would really like to go on and on about the game to tell of my adventure, but this is a special game, and so it is far better for you to experience this adventure for yourself than it would be for me to tell you about it.
Now, the art direction of this game is phenomenal! Your eyes will be treated to some of the most beautiful level designs I have seen in any game. The game is powered by Unreal, so don't expect the graphical fidelity that you would see in Far Cry 4 or Shadow of Mordor. The way the art team handled this game, though makes it absolutely beautiful amidst the backdrop of the story. The striking beauty clashes with the deaths in the game, so much so that many of the deaths you see look peaceful and beautiful, again only invoking sadness and compassion, not anger. The texture quality for the caliber of this game and its particular art direction is more than satisfactory. I had no issues with the textures, I experienced no pop ins or anything of the sort. It should be noted that there is no graphical options other than resolution and gamma, but honestly that is all you need in this game anyway.
The other very noteworthy factor of Brothers is the the sound design. It complements the art direction. The audio is quite rich and flavorful. The ambient sounds can be heard clearly and I did not experience any muddled audio. The score is also very well done. The developers and the composer implemented each score at just the right time to maximize whatever emotion they wanted the player to feel at that ime. Damn good job on their end.
As for the gameplay. It is fun and exciting, it never grows dull as this adventure really does take you to unexpected places. The developers added the right amount of freshness to prevent a dull experience, however, the gameplay is not flawless. I had some issues with the controls, with getting one or both of the brothers to do what I needed them to do. I felt that the controls could have used some more work. This is the only gripe that I have with this outstanding title and it is a minor one, as the gameplay is pretty solid, just not as perfect as the other aspects of Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons. I experienced no bugs or glitches during my playthough, and while the game is quite short by today's standards, I was very pleased and felt the QA team did a good job as did the programmers. I must confess that I look forward to Starbreeze Studios' next IP. They have certainly developed a game that will stay with you.

Spelunky is easily one of the best rogue-likes ever made. It's brutally difficult - the tiniest mistake, or the slightest whim of not progressing carefully, can result in an instant death, or at the least, harsh punishment. I've put about 20 hours in at the time of writing, and I've not gotten even REMOTELY close to winning. Not even halfway.
What makes the game great, beyond it's difficulty? Well, it's fair, almost always. Your deaths are your fault - you didn't look carefully enough, you reacted too slowly to a bad situation, you hurried too much. There is the occasional death from just... the most unfortunate circumstances, such as a glorious moment in which you're knocked around 3 or 4 times in hitstun, straight into some instant kill spikes, but I'd say that's rare.
What makes Spelunky so... replayable, is that it is QUICK. You boot up the game, you can press a button to skip the main menu entirely, straight into the "level select" area, in which you can take shortcuts to areas after you have reached them a couple times and met some prerequisites. However, you can not win the game if you do this - it's impossible. When you die, you can press a button to immediately get back into the action, we're talkin less than 2 seconds. It's... addicting. Just one more run... I'll do better this time. It's a great time-killer, since unless you're pretty good, most runs don't last more than 5-10 minutes. It's an amazing, well built cycle of throwing yourself at the brick wall in the best painful way.
It's just plain fun. Rage inducing? Sometimes. But even with my BIGGEST rage quits, I'm often back within the hour. The gameplay loop is just that satisfying.
Do you want a great rogue-like game with infinite replayability, a satisfying gameplay loop, and kills a lot of time, without much actual time commitment? Buy this game. It's easily worth full asking price. Just get it.

For people out there asking 'Is this better than its prequel?' my answer is yes, but still not worth your god damned time. Maybe if it allowed for custom games or maybe if it had dedicated servers instead of letting some random guy host then maybe it would be worth it. But my experience so far after reaching level 8 is a mix of unsatisfaction and irritation. The game is decided almost immediately after it starts just by looking at who's the host and my corresponding ping to the said host and it's frustrating.
But I will not dwell more on that because thankfully the game gives me more to harp about.
Graphics:
Yes, the game indeed surpasses its original but you've seen this kind of detail before and even better. In fact, I can even dare say that this falls off compared to some games because there are some actions that are not rendered too well. The characters you can choose from are lack-lustered and it wouldn't be too annoying if you had morethan four to choose from, i am not too sure if you can change hairstyles later on cause as I said I am only level 8 but the inability to do so even at my level makes looking at my character a chore.
Plot:
The previous gunz didn't have this but now we have a campaign mode. It's always a good thing for me if a game has a single player mode that can help him burn his time while waiting for his friends but this campaign mode doesn't really hit that spot. The game just basically keeps spawning mobs and mobs of 'Adam Soldiers' at you until you die. Are there respawns? There are but you have to buy them with steam money.... Yeah, ♥♥♥♥ that. As I said this mode is repetitive and gets really boring really fast so I didn't even bother to finish up to the second chapter. Maybe I will when I get some of my friends to play with me. Hopefully they don't get bored and last at least two chapters.
Gameplay:
If Gunz 2 does something right it's this. Fighting with another player is intense and exciting. The different classes add variety and forces players to incorporate strategy into their game which the old GunZ didn't have. The class specific specials look amazing and feels amazing to use! One can feel like a total badass after slicing an opponent into half with a katana as the poor victim slowly kneels on the floor electrified before he dies. A successful and cunning illusionary escape with a shadow dancer feels very satisfying after you see your fooled foe die from the explosion your illusion creates! All of these plus the already amazing wall walking mechanics now improved to make continuos wall run possible without being a validictorian at the game. You can run from walls to walls just by properly positioning your mouse and pressing the jump button without having to pause and this makes for very flashy acrobatic kills!
Too bad though that no matter how good its gameplay is the fact remains that it only matters if your enemies don't stand in front of you and take the brunt of all your attacks and yet take no damage because you have too high ping due to the host living in the far side of the planet or because he has a dial up. Over and over you will hear complains in game about changing hosts and even if the host changes it's still not guaranteed that the next host will be more decent! Your only real salvation is if the system chooses you to host the game but even then, your experience will be mediocre as people who lag with you as host will soak up damage like the world's most porous sponge! Having dedicated servers instead of this kind of interface will fix this! There was lag back in the old gunz but not like this! This kind of lag makes the game almost unplayable as the good lag free games are very, very, rare.
Overall gunz is a good game but I cannot recommend this game with all the lag. It's free to play so it's safe to try but I wouldn't recommend buying bundles for it because chances are you will quit this game unless you're a hardcore fan of the prequel. However, I do recommend keeping this game in your memory because if the game fixes its lag problems then it's an experience worth your money.

Straight Up: This has to be one of the best story-driven RPGs I've ever played.
With an award-winning cast of authors on the team, the game's actual storyline elements and plethora of sidequests don't ever fail to disappoint. Combine this with a sort of choose-your-own-adventure approach to your hero's class, and you have a definite thumbs-up.
There is a vast array of both skills (like blacksmithing, artificing, herbology, persuasion, etc) and abilities (magic, swordplay,  backstabbing - fun!) that can be combined in any manner to create your own unque character and stylistic experience. Furthermore, many of the quests have multiple outcomes and allow for some fun variation. (Also, there is a "wanted" system that kicks in if you kill randoms that enables you to bribe or kill guards, go on endless frenzies, and if you so desire, to break out of jail).
The best part about the game for me was definitely the voice acting and the music. It seemed as if every character with whom you could speak actually had a different voice actor, creating a much more realistic world and a much more immersive storyline. Also, there are characters who you'll actually grow to love dialogues with because they're just SO FUNNY. Which is great.
Lastly, if you think that DLCs are all a waste of money, this game has two story-driven DLCs that add achievements, weapons, story, characters, a higher level cap, and many side quests. Oh, and in one there's a debating club with Half-Giants in which you argue by beating each other to a pulp. Which is also great.
PROS:
Immersive storyline.
The game has LOADS of side quests for many extended hours of play.
Enjoyable factions to join.
Many different voice actors.
Great soundtrack.
No pre-set class system. Any ability can work with any weapon and any race is you allocate your skill ponts correctly.
Arguably the most worthwhile DLCs I've seen since the expansions for Age of Empires back in the day.
The game is ultimately like Skyrim with a proper combat system.
